talivaṉ uṟiyum aṟiyil pañcu mettikaḷ iṭappaṭṭa iraṇṭu kaṭṭilkaḷ iruntaṉa. mettiyiṉ nāṟpakkaṅkaḷilum aṇikaḷ iṭappaṭṭiruntaṉa. talip pakkattukku aṇmiyil ularnta marattaṭṭu iruntatu. kāliyil alaṅkarittuk koḷvataṟku vēṇṭiya cantaṉam, vācaṉit tilam, pūmāli mutaliyaṉa ataṉmītu vikkappaṭṭiruntaṉa. tariyil eccil umiḻum kāḷāñci iruntatu. aṟikku veḷiyē vaḷarkkum kiḷikaḷ kūṭukaḷil iruntaṉa.
talivaṉ kāliyil eḻuntu kālik kaṭaṉkaḷi muṭittapiṉ taṉṉi alaṅkarittāṉ. alaṅkārap poruḷkaḷil ciṟantavi cantaṉam, vācaṉit tiraviyaṅkaḷ eṉpaṉa. avaṉ vācaṉip puki ūṭṭappaṭṭa āṭiyi uṭuttup pūmāliyi aṇintāṉ. kaṇṇukku mi tīṭṭiṉāṉ; tāmpūlamiṭṭuc civanta itaḻkaḷukku arakkuk kūṭṭic ceyta cāyam pūciṉāṉ. taliyi vāriṉāṉ. viralkaḷukku mōtiraṅ kaḷi aṇintāṉ. mēlē uttarikam tarittāṉ.
kāliyil pārkkum kaṭamikaḷ muṭintatum avaṉ tiṉamum nīrāṭiṉāṉ. ovvoru iraṇṭāvatu nāḷum avaṉ uṭampu piṭittuk koṇṭāṉ. ovvoru mūṉṟāvatu nāḷum oruvakip poruḷip pūci nīrāṭiṉāṉ. nakaṅkaḷ miṉukkamāka irukkumpaṭi avaṉ avaṟṟi aḻaku ceytu koṇṭāṉ. viyarviyit tuṭippataṟku avaṉ eppoḻutum oru ciṟiya tuṇiyi vittiruntāṉ. muṉ poḻutil oṉṟum piṉpoḻutil oṉṟumāka nāḷirumuṟi uṇavu koṇṭāṉ. iṟicci porittum, camittum, avitta nīrākavum koḷḷappaṭṭatu. naṇpakal uṇavukkup piṉ avaṉ naṇparkaḷōṭu aḷavaḷāviṉāṉ. māli nērattil kōḻip pōr, kutārip pōr, āṭṭup pōr kaḷik kaṇṭu poḻutu pōkkiṉāṉ. kūṭukaḷil vaḷarkkum ciṅkaṅ kaḷum pulikaḷum niṉṟaṉa. iraviṉ muṟpakutiyil avaṉ iciyik kēṭṭum naṭaṉaṅkaḷip pārttum makiḻntāṉ. aṟikaḷil naṟumaṇam kamaḻntatu.
celvaṉiṉ maṉivi urattuc cirikkavum urattup pēcavum māṭṭāḷ. kaṇavaṉiṉ peṟṟōr kuṟi kūṟiṉāl avaḷ etirttup pēca māṭṭāḷ; periya celvattilum ullāca vāḻkkiyilum tiḷittapōtum akanti koḷḷamāṭṭāḷ; viḻākkaḷukkuc cellumpōtu āṭamparamākac celvāḷ. cila aṇikalaṉkaḷi aṇintu koḷvāḷ. kaṇavaṉ tūratēcam ceṉṟiruntāl avaḷ caṅku vaḷikaḷiyum tāliyiyumtavirap piṟa aṇikalaṉkaḷi aṇiyamāṭ ṭāḷ. avaḷ kāli, naṇpakal, māli eṉṉum mūṉṟu nēraṅkaḷilum illuṟi teyvaṅkaḷukkup pali tūvuvāḷ.
75. kūttu
ātikāla makkaḷ tammiṭam tōṉṟum uṇarccikaḷi āṭik kāṭṭiṉārkaḷ. piṟpōkkiluḷḷa makkaḷiṭiyē iṉṟum ivvāṭ ṭaṅkaḷ kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. ivvaki āṭṭaṅkaḷiliruntu kūttuk kali vaḷarcciyaṭintatu. atu iṉṟu naṭipeṟum nāṭakam pōlal lātu, oru karuttiṉi, uṭalnili, pārvi, apinayaṅkaḷāl naṭittuk kāṭṭum kaliyāka iruntatu. atu piṟkālattil parata nāṭṭiyam eṉavum catirāṭṭam eṉavum peyar peṟṟatu. cintuveḷi nākarika kālattil itu naṉku vaḷarcciyaṭintiruntatu. cintuveḷiyil kiṭitta tolporuḷkaḷil naṭarācarip pōṉṟu naṭaṉamāṭum mūṉṟu kompukaḷuṭiya oru kaṭavuḷ uruvamum, naṭṭamāṭum niliyil niṟkum peṇ teyvattiṉ uruvamum, nāṭṭiyamāṭum niliyil niṟkum oru nāṭṭiyap peṇṇiṉ uruvamum kāṇappaṭṭaṉa1. nāṭṭiyak kaliyi puttarum, camaṇarum, pirāmaṇarum veṟuttārkaḷ. ikkali teṉṉintiyāvilēyē vaḷarcciyaṭintatu. paratanāṭṭiya nūlic ceyta paratar tirāviṭa vakuppiṉarāvar2. paratar ceyta nūl vaṭamoḻiyiliruppatāl kūttukkali āriyanāṭṭiṉiṉṟu teṟkē vantateṉap palar tavaṟākak karutuvar.

1. Vishnu, Shiva and Kali, the great gods of Hinduism, are not Rigvedic deities at all. It is probably significant that the word Lingam is definitely of non-Aryan origin, as Przyluski has demonstrated. while the word puja is also believed to be a non-Samskritic loan word. 1. The progress of research into various phases of Indian antiquities is helping to pile up evidences to demonstrate the fact that the texure of Indian culture is
made of the work of non-Aryan and pre-Aryan threads crossed with the woof of Aryan Hinduistic character. In the light of these evidences the conviction has been gining ground that the great process popularly known as Hinduism is nothing but a synthesis and harmonization of complex elements of Aryan, pre-Aryan, non-Aryan and aboriginal culture, a good deal of which must have been autocthonus and indigenous, that is to say, was born on, or sprung from the soil of Indian continent. It has become impossible to contradict the fact that aboriginal and Indian Aryan cultures have greatly contributed to the development of what has become to be known during historical times as characteristically Indian civilization. Sometimes the elements and types of aboriginal culture has been transformed and modified so as to fit into the ideals and systems of Aryan thought and culture. Sometimes the aboriginal elements have been bodily annexed and appropriated into Indian system by removing the property mark of earlier aboriginal ownership and origins - Non.Aryan contribution to Indian Music - O.C.Ganguly - Annals of Bhandarkar - Oriental Research Institute - Vol. XIX (1938-1939).

On the grounds indicated above, we may infer the, Upanishadic speculations originated wholly outside the pale of Vedic Brahmanism and had their source in the religio-philosophical thought currents already prevalent in India since pre-Aryan days. That a rich culture which had been flourishing in India for at least two millena before the advent of the Vedic Aryans, should produce philosophical thinking and religious ideas of refined types is no difficult to make, for, it is but normal to expect this evolution ... the pre-Vedic elements constituted the texure while the Vedic did probably no more than imprint the stamp. It would be historically more correct, therefore, to regard Upanishadic as much as Jaina and Buddhist thoughts as having their roots more in non-Vedic than in Vedic ideas. We also find the basic ideas of the Samkhya and Yoga permeate Jaina, Buddhist as well as the Upanishadic outlook and it is probable that the primitive Samkhya consisted the philosophical background par excellence of pre-Vedic Indian thought and Yoga consisted an essential element in the cultivation of matters concerning the spirit. Both Samkhya and Yoga had developed probably already in pre-Aryan India ... the origin of Upanishads was not at all Vedic. We must not forget the priestly classes and philosophical thinkers with their religious practices and ideas who existed in India from before the coming of the Indian Aryans. By Buddhas time they have probably been absorbed in the part of the Vedic society and came to called Brahmans - Back ground of Buddhist philosophy - Prof. Dr.B.B.Bhattacharia, M.A.D., Ph.D. Indo Asian Culture, No.1.

It is an established fact that the god Siva was the form which the Vedic god Rudra later assumed. In other words the god Siva, at least as he has been described in classical times, was unknown to the Vedas, and Rudra the Tempest God of the Vedas is not given any of the distinctive epithets which later came to be associated with the god Siva. If we accept the alleged identification we have to date the god Siva or his proto type in the middle of the third millenium B.C. For, that is the date of the Mohenjo-Daro finds, as has been proved by Professor Selon Lloyd on the strength of the happy discovery of the cylindrical seal at Tel-as-mar which contins a representation of a typically mohenjo-Daro scene-an Indian elephant, rhinoceros and a crocodile. Identification of Mohenjo-Daro figure-B.A. Saletore-New review X, July - Dec. 1939.
Now it seems possible that Rudra in the Rig-Veda was an Aryanised form from the pre-Aryan proto-Siva. Only three hymns have been given to him, and he is identified with Agni. The cult of linga in three faced Siva is common among represen-
tations of Siva. It is ordinarily Agamic principle that Siva in his aspect of Maheswara or Sadasiva can be represented with one, three, four or five faces but not with two. But the fact is there, the image represented with three faces and other associations are clearly Saivic in character. The conclusion there fore seems to be thoroughly justified that it is the figure of Siva that is represented on this. This would only be confirmed by the yogic posture of Siva in one aspect is represented as Mahayoge and sometimes called Yoge - Daks hanamurthi. 1. From the identification of Chandragupta Maurya to the excavations of Mohenjo Daro and Harappa, from the deciphering of the inscriptions of Asoka to the comparative survey of epigraphic records over India, the material for the writing of Indian history was provided by the work of European scholars. Even more striking is the case of Indonesia, where few European scholars, mostly Dutch reconstructed from inscriptions the history of the great empires of Java and Sumatra which provided Indonesian nationalism with a solid historical basis. In this sense it cannot be denied that European scholars and thinkers, by their labour in the interest of knowlge, enabled India, Ceylon and Indonesia to think on terms of historical continuity.
- Asia and Western Dominance
K.M. Panikkar (London - 1954)
* Of European tongues, the nearest congeners to Sanskrit are the Samaritin languages of the Russian Empire, then the classical tongues of Rome and Greece, then those of Germany and the Keltic, this class of languages being called Indo-Germanic, of the sclavonic and Lithuanian, the two branches of samaritin, the affinities of the sanskrit are closer in the Lithuanian than with any other known tongue. Sanskrit next to Lithuanian is most like Sclavonic. It will thus
be observed that the Aryan or Sanskrit speakig races of India seem to have been closely connected with the Zend speaking, Greek speaking, Latin speaking races and not at all with Arabic, Phoenician and Hebrew families.

* Rudra has a very subordinate position in Rig-Veda being celebrated only in three entire hymns. He holds a thunderbolt in his arms and discharges lightning shafts from the skys. Siva the benignant with a whole tradition developed round him. - Indian Philosophy Vol. I. p.81 Dr.S.Radhakrishnan.
Rudra is the lord of animals, and forms the point of linkage between the Vedic religion and the later Siva worship. Siva in the Rig-veda means auspicious , but is not the name of a God; the Rudra in Rig-veda is a malignant cattle destroying deity. * The early Vedic religion was a cult of magic, a system of propitation or constrint of Nature-powers (Devas) by means of sacrifices (Yajnas), offerings of animal fat, (ghee vapa, etc) and fermented liquor (Soma) poured into fire regarded as the mouth of the Gods, and accompanied with the chanting of mantras. Some of these mantras were incantations of prise, and others combinations of sounds having no meaning, being sometimes inarticulate cries (“like the bellowing of a bull etc.”) They were believed to please or constrin the Devas and thus to secure the fulfilment of the sacrificers desires, whether these were the acquisition of material objects in this life or the enjoyment of pleasures in post-mortem states. - Outlines of Indian Philosophy p.118.

* They were translated from Sanskrit into Persian by or for Dara Shukoh, the eldest son of the Mugal emperor Shah Jehan who held the liberal religious views of Akbar. He had heard of the Upanishads in Kashmir in 1640 invited several Pandits to Delhi to assist in their translation and finished the work in 1657. Translated into Persian then the most widely read language of the East, they became generally accessible. In 1775 a manuscript of this Persian translation was sent by the French resident at the court of Shujud Daula to Anquetil Duperron the discoverer of the Avesta; and later another manuscript. Anquetil Duperron collected the two and translated the work into French and into Latin publishing the latter version in 1801 and 1802 under the title of Oupnekhat a corruption of upanishad. This Latin translation was studied by Schopenhaner. Twelve of them are translated by Maxmuller with introduction and notes in the “Sacred books of the East”. - The century cyclopedia of names.

* Vedanta - The most Common designation of the Uttaramimamsa school of Hindu philosophy given to it either as teaching the ultimate aim of Veda or as founded on the Upanishads, came at the end of the Veda as the last stage in its historic evolution. It is ascribed to Vyasa or Badarayana. The first of the names (‘arranger’) is also given to the legendary person who is supposed to have arranged the Vedas and written the Mahabharata, Puranas and Dharmasastra and was doubtless applied to various great writers or compliers as a kind of title. In this sense it seems to have been given to the founder of the Vedanta. Its principles are propounded in Sutras, but Badarayana’s Sutras are generally called Brahmasutras or sometimes Sharirakasutra. The text of the celebrated commentary of Sankaracharya have been edited in the “Bibliotheca Indica” and a portion translated, and also the commentary known as Vedanta Sara. The most authoritative recent works on the Vedanta are however pul Deussen’s “Die Sutras des Vedanta” - The Century Cyclopedia of Names.

# Smartas: Smarta Brahmins - one of the three principal classes into which the Hindus proper of the present day may be divided as to religion, the other two being the Saivas and the Vaisnavas. The Smarta believe that the man’s spirit is identical with the one spirit which is the essence of the universe and only cognizable through the three personal gods Brahma, Shiva and Vishnu with their subordinate dieties but only as co-equal manifestations of one impersonal spirit and as destined to be reabsorbed into the spirit. They are followers of Sankara - The Century Cyclopedia of Names.

* Puranas - The name of each of a class of Sanskrit works important in their connection with the later phases of Brahmanism, as exhibited in the doctrines of emanation, incarnation and triple manifestation. They are the Vedas of popular Hinduism and contin the history of the Gods, interwoven with every variety of legendary tradition on other subjects. Though nominally tritheistic, they are practically polytheistic and essentially pantheistic. Their form is in general that of dialogues in which a well known sage answers the questions of his disciples, while others are monologues. They are written in sloka matter of the Mahabharata, with occassional passages in prose. They are 18 in number. There are also 18 Upapuranas or Subordinate Puranas
- The Century Cyclopedia of Names.

* The Dharma Sutras were manuals written by the teachers of the Vedic Schools for the guidance of their pupils. Their use was therefore, at first restricted to these schools alone and it was not till a later period that they were acknowledged as authority all over India. The Smirthis on the other hand were declared to be of divine origin and hence climed from the very beginning to be authentic sources of law for all Aryans - “The History and Culture of the Indian People - Vol.II p.225.”

* No.99 in vol.ii. part V. of South Indian inscriptions gives an interesting account of a gift of a village for the purpose of supporting 308 learned Brahmans in persuit of their sacred vocations of studying and teaching as prescribed in the Sastras. Regarding the qualifications of the select body of Brahman scholars it is stated in the inscription that they had all studied the three Vedas and Smiritis. The inscription applies to them various learned designations such as Cathurvedin, Triveden, Somajajin, Sadangavid, Bhatta, Kramavid (proficient in the Krama - patha of the Rig Veda & C.)
A similar gift for establishing a similar colony of 308 Brahmans is also Registered in No.7 of 1912 No.277 of 1913 refers to the establishment of another cultured colony of 108 Brahman families equipped with all necessaries of life and even with library called Saraswathi Bhandara. No.278 of 1913 registers a similar grant for the same number of Brahman colonists. No.198 of 1919 records the interesting case of an assembly holding a special meeting in response to a royal order which requested them to adjudge the merits of a literary work composed by a poet. The work was recited before the assembly and the author obtined as a reward for his labours a grant of land to be held in perpetual ownership. Students of Tamil literature may find here a lingering literary tradition of the more ancient Dravidian Sangam established in Madura to scrutinze
the works of Tamil poets and advance the cuse of Tamil literature (mid. Ep. Rep. for 1919. p.98) - Local Government in Ancient India p.283. Radhakumud Mookerji M.A. Ph.D.

* The Agamas represent the oldest products of Dravidian literature, that in prehistoric times they were written in the Dravidian (Tamil) language, and a great part of them was lost in a flood which swept over the land south of the present Cape Comorin, the chief dwelling place of the old Dravidians. Only remnants of the older Agamas were translated into Sanskrit and preserved in this form. But as has been urged, all that one can say is that the home of the Agamas was in the land of the Dravidians i.e. the south of India. From the south they seem to have pushed up north, and later to have turned back to the south where they helped to drive out Jainsm and Buddhism. It has been further sid that should one incline towards the theory that Agama literature was of Dravidian origin, one must at the same time admit that it came under the influence of Sanskrit literature very early. What is preserved to us of the Agamas bears unmistakably the stamp of Sanskrit literature, for the Agamas that are preserved are in the Sanskrit language, and the systems based in the Agama and written in the non-Sanskrit language employ Sanskrit terms so that as matters now stand, we have to consider the Agama literature as a part of the Sanskrit literature - The Saiva Siddhanta in the Meykanda Sastra - Violet Paranjothi M.A.L.T.Ph.D. (Isabella Thouburn College, Lucknow - 1938) quoted as an English translation from Der Saiva Siddhanta, a German book by H.W. * The Vedic culture which resembles that of the Homeric Greeks or the Celtic Irish at the beginning of the Christian era, or that of the pre-Christian Teutans and Slaves becomes transformed in the epics into the Hindu culture through the influence of Dravidians. The Aryan idea of worship during the earliest period was to call on the Father sky or some other shining one to look from on high on the sacrificer and receive from him the offerings of fat or flesh, cakes and drink. But soon puja or worship takes the place of Homa or sacrifice. Image worship which was a striking feature of the Dravidian faith was accepted by the Aryans. The ideals of vegetarianism and non-violence (ahimsa) also developed. The Vedic tradition has dominated by the Agamic and today Hindu culture shows the influences of the Agama as much as that of the Vedas. The Aryan and the Dravidian do not exist side by side in Hinduism. “contact with the highly civilized Dravidians led to the transformation of Vedism into theistic religion.” - Hindu view in life - Dr.S.Radhakrishnan.

1. Many other nations mention, in the mythological part of their history, in undations which in their essential particulars, agree with the scriptural account of Noah’s preservation. Hence many persons have inferred the universality of this inundation. To this it has been replied that each nation localizes the chief events and actors as connected with itself, necessitating an Ararat, an ark and a Noah in each instance. Fohi in the Chinese mythology, Satyavrata in the Indian, Xisuthrus in the Chaldean, Ogyges and Deucation in t he Greek, have each been recognised by many as the Noah of the sacred scripture under different names. Even the American Indians have a tradition of a similar deluge, and a renewal of the race from the family of one individual. All these individuals are sid be their respective nation to have been saved , and to have become the father of mankind.’ - A New Popular Encyclopedia Vol.IV p.325.

1. Ann (āṇ) is supposed to be the highest God, the God of Heaven. In fact he is, as we shall see later on, identified with the sun. Now the sun in the course of the year travels through the constellations of the Zodiac, which were called houses. Accordingly each month of the sun being in a different house was supposed to take a different form and since the constellations of the Poto - Indians as sid above were only eight, the forms of the sun i.e., the Supreme Being were eight. The eight forms of the Supreme Being were the eight constellations which were the following: The Ram, the Harp, the Crab, the Mother, the Scale, the Arrow, the Jar and the Fish or the two Fishes. Images of the supreme being under these forms were worshipped in different parts of the country. The most popular of these forms of God, seem to have been the Fish. Several inscriptions refer to this - Father Heras.

Ophiolatria, the worship of the serpent next to the adoration of the Phallus , is one of the most remarkable and at first sight unaccountable forms of religions the world has ever known. Until the true source from whence it sprung can be reached and understood, its nature will remin at mysterious as its universality, for what man could see in an object so repulsive and forbidding in its habits, as this reptile, to render worship to its one of the most difficult of problems to find a solution to. There is hardly a country of the ancient world, however where it cannot be traced pervading every known system of mythology, and having proofs of its existence and extant in the shape of monuments, temples and earthworks of the most elaborate and curious character. Babylon, Persia, Hindustan, Ceylon, China, Japan, Burmah, Java, Arabia, Syria, Asiya minor, Egypt, Ethiopia, Greece, Italy, North and Western Europe, Mexico,
Peru, America all yeild abundant testimony to the same effect and point to the common origin of Pagan system wherever found Ophiolatria - p.1.

1. Horned Gods were common in Mesopotamia, both in Babylon and Assyria. The great Gods and Goddesses had seven horns, which is the reason that the divine lamb in the book of revelation was sid to have seven horns ... The horns were a sign of divinity. When king or high priest appeared as the God Asshur with the queen or high priestess as his consort Ishtar, the appropriate number of horns was worn on the royal pir being then regarded as the incarnat e deities. When Alexander the Great rised himself above the king of the earth and made himself a God, he wore horns in sign of his divinity hence his name in the Koran Dhu’l Karnan, the two horned ... The Indian figures of the horned Gods found at Mohenjo - Daro, are of the earliest bronze - age. The most remarkable is that of a man with bull’s horns on his head sitting crosslegged, surrounded with animals the representative was regarded in historic times as a form of Siva and is called Pasupathi ... When in relief sculpture Pasupathi is three faced, as here; but in figures in the round he has four faces. Such a representation in a native attempt to show the all seeing God, as is found in Europe in the four faced of Janus. It is still uncertin whether the four faced form arose independently in India and Europe, or whether one is the prototype of the other if the later, the India appears to be the earlier - The God of the witches p. 15 - Margret Allice Murray.

“The beared God who grasping a trident in his extended left hands heads, the procession of male figures is probably the father deity. The great Hittite God
of thundering sky, whose emblems were the thunderbolt and the bull; for the trident which he carries may resonably be interpreted as thunderbolt. The deity is represented in two stone monuments of Hittite art which were found at Zenjirli in Northern Syria and Bobylonia repectively. On both we see a male God wearing the usual Hittite costume of tall cap, short tunic, and shoes turned up to the toes, a crescent hilted sword in girt at his side; his hands are rised in the right, he holds a single headed axe or hammar, in his left a trident of wavy lines, which is thought to stand for forked lightning or a bundle of thunderbolts. On the Babylonian slab which bears a long Hittite inscription the God’s cap is ornamented with a pir of horns. The horns on the cap are probably those of a bull; for in another Hittite monument found at Malatia on the Euphrates there is carried a deity on the usual Hittite costume standing on a bull grasping a trident or thunderbolt in his left hand, while facing him stands a priest clothed in long robe holding a crook or curved staff in one hand and pouring a libation with the other.” 
In the sculpture the God on the bull holds in his right hand what is discribed as a triangular bow instead of a mace or an axe or a hammer. The Hittite Thunder God also is known to us from a treaty of alliance which about the year 1290 B.C. was contracted between Huttusil, King of Hittites and Remeses II, King of Egypt. By a singular piece of good fortune we possess copies of this treaty both in Hittite and in Egyptian languages. The Hittite copy was found some years ago inscribed in cuniform characters in a clay tablet at Borgazkeni; the copies of the treaty of Egyptian language are engraved on the walls of the temples of Thebes. From the Egyptian copies which have been read and translated, we gather that the sun God was principal deity, of the Hittites and the Hittite scales which appended to the treaty exhibited the king embraced by the Thunder - God and the queen embraced the sun goddess Arenna. The Hittite divinity of thundering sky appears to have long survived at Doliche in Commagene, forin late Roman art he reappears under the title of Jupiter. Dolichenus wearing a phrygian cap, standing on a bull and weilding double axe in one hand and a thunder bolt in the other. In this form his worship was transported from the native Syrian home by soldiers and slaves, till it had
spread over a large part of the Roman Empire especially in the frontiers, while it flourished in the camps of the legions. The combination of the bull with the thunderbolt as emblems of the deity suggests that the animal may have been chosen to represent the sky God not merely of its virility but of its voice; for in the peal of thunder primitive man may well have heard the bellowing of a celestial bull.

The tall flat totted hat with perpendicular grooves which she wears, and lioness or panther in which
she stands, remind as the turetted crown and lion drawn car of Cybele, who was worshipped in the neighbouring land of Phrygia across the Halys so stagnates the great Syrian Goddess Hierapolis Bambyce, was portrayed sitting on lions and wearing a tower on her head. 1. The theory and practice of yoga are entirely foreign to the trend of early and later Vedic religious thoughts and inclinations. It has now been definitely shown by Mr. Chanda with the help of some Mohenjo - Daro sculptures that the idea can be traced to Indus people. It is but natural that the people should have attributed to their God all the characteristics of a yogie including austerities and self - mortification. It is common to believe that the creator himself must perform austerities in order to aualify himself for the capacity of creating manthought Gods, in his own light; process which could bring destruction on man must have been gone thoroughly by Gods to attin their exalted position. It must have been such a belief which led the Indus people to conceive of and depict their God as a meditator.
The intimate connection between Samkhya and yoga are too well known to require repetition. The philosophy of the yoga system may be regarded as practically the same as that of the Samkhya with conception of a personal God super imposed upon it. It therefore appears certin that Samkhya too, which orthodox Hindu opinion has regarded as non-Vedic in character, was, like yoga, a system of thought which had a pre-Vedic origin.
It has been suspected for a long time by scholars that some non-Aryan tracts are contined in the later-day. Siva worship the tract assumption that everything. Aryan must have been nobler than and superior to the non-Aryan led them to think that the uncanny features which the worship involves, could not have come out of the Aryan religion without the impact of some alien ideas.
But so long there was no evidence to lend force to the conjecture or to asce rtin what was the nature of the Aryan influences - Indian Culture - Vol.II - Siva, His Pre-Aryan Origins - Amalananda Ghosh.

The word Sambu - as a Vedic epithet, is well known to be derived from Sam; blessing, welfare, prosperity plus the radical bhu; ‘be, become and to mean’ being a blessing beneficient as a name in later times, of Siva. I feel that it is likely to have been chosen becuse it suggested in the minds of the speakers some Dravidian word akin to the Tamil Cem, ‘redness’ (of Tamil cempoo ‘copper’) the colour red being always associated with this deity. That is to say, the application of the epithet to Siva - seems to me to become more intelligible under the above assumption of the existence in northern India at an early period of a race or races related to the Dravidians of the South, Sambu as a name of Siva becomes in Tamil Campu which, if an early importation, would as I argue, have been originally pronounced with an initial sound like that of the English Church. I venture the suggestion that this word has reverted to Sanskrit from some Dravidic dialect in the form of Jambu, as a name of Siva bearing the connection of ‘reddishness’. Both Jambuka and Siva are used to denote a jackal, possibly becuse of the tawny colour of the animal and when it is considered that the area characterized pre-eminently by the worship of Siva must have been originally south of the zone into which Aryan civilization had advanced, it will not, I think, be felt to be impossible that it was to this unkown region that the expression Jambu-dvipa, ‘the Siva-country first had a reference - Sanskrit Element in the Vocabularies of the Dravidian Languages pp.61,62 - Remarks by M.Collins.

camayat tōṟṟam
ellā uyirkaḷukkum periya accatti viḷivippatu maraṇam. muṟkāla maṉitaṉ taṉṉuṭaṉ vāḻpavarkaḷ iṟantu pōvatip pārt tāṉ. avaṉ avarkaḷiṉ uṭalkaḷit tūrattē koṇṭu ceṉṟu eṟintāṉ. uṭampil irukkum āvi, uṭali viṭṭu nīṅkuvatē maraṇam eṉa avaṉ eṇṇi muṭivu ceytāṉ. avaṉ, āvi allatu uyir aḻiyātu eṉa nampiṉāṉ. uyir uṭaliṉ pakkattē taṅki niṟkum. atu cila camayaṅkaḷil uṭaliṟ pukuntu uyirttu eḻum. atu paḻiyapaṭi tāṉ vāḻnta iṭatti aṭiyum. ataṉāl tīmikaḷ uṇṭākum eṉṉum oru putiya eṇṇam avaṉ maṉatil utittatu. pirētam uyirtteḻum eṉṉum nampikkiyiṉāl maṉitaṉ muṟkālattiṟ kiyāṇṭa vaḻak kaṅkaḷ cila iṉṟum cila makkaḷiṭiyē kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. pirētaṅ kaḷi iṭukāṭṭukku eṭuttuc cellumpōtu vīṭṭiṉ vaḻakkamāṉa vāyilāl eṭuttuc cellātu, piṟitoru vaḻiyāl eṭuttuc cellum vaḻakku makkaḷ palariṭiyē uṇṭu. ivvāṟu ceyvatu pirētam uyirt teḻiṉ vīṭṭukkuc cellum vaḻiyi aṟiyāmal irukkumpaṭiyākum. kāl kikaḷi kaṭṭuvatum, avi eḻuntālum naṭakka muṭiyātirukkum paṭiyē. pirētaṅkaḷukkup piṉṉē neṟpori, tēṅkāyt tuṇṭukaḷi eṟivatu, āvikaḷ vīṭṭukkut tirumpivarātu avikaḷi uṇṭukoṇṭu iṭukāṭṭukkuc cellumpaṭiyēyākum. iṉṉum pirētattip putitta piṉ ampaṭṭaṉāl ceyyappaṭum kiriyikaḷum itu toṭarpāṉavi kaḷē. kiṟittuva matattiṉar iṟantavarkaḷ uyirt teḻuvārkaḷ eṉa iṉṟum nampi varukiṉṟaṉar.
pirētattip putittu ataṉ neñci ūṭuruvumpaṭi kūriya marakkaṭṭiyi aṟivatum muṟkāla vaḻakku. ivvāṟu ceyvatu pirētam eḻumpāmal irukkumpaṭiyēyākum. iṅkilāntiṉ cila iṭaṅkaḷil taṟkoli purintavarkaḷiṉ pirētaṅkaḷukku ivvāṟu ceyyappaṭukiṉṟatu. ataṉāl avaṉ iṟantavarkaḷiṉ uṭalkaḷ uyirtteḻātapaṭi avikaḷip putikkalāṉāṉ. in nampikki valuvaṭintapōtu pirētaṅkaḷ āḻamāṉa kuḻikaḷil putikkap paṭṭaṉa. kuḻikaḷ kaṟpalakikaḷāl mūṭappaṭṭaṉa. kaṟpalakikaḷiṉ mēl uyaramāka maṇ koṭṭi mēṭu ceyyappaṭṭatu. mēṭṭiṉ mītu periya kal vikkappaṭṭatu. ivvāṟu ceytāl putikkappaṭṭa pirētam eḷitil veḷiyē varamāṭṭātu eṉa muṟkāla makkaḷ karutiṉārkaḷ.
iṟantavarkaḷiṉ āvikaḷ uṭal putikkappaṭṭa iṭattil taṅki niṟkiṉṟaṉa. avikaḷukkup paci tākaṅkaḷ uṇṭu. vāḻnāḷil avarkaḷ payaṉpaṭuttiya poruḷkaḷum avarkaḷukkut tēvi uṇṭu eṉavum makkaḷ eṇṇattil paṭṭatu. ākavē avarkaḷ pirētaṅkaḷip putikkum pōtu uṇaviyum nīriyum avarkaḷ payaṉpaṭuttiya poruḷkaḷiyum pakkattē vittārkaḷ; piṉpum avviṭattil uṇaviyum nīriyum vittu varuvārāyiṉar.
iṟantavarkaḷiṉ āvikaḷ makkaḷukku naṉmiyiyō tīmiyi yō ceyya vallaṉa eṉṟum avarkaḷ karutiṉārkaḷ. nāṭṭil nōy, piṇi, pañcam pōṉṟa tuṉpaṅkaḷ nērnta kālattil, avi āvikaḷiṉ kōpattiṉāl uṇṭāyiṉa eṉṟu avarkaḷ nampiṉārkaḷ. ākavē akkālaṅkaḷil āvikaḷukkuc ciṟappāka uṇavum nīrum (pali) vaḻaṅkappaṭṭaṉa. cila talimuṟikaḷ kaḻintaṉa. iṟantavarkaḷip paṟṟiya niṉivukaḷ maṟakkappaṭṭaṉa. appoḻutu iṟantavarkaḷiṉ camātikaḷ ciṟu teyvaṅkaḷākavum kirāmat teyvaṅkaḷākavum māṟiṉa. kuṭumpatta variṉ āvikaḷ illuṟi teyvaṅkaḷāyiṉa. kuṭumpat talivaṉiṉ āvi (kuṭumpa) teyvamāyiṟṟu. atikāriyiṉ āvi kirāma teyvamāyiṟṟu. aracaṉiṉ āvi nāṭṭu makkaḷiṉ teyvamāyiṟṟu. camātikaḷ vikkap paṭṭa kaṟkaḷē āvi uṟiyum iṭaṅkaḷākak karutappaṭṭaṉa. avikaḷiṉ muṉ palikaḷ iṭappaṭṭaṉa. ivvāṟu teṉpulattār (iṟantavar) vaḻipāṭē mutalil tōṉṟi iruntatu. piṉpu teṉpulattār teyva māyiṉar. itupaṟṟiyē vaḷḷuvaṉār “teṉpulattār teyvam” eṉak kūṟiṉāreṉka. iṉṟum maliyāḷattil teṟkaṭṭu eṉṉum vīṭṭiṉ oru pakutiyil iṟantavarkaḷiṉ cāmpar, avarkaḷ payaṉpaṭuttiya kittaṭi mutaliyaṉa vittu vaḻipaṭap paṭukiṉṟaṉa.
pūcāriyiṉ tōṟṟam
iṟantavarkaḷiṉ āvikaḷukku avarkaḷiṉ kiṭṭiya uṟaviṉar pali celutti vantaṉar. atikāri, aracaṉ mutaliya perumakkaḷiṉ āvikaḷuk kum avvāṟu ceyyappaṭṭatu. perumpālum vēliyāṭkaḷum aṭimikaḷum avvēliyic ceyyumpaṭi niyamikkappaṭṭaṉar. avarkaḷukkuk kūli koṭukkappaṭṭatu. avarkaḷ ceytuvarum paṇiviṭi kāl vaḻiyākat toṭarntu naṭipeṟum poruṭṭum, avarkaḷiṉ kūli eḷitiṟ kiṭikkum poruṭṭum accamātikaḷukku māṉiyaṅkaḷ viṭappaṭṭaṉa. nāṭkaḷ kaḻintaṉa. pūcārikaḷiṉ toṭak kattip paṟṟiya varalāṟukaḷ maṟakkappaṭṭaṉa. pūcāriyum avaṉ kuṭumpattiṉarum, camātiyum ataṟkuriya māṉiyaṅkaḷum tamakkuc contam eṉak karutiṉārkaḷ. camāti teyvamāṉapōtu pali iṭṭu vaḻipaṭum poruṭṭu makkaḷ avviṭaṅkaḷiṟ kūṭiṉārkaḷ. avi potumakkaḷ vaḻipaṭum iṭaṅkaḷāka māṟiṉa.
kōvilkaḷiṉ toṭakkam
toṭakkattil makkaḷ iṟantavarkaḷik kukiyil aṭakkañ ceytārkaḷ. itu oru kuṭici allatu pantariṉ kīḻ avarkaḷi viṭuvati ottatu. ellā nāṭukaḷilum kukikaḷ kāṇappaṭuvatilli. ākavē ceyaṟkik kukikaḷ ceyyappaṭṭu, avikaḷil pirētaṅkaḷ aṭakkañ ceyyappaṭṭaṉa. ekiptiya aracar uṭalkaḷ aṭakkañ ceyyappaṭṭuḷḷa kūrnutic camātikaḷ ivvakic ceyaṟkik kuṉṟu kaḷēyākum. puttar cēṭaṅkaḷi vittuk kaṭṭappaṭṭa “ṭākapā” eṉappaṭum camātikaḷum iv vakiyiṉavē. ekiptiya camātikaḷip pōṉṟavi teṉ amerikkāvilum kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa.1
teyvam uṟiyum kaṟkaḷic cuṟṟik kaṭṭaṭam eḻuntatu. ak kaṭṭaṭam muṟkālac camātikaḷ pōṉṟa kukikaḷ vaṭivākak kaṭṭap paṭṭaṉa. cila camayaṅkaḷil iṟantavariṉ kuṭiciyum, iṟantavarip putitta iṭattiṉ ayalē pali celuttum poruṭṭum, niḻaliṉ poruṭṭum, iṭappaṭṭa pantarum kōyilāka māṟiyuḷḷaṉa. makkaḷ nākarikam aṭin tārkaḷ. kaṭṭaṭaṅkaḷ aḻakākak kaṭṭappaṭṭaṉa. kōyil perukkap perukka vaḻipaṭu makkaḷum palarāyiṉar. avarkaḷ teyvattukkuk kāṇikki aḷittaṉar. pūcāri ak kāṇikkikaḷip peṟṟu celvaṉ āṉāṉ. kōyil evvaḷavukkup peritākiṉṟatō avvaḷavukkut teyvattiṉ uyarvum uṇṭākiṉṟatu. appoḻutu vaḻipaṭuvōrum atikarikkiṉṟaṉar. ataṉāl atika varuvāy uṇṭākiṉṟatu. ivi kaḷi aṟinta pūcāri ālayattip peritākavum aḻakākavum amikka lāṉāṉ. makkaḷ tām vaḻipaṭum teyvam tammippōla muṉ maṉita vaṭivil iruntateṉpati ippōtu nampamāṭṭārkaḷ.
camaya nūlkaḷ
kōyil evvaḷavu peritākiṉṟatō avvaḷavukkup pūcāriyum perumi aṭikiṉṟāṉ; teyvamum perumi aṭikiṉṟatu. teyvat tiṉ perumiyip poṟuttatē pūcāriyiṉ perumiyākum. pūcāri teyvattip perumippaṭutta eṇṇiṉāṉ. avaṉ teyvattip paṟṟip pala kaṟpaṉik katikaḷip puṉintāṉ. avikaḷōṭu cila uṇmi varalāṟukaḷiyum kalantukoṇṭāṉ. teyvat tiṉ perumi kaḷik kūṟum katikaḷiṉ iṭiyiṭēyē avaṉ taṉatu perumikaḷi yum nāṭṭa maṟantuviṭavilli. ivvāṟu teyvaṅkaḷip paṟṟiya “purā ṇaṅkaḷ” tōṉṟiṉa. pūcāri, tāṉ, taṉatum pali celuttum teyvatti ṉatum perumikaḷik kaṟpittu eḻutivitta nūlkaḷē muṟkālac camaya nūlkaḷākum.
camayam eṉpatil aṭaṅkiyavi
camayam eṉṟavuṭaṉ teyvam, pūcāri, pali, vaḻipaṭupavaṉ eṉṉum nāṉkiṉ tōṟṟaṅkaḷum namatu akattē eḻukiṉṟaṉa. innāṉkiṉ cērkkiyē camayam eṉṉum karuttu makkaḷ uḷḷattiṟ patiyalāyiṟṟu.
teyvaṅkaḷiṉ vaṭivam
camātik kaṟkaḷē teyvam uṟiyum iṭamākavittu vaḻipaṭap paṭṭaṉa. kaṟkaḷi vaḻipaṭṭa makkaḷ iṟantavarkaḷik kaṟkaḷil cetukki vittum vaḻipaṭuvārāyiṉar. im muṟiyiṉāl kaṟkaḷiṉ iṭattik kaṟkaḷil cetukkappaṭṭa āṇ peṇ uruvaṅkaḷ ēṟṟatum uṇṭu.
mara vaṇakkattiṉ tōṟṟam
iṟantavarkaḷ vaṇakkatti oppa, mara vaṇakkamum ivvulakam muḻumiyilum paraviyiruntatu. makkaḷ maraṅkaḷit teyvaṅkaḷāka vaḻipaṭuvatilli; am maraṅkaḷil teyvaṅkaḷ uṟivatākak karuti avikaḷiyē vaḻipaṭukiṉṟaṉar. pirētam putikkappaṭṭa iṭattil, muḷittu vaḷarum maraṅkaḷ iṟantavariṉ allatu avariṉ āvikaḷ uṟiyum iṭaṅkaḷākak karutappaṭṭaṉa. pirētaṅkaḷip putittapiṉ avviṭaṅkaḷil maraṅkaḷi allatu marakkiḷikaḷi nāṭṭum vaḻakku iṉṟum pala makkaḷiṭiyē kāṇappaṭukiṉṟatu. ākavē iṟantavarkaḷ āvikaḷukkuc ceyyappaṭum vaḻipāṭṭi oppa im maraṅkaḷum pali koṭuttu vaḻipaṭappaṭṭaṉa.
pāmpu vaṇakkam
camātikaḷil ūrntu cellum pāmpu, iṟantavariṉ piṟappu eṉṟu karutappaṭṭatu. ik karuttu allatu nampikki iṉṟum ulakiṉ pala pākaṅkaḷiluḷḷa makkaḷiṭiyē kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. ākavē pāmpukaḷ iṟantavarkaḷiṉ maṟu uruvaṅkaḷākak karutappaṭṭaṉa. 1ākavē makkaḷ ataṉik kollātu ataṟkup pāl vittum piṟa uṇavukaḷik koṭuttum vaḻipaṭalāyiṉar. ulakil pāmpu vaṇakkam kāṇappaṭāta iṭam illi eṉak kūṟalām. itaṉāl pāmpu vaḻipāṭum iṟantavar vaḻipāṭṭiṉ oruvaki eṉat terikiṉṟatu.
kiṇaṟukaḷ
muṟkālac camātikaḷ āṟukaḷiṉ arukē eṭukkappaṭṭaṉa. camātikaḷ kōyilkaḷāṉapōtu avikaḷiṉ pakkattiṟ cellum nīr ūṟṟukkaḷ teyvattaṉmi uṭiyaṉavākak koḷḷappaṭṭaṉa. avvāṟukaḷukkup palikaḷ iṭṭu vaṇaṅkappaṭṭaṉa. avi pāvattit tīrkkum tīrttaṅkaḷākak koḷḷappaṭṭaṉa. ellā iṭaṅkaḷilum āṟu iruppatilli. āṟu illāta iṭattil āṟṟukkup patil kiṇaṟu tōṇṭappaṭṭatu. kiṇaṟṟukkup palikaḷ iṭappaṭṭaṉa. ivvāṟu kōyilkaḷukkup pakkattē uḷḷa kiṇaṟukaḷ tīrttaṅkaḷāyiṉa.
kuṟippu: ituvariviṟ kūṟiyavi camayam tōṉṟiyatiṉ oru vaki. camayam vēṟu vaki yilum tōṉṟiyuḷḷatu. vevvēṟu vakiyākat tōṉṟiya camayak koḷkikaḷ oṉṟōṭu oṉṟu kalantuḷḷaṉa. avikaḷi iṉṟiya camayaṅkaḷuṭ kāṇalām.
tāy vaṇakkam
makkaḷiṉ muṟparuvattil tāyē atikāramuṭiyavaḷāyirun tāḷ; 1 āṭci avaḷ kiyil iruntatu. tantikkup piḷḷikaḷiṭattil urimi uṇṭākavilli. cottu peṇkaḷukkē uṭiyatāyiruntatu. ak kālattil makkaḷ tāyik kaṭavuḷāka vaḻipaṭṭaṉar. ulakil, mutal tōṉṟi naṭipeṟṟatu tāyvaṇakkam eṉpati varalāṟṟu āciriyarkaḷ ellōrum ottuk koḷkiṉṟaṉar.
taritteyvam
ip pūmiyiṉiṉṟum payir paccikaḷ tōṉṟuvatip paḻaṅkāla makkaḷ kaṇṭārkaḷ. avarkaḷukku atu mika viyappāyiruntatu. payir paccikaḷit tōṟṟuvikkiṉṟa it tariyi avarkaḷ tāyk kaṭavuḷākak koṇṭu vaḻipaṭalāṉārkaḷ. vitippuk kālaṅkaḷil avarkaḷ ik kaṭavuḷukkup palikaḷ iṭṭu vaḻipaṭṭārkaḷ. viḻāk kālaṅkaḷil iṭakkarāṉa kiriyikaḷ naṭattappaṭṭaṉa. ivvāṟu tōṉṟi naṭipeṟṟa tāyk kaṭavuḷ vaḻipāṭē, cattivaṇakkam eṉṉum peyar peṟuvatāyiṟṟu. iv vaḻipāṭu ulaka makkaḷ ellōrukkum potuvāṉatu.
kōyiṟ kiriyikaḷ
āvikaḷukkup paliyiṭṭōr oruvarukku uṇavu aḷikkum pōtu ceyyum upacāraṅkaḷit teyvattukkuc ceytārkaḷ. tāyk kaṭavuḷi vaḻipaṭṭōr oru tāykkuc ceyyappaṭum paṇiviṭikaḷi otta kiriyikaḷic ceytārkaḷ. ivvāṟu kiriyikaḷ makkaḷiṉ vāḻkki muṟiyi aṭippaṭiyākak koṇṭaṉa. piṟkālattil tām ceyyum kiriyikaḷiṉ poruḷ, maṟivāyirukkumpaṭi cila māṟṟaṅ kaḷiyum ceyyalāṉārkaḷ.
ñāyiṟṟu vaṇakkam
muṟkūṟiya vaḻipāṭukaḷ tōṉṟi naṭipeṟumpōtu iṉṉoru vaḻipāṭu tōṉṟiṟṟu. iv vulakil niṟintuḷḷa iruḷip pōkkuva tākiya ñāyiṟṟiṉ tōṟṟam makkaḷ karuttiṟpaṭṭatu. avarkaḷ ivvoḷiyuṭiyatākiya poruḷē ellāt teyvaṅkaḷukkum mēlāṉatu eṉṟu eṇṇiṉārkaḷ; pali celutti ataṉi vaḻipaṭ ṭārkaḷ. iv vaḻipāṭu ulaka makkaḷ ellōrukkum potuvāyuḷḷatu.
ñāyiṟṟi makkaḷ mali mukaṭukaḷiṟ kaṇṭu vaḻipaṭṭārkaḷ. ākavē kaṭavuḷiṉ iruppiṭam malimukaṭu eṉa makkaḷāl nampap paṭṭatu. ākavē ñāyiṟṟu vaṇakkam mali cūḻnta nāṭukaḷ oṉṟil tōṉṟiyiruttal ākalām.
cey kuṉṟukaḷ
ellā nāṭukaḷilum malikaḷ iruppatilli. maliyillāta nāṭukaḷil vāḻnta makkaḷ malikaḷukkup patil ceykuṉṟukaḷ eḻuppi ṉārkaḷ. ac cey kuṉṟukaḷ mītu ñāyiṟṟiṉ vaṭivāṉa vaṭivaṅkaḷi vittārkaḷ. aṅku ñāyiṟṟuk kaṭavuḷi vaḻipaṭṭārkaḷ. iv vakiyāṉa ñāyiṟṟiṉ kōyilkaḷ amerikkā, āppirikkā, mēṟku āciyā mutaliya nāṭukaḷil kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa.
mukkōṇak kaṟkaḷ
cey kuṉṟukaḷi eḻuppuvatu eḷitaṉṟu. ākavē makkaḷ ceykuṉṟu allatu malivaṭivamāṉa mukkōṇak kaṟkaḷi niḻal maraṅkaḷiṉ kīḻ niṟuttiṉārkaḷ. avikaḷi ñāyiṟṟiṉ vaṭivaṅkaḷāka vaḻipaṭṭārkaḷ. mukkōṇak kaṟkaḷ nāḷaṭivil aṭi akaṉṟu nuṉi oṭuṅkiya ‘ātīṇṭu kuṟṟi’kaḷiṉ vaṭivi aṭintaṉa.
tī, tiṅkaḷ vaḻipāṭukaḷ
oḷiyuṭiya ñāyiṟṟi vaḻipaṭṭa makkaḷ oḷiyuṭiyaṉavākiya tiṅkaḷ, tī eṉpavikaḷiyum vaḻipaṭalāyiṉar. kōyilkaḷil oru pōtum avintu pōkātapaṭi tī erittuk kāppāṟṟappaṭṭatu. ellāk kālaṅkaḷilum ñāyiṟu tiṅkaḷ eṉpavikaḷik kāṇṭal aritu. ākavē makkaḷ ñāyiṟu, tiṅkaḷ, tī eṉpavikaḷik kuṟikka vaṭṭam, piṟi, mukkōṇa vaṭivāṉa kuṇṭaṅkaḷil tī vaḷarttu, mūṉṟu oḷi yuṭip poruḷkaḷiyum vaḻi paṭuvārkaḷ. aṭi nimirntu nuṉi oṭuṅkiya kaṟkaḷ muccuṭarkaḷik kuṟikkum vaṭivaṅkaḷākavum karutappaṭṭaṉa.
pala uṟpattiyuṭiya kaṟṟūṇkaḷ ñāyiṟṟiṉ kuṟiyāka māṟutal
camātikaḷiṉ mītu niṟuttappaṭṭa kaṟṟūṇkaḷ, āvikaḷ uṟiyum iṭaṅkaḷ eṉak koḷḷappaṭṭu, vaḻipaṭappaṭṭaṉa eṉṟu muṉ kūṟiṉōm. paḻiya pali pīṭaṅkaḷum tūṇkaḷiṉ vaṭivip peṟṟu vaḻipaṭappaṭṭaṉa. ivvāṟu vaṇakkattuk kuriyaṉavākiya kaṟṟūṇkaḷ ippoḻutu ñāyiṟṟiṉ vaṭivam eṉak koḷḷappaṭalāyiṉa. itu paṟṟiyē ñāyiṟṟiṉ vaṭivākiya iliṅka uṟpattik kuriya paḻaṅkati palavākak kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa.
mikap paḻiya makkaḷ vaḻipaṭṭa tāyk kaṭavuḷiṉ vaṭivam
mikap paḻiya makkaḷ ‘cōki’ eṉṉum oru vakikkaṭal uyiriṉ ōṭṭiṉit tāyk kaṭavuḷiṉ vaṭivākak koṇṭu vaḻipaṭṭaṉar. itaṟkuk kāraṇam avvōṭu peṇkaḷ irakaciya uṟuppu pōṉṟa vaṭivuṭiyatu. im muṟiyiliruntu tāykkaṭavuḷik kuṟikkap peṇṇuṟuppiṉ vaṭivaṅkaḷum amittu vaḻipaṭap paṭalāyiṉa. ivvaki vaṭivaṅkaḷ ‘mokañcatarō’viṟ kāṇappaṭṭaṉa.
tanti āṭci uṇṭātal
ulakil tāyāṭciyē mutalil iruntateṉṟu ōriṭattiṟ kūṟiṉōm. ciṟitu ciṟitāka nilimi māṟat toṭaṅkiṟṟu. tanti āṭci uṇṭā yiṟṟu. appoḻutu ellāk kaṭavuḷukkum talivarākiya ñāyiṟṟuk kaṭavuḷi āṇ kaṭavuḷ eṉak karutappaṭalāyiṉar. atuvē ñāyiṟṟiṉ vaṭivamākiya iliṅkam, āṇ teyvamākak koḷḷappaṭṭatu.
vāṉak kaṭavuḷ
tarikkaṭavuḷit tāykkaṭavuḷākak koṇṭu vaḻipaṭṭa makkaḷ, vāṉattit tantik kaṭavuḷ eṉak koṇṭārkaḷ. ivvāṟu koṇṭa makkaḷ, iliṅkaṅkaḷi vāṉkaṭavuḷiṉ vaṭivākak koṇṭa ṉar. nāḷaṭivil vāṉ kaṭavuḷ ñāyiṟṟuk kaṭavuḷākak koḷḷap paṭṭatu. tarik kaṭavuḷ, vāṉkaṭavuḷkaḷi vaḻipaṭṭa makkaḷ, tarik kaṭavuḷi peṇvallami (uyirkaḷik karukkoṇṭu īṉukiṉṟa vallami) eṉṟum, vāṉ kaṭavuḷi āṇvallami (uyirkaḷi uṇ ṭākkukiṉṟa vallami) eṉṟum karutiṉārkaḷ. avarkaḷ iliṅkaṅ kaḷi āṇ vallami eṉavum koṇṭaṉar.
iliṅkattiṉ vaṭivu māṟupaṭutal
ivvāṟu koṇṭa makkaḷ iliṅkaṅkaḷi āṇ uṟuppu vaṭivāka amikkalāyiṉar. āṇ peṇ vallamikaḷ cērvatāl, paṭippukkaḷ tōṉṟukiṉṟaṉa eṉpati uṇarnta avarkaḷ, iru vaṭivaṅkaḷiyum iṇittu oru vaṭivamākak koṇṭum vaḻipaṭa lāyiṉar. ivvāṟu iṇinta vaṭivaṅkaḷ mēṟku āciyāvil ‘ellōkim’ eṉṉum peyar peṟṟaṉa. taṉi vaṭivam pettel, allā, pāl mutaliya peyarkaḷip peṟṟatu. intiya nāṭṭil ataṟku āvuṭiyār eṉṟu peyar.
ñāyiṟum tiṅkaḷum āṇ peṇ teyvaṅkaḷātal
intiya makkaḷ tiṅkaḷi āṇ teyvamākavē koṇṭārkaḷ. mēṟku āciya nāṭukaḷil tiṅkaḷ peṇ teyvamāka koḷḷappaṭṭatu. iliṅkaṅkaḷ niṟuttappaṭṭirunta niḻal maram, peṇ teyvamākak koḷḷappaṭṭatu. ñāyiṟum tiṅkaḷum kaṇavaṉ maṉiviyar eṉak koḷḷappaṭalāyiṉa. camātiyiṉ mītu vaḷarnta maram vaḻipaṭappaṭṭa teṉa muṉpu kūṟiṉōm. av vaḻipāṭṭukkuriya varalāṟukaḷum ip poḻutu mara vaṇakkattuk kuriyaṉavōṭu kalantaṉa. nāḷaṭivil marattukkup patil marattūṇ, kaṟṟūṇukkup pakkattē niṟutti vaḻipaṭap paṭṭatu. im marattūṇ vaṇakkattiyum oṉṟāka vittu mayaṅkaṟka. ippoḻutu iṟantavarkaḷiṉ āvi campantamāṉa vaṇakkaṅkaḷ ellām maṟakkappaṭṭu avi ñāyiṟu tiṅkaḷ toṭarpāṉa vaṇakkaṅkaḷ eṉak koḷḷappaṭṭaṉa.
aracak kaṭavuḷ
makkaḷiṉ aṟivu iṉṉoru niliyi aṭintapōtu avarkaḷ ñāyiṟē iv vulakattukkellām aracaṉ. avaṉāl makkaḷi āḷum poruṭṭu aṉuppappaṭṭa avaṉ putalvaṉē aracaṉ eṉa eṇṇat talippaṭṭārkaḷ. appoḻutu makkaḷ aracaṉukkuk kaṭavuḷukkuc ceyyum vaḻipāṭṭic ceytu vantaṉar. avarkaḷum tām kaṭavuḷiṉ atikārattip peṟṟu āḷap piṟantavarkaḷ eṉa nampi makkaḷ mītu atikāram celuttiṉar. iṟantapiṉ avarkaḷ ñāyiṟṟi aṭintu ñāyiṟṟuk kaṭavuḷāka māṟukiṉṟārkaḷ eṉa makkaḷ nampiṉārkaḷ. avarkaḷip putitta iṭattil ñāyiṟṟiṉ kuṟiyākiya kal naṭṭu vaḻipaṭṭārkaḷ. ivvāṟu tōṉṟiya ñāyiṟṟuk kaṭavuḷarē ekiptil “rā” eṉappaṭuvar.
aracaṉ āṇ kaṭavuḷākak karutappaṭṭatu pōla, araciyar peṇ kaṭavuḷarukkuriya mariyātiyip peṟṟaṉar.
ñāyiṟṟuk kaṭavuḷiṉ kōyilil aracaṉē pūcāriyāka iruntāṉ
aracaṉ ñāyiṟṟiṉ putalvaṉ eṉak koḷḷappaṭṭa pōtu ñāyiṟṟuk kaṭavuḷiṉ ālayam aracaṉukku uṟiviṭamāṉa araṇmaṉi yiṉ vaṭivi aṭintatu. ñāyiṟṟuk kaṭavuḷukkup pūci ceyyum pūcāri aracaṉāka iruntāṉ. cila camayaṅkaḷil araca kuṭumpattiṉarē pūcāriya rāka iruntu vantaṉar.
ñāyiṟṟuk kaṭavuḷiṉ vaṭivu māṟupaṭutal
ñāyiṟṟuk kaṭavuḷ, aracaṉukku aracaṉākak karutappaṭṭapōtu, makkaḷ avarip pēraracaṉ vaṭivil vaḻipaṭat toṭaṅkiṉārkaḷ.
ñāyiṟṟuk kaṭavuḷukku muṟkāla makkaḷ iṭṭu vaḻaṅkiya
iru ciṟanta peyarkaḷ
iv vulakil nākarikam peṟṟu viḷaṅkiya makkaḷ ellōrum nam muḻu mutaṟ kaṭavuḷukku iṭṭu vaḻaṅkiya peyarkaḷi ārāyiṉ, avi oḷi, allatu oḷiyuṭiyavaṉ eṉṉum poruḷkaḷuṭiyaṉavākak kāṇap paṭukiṉṟaṉa. ap peyarkaḷuḷ ‘el’ eṉṉum peyar mika virivu aṭintiruntatu. el eṉpatu oḷi eṉṉum poruḷ tarum paḻantamiḻc col. “ellē ilakkam” eṉpatu tolkāppiyam. mēṟku āciya nāṭukaḷil kaṭavuḷik kuṟikka el eṉṉum peyar ciṟappāka vaḻaṅkiṟṟu. arāpiyar mēṟku āciyā mutaliya nāṭukaḷil el toṭarpāṉa iṭap peyarkaḷ nūṟṟuk kaṇakkiṟ kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. avikaḷ ellām el kaṭavuḷiṉ kōyilkaḷ irunta iṭaṅkaḷākum. mukamatiyar vaṇaṅkum kaṭavuḷiṉ peyarākiya allā eṉṉum peyar el aṭiyākap piṟantatu. “ellā” eṉpatu allā eṉa vaḻaṅkum. kiṟistuva vētattilum el eliyaṉ, elōkim, elcaṭi mutaliya peyarkaḷ ‘yēkōvā’ kaṭavuḷik kuṟikka vaḻaṅkiṉa. aracar kaṭavuḷiṉ piṟappukaḷāka (avatāraṅkaḷ) koḷḷappaṭṭa pōtu avarkaḷum tamatu peyarkaḷiṉ iṟutiyil ‘el’ eṉṉum peyaric cērttu vaḻaṅkiṉārkaḷ. ‘el’ eṉṉum peyarē ‘pāl’ (Baal) pel (Bel) eṉat tirintum vaḻaṅkiṟṟu. kaṭavuḷiṉ aṭiya varkaḷum tam peyarkaḷuṭaṉ el, pāl, pel mutaliya peyarkaḷic cērttuk koṇṭaṉar. itu intiya makkaḷ cilar tam peyarkaḷuṭaṉ civam, piramam mutaliya peyarkaḷic cērttu vaḻaṅkuvati ottatu. ilaṅki aracar palar, tam peyarkaḷiṉ iṟutiyil civaṉ eṉṉum peyari iṭṭu vaḻaṅkiṉārkaḷ.
mēṟku āciyāvilaṉṟi intiya nāṭṭilum elleṉṉum peyar kaṭavuḷik kuṟikka vaḻaṅkiṟṟu. iṉṟum maliccātiyiṉar cilar ellammā, ellappaṉ (elliyaṉ) mutaliya kaṭavuḷari vaḻipaṭukiṉṟa ṉar. maṉuviṉ pēḻi ceṉṟu taṅkiyateṉappaṭum mali, iḷā virutam eṉappaṭukiṉṟatu. iḷāvirutam eṉpatil iḷā eṉpatu el eṉpataṉ tiripu. ilaṅkit tīviṉ paḻiya peyar ellam. ellam eṉpataṉ aṭi el. ellē piṉpu il āki ilaṅki īḻam mutaliya tiripukaḷip peṟṟatu. el toṭarpāṉa iṭap peyarkaḷ pala, ilaṅkiyiṟ kāṇap paṭukiṉṟaṉa. ‘nuvara eliyā’ eṉpatu avikaḷuḷ oṉṟu.
elli oppa mikap paḻami uṭiyatāy, ñāyiṟṟik kuṟikka vaḻaṅkiya peyar civaṉ. civaṉ eṉpataṟkuc civantavaṉ eṉpatu poruḷ. itaṟku aṭi civa(ppu). iṉṟum pilippiṉ tīvukaḷ cilavaṟṟiluḷḷa makkaḷ kaṭavuḷic civappaṉ eṉa vaḻaṅkuvar. civaṉ eṉṉum peyar, makkaḷiṭiyē tanti āṭci tōṉṟip, periya kaṭavuḷ āṇ eṉṉum koḷki uṇṭāyirunta kālattil tōṉṟiyiruttal vēṇṭum. mekcikōvil “kolaṟaṭō” āṟṟup paḷḷattākkiluḷḷa kuṉṟu oṉṟil, civaṉ ālayam oṉṟu uḷḷatu. civaṉ ālayam eṉpatu mali ucciyiluḷḷa taṭṭiyāṉa pakutiyēyākum. ac civaṉ ālayattiṉ kālam, kuṟintatu pattāyiram āṇṭukaḷukku muṟpaṭṭatāka vēṇṭu meṉa mēl nāṭṭu aṟiñar kūṟiyirukkiṉṟaṉar. epirēyariṉ (Hebrew) mūṉṟāvatu mātam civaṉ eṉappaṭṭatu. mōcē eṉpavar im mātat tiṉ āṟāvatu nāḷ kaṭavuḷāl taṉakku uṇarttappaṭṭa ēḻu kaṭṭaḷi kaḷi makkaḷukku veḷiyiṭṭār. mōcēyiṉ kālam iṟṟikku 17000 āṇṭukaḷiṉ muṉ. kirīs nāṭṭukku ayalē uḷḷa kirēttā (crete) eṉṉum tīvil, civaṉ eṉṉum paḻiya nakaram oṉṟu iruntatu. aṅku cintuveḷiyiṟ kiṭitta puti poruḷkaḷi ottavi kāṇappaṭṭaṉa. cakarā vaṉāntarattil civaṉ eṉṉum pālinilap pacuntari uṇṭu. aṅku ñāyiṟṟuk kaṭavuḷiṉ aḻipāṭukaḷ kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. ciṉṉa āciyāvil civās eṉṉum ōr iṭamuṇṭu. cumēriya makkaḷ cilar civaṉ eṉṉum peyarip peṟṟiruntaṉar. kiṟistuva maṟiyil col lappaṭum ciyaṉ (Cian) vaḻipāṭu civaṉ vaḻipāṭē eṉa mēṟ pula aṟiñarāl nāṭṭappaṭṭuḷḷatu. ilaṅkit tīvil civaṉ oḷimali eṉa oṉṟu uḷḷatu. ivi pōṉṟa pala cāṉṟukaḷāl el eṉṉum peyari oppac civaṉ eṉṉum peyarum ñāyiṟṟuk kaṭavuḷiṉ cālac ciṟanta peyarāka ivvulaka makkaḷāl vaḻaṅkappaṭṭateṉat terikiṉṟatu.
el allatu civaṉ kaṭavuḷiṉ vaṭivaṅkaḷ
iv vulakam muḻumiyilum el allatu civaṉ kaṭavuḷ kaṟṟūṇ vaṭivil vaḻipaṭappaṭṭār. makkaḷ varalāṟṟip paṟṟiya ārāycci yāḷar itaṉi naṉku ārāyntu kāṭṭiyuḷḷārkaḷ. makkaḷ ñāyiṟṟuk kaṭavuḷip pēraracaṉ vaṭivil vaḻipaṭṭa kālam oṉṟu uṇṭu eṉak kūṟiṉōm. av vaḻakku intiya nāṭṭilē toṭaṅki mēṟku nōkkip paraviyiruntateṉat terikiṉṟatu. civaṉ kaṭavuḷiṉ ūrti iṭapam. intiya makkaḷ āriyariṉ varukikkup piṉṉarē kutiriyip paṟṟi aṟintārkaḷ. ataṉ muṉ kaḻuti, erutu eṉpaṉa makkaḷiṉ ūrtika ḷāka iruntaṉa. ak kāla aracar māṭṭiyē ciṟanta ūrtiyākak koṇṭaṉar. piṟkālaṅkaḷil kaṭavuḷiṉ ūrtiyākiya iṭapamum kaṭavuḷāka vaṇaṅkappaṭṭatu. iv vaṇakkam mēṟkut tēcaṅkaḷukkup paraviṟṟu. appōtu nāṇayaṅkaḷilum muttirikaḷilum iṭapaṅkaḷ poṟikkappaṭṭaṉa. avviṭapaṅkaḷukku imil kāṇappaṭukiṟatu. imil uḷḷa iṭapaṅkaḷ intiya nāṭṭukkē uriyaṉa. itupaṟṟi iṭapa vaḻipāṭu intiya nāṭṭiṉiṉṟum mēṟkut tēcaṅkaḷukkuc ceṉṟa teṉat tuṇiyappaṭukiṉṟatu. intiya makkaḷ civaṉ kaṭavuḷi iṭapa ūrti uṭiyavarāyum, oru kiyil muttaliccūlam, uṭiyavarāyum maṟṟak kiyil kikkōṭari (maḻu)yi uṭiyavarāyum vaḻipaṭukiṉṟa ṉar. iv vaki vaṭivaṅkaḷ mēṟkut tēcaṅkaḷiṟ kāṇappaṭṭaṉavāyiṉ avi intiya nāṭṭiṉiṉṟum ceṉṟaṉa eṉṟu tuṇiyappaṭumaṉṟō? papilōṉ nāṭṭilum, ciriyā nāṭṭilum, ciṉṉa āciyāviluḷḷa kititi nāṭṭilum ivvaki vaṭivaṅkaḷ kāṇappaṭṭaṉa. ivvaki vaṭivaṅkaḷ kirēkka nāṭṭilum pirittaṉ (iṅkilāntu) nāṭṭilum vaḻipaṭappaṭṭaṉa eṉṟu mēṟpula aṟiñar ārāyntu kūṟiyuḷḷārkaḷ. ekiptiya makkaḷ iṭapatti vaṇaṅkiṉārkaḷ. avarkaḷiṉ amaṉ, ociṟis eṉa ñāyiṟṟik kuṟikkum kaṭavuḷariṉ ūrti iṭapamākavē iruntatu. 
kaṭavuḷ pēraracaṉ vaṭiviṉaṉāṉa pōtu paḻiya vaḻipāṭṭuc ciṉṉaṅkaḷ vantu aṭital
kaṭavuḷ pēraracaṉ vaṭiviṉaṉāṉapōtu, āvi vaṇakkattōṭu toṭarpu peṟṟirunta pāmpu, ak kaṭavuḷiṉ aṇikalamāyiṟṟu. āvikaḷ uṟiyum cuṭaliyil tirivaṉa eṉṟu karutappaṭṭa picācukaḷum pūtaṅkaḷum avar parivāraṅkaḷāyiṉa. ñāyiṟu, tiṅkaḷ, neruppu eṉṉum muccuṭar vaḻipāṭṭiṉariṉ mūṉṟu cuṭarkaḷum kaṭavuḷiṉ kaṇkaḷāyiṉa. cuṭaliyil kiṭakkum elumpukaḷ avar mālikaḷāyiṉa. cuṭaliyil uṇṭākum ūmatti erukku eṉpavi, avar cūṭum pūkkaḷāyiṉa. maṇṭi avar ēntum ōṭu āyiṟṟu.
tāykkaṭavuḷ
intiya makkaḷ tāykkaṭavuḷic ciṅkavākaṉa muṭiyavaḷākavum, oru kiyil taṇṭiyum iṉṉoru kiyil kēṭakattiyum vittirup pavaḷākavum koṇṭu vaḻipaṭukiṉṟaṉar. ekiptiya makkaḷ vaḻipaṭṭa tāyk kaṭavuḷ ciṅka ūrtiyiṉmēl niṟpatākum. itaṉi ottaṉavē ciṉṉa āciyā, ciriyā mutaliya nāṭukaḷil vaḻipaṭappaṭṭa, tāyk kaṭavuḷariṉ vaṭivaṅkaḷumākum. ciṉṉa āciyāvilē kititi eṉṉum iṭattilē kiṭitta paḻiya nāṇayam oṉṟil, oru pakkattē iru iṭapaṅkaḷ tāṅkum kaṭṭiliṉ mītu tantik kaṭavuḷum, iru ciṅkaṅkaḷ tāṅkum kaṭṭiliṉmītu tāyk kaṭavuḷum irukkum vaṭivaṅkaḷ poṟik kappaṭṭuḷḷaṉa. tāykkaṭavuḷ vaḻipāṭṭukkuriya ivvaṭivam, intiya nāṭṭiṉiṉṟē ceṉṟiruttal vēṇṭumeṉak karutappaṭukiṉṟatu. ivvulaka nākarikam intiya nāṭṭiṉiṉṟē maṟṟat ticikaḷukkup parantiruttal vēṇṭumeṉa ji.ār. haṉṭar (G. R.Hunter) heras pātiriyār, ṟis ṭēviṭs, cilṭi mutaliya pala mēlnāṭṭu ārāycci yāḷarkaḷ karutiṉārkaḷ.
mummūrttikaḷ
muṟkāla makkaḷ ellōriṭiyum mummūrttikaḷ vaḻipāṭu iruntu vantatu. mummūrttikaḷil tāy, tanti, kumāraṉ eṉṟu mūṉṟu kaṭavuḷarum aṭaṅkum. āriyamakkaḷ intiyanāṭu vanta piṉpu mummūrtti kaḷ piramā, viṭṭuṇu, uruttiraṉ eṉappaṭṭaṉar. itu tamiḻ makkaḷum, piṟa makkaḷum koṇṭa muṟiyaṉṟu.
cevvāṭi uṭuttutal
ñāyiṟu cenniṟakkaṭavuḷ ātaliṉ, ñāyiṟṟuk kaṭavuḷukkup pūci ceyyum pūcāri civanta uṭiyi uṭuttāṉ. aracaṉ ñāyiṟṟiṉ putalvaṉ eṉappaṭṭamiyiṉ avaṉum cevvāṭiyi uṭuttāṉ. ñāyiṟṟuk kaṭavuḷiṉ pūcārikaḷum aracarkaḷum allāmal araca kuṭumpattiṉarum civappu āṭiyi uṭuttaṉar. ekiptu papilōṉ mutaliya nāṭukaḷil teyvaṅkaḷukku uṭuttappaṭum uṭi civappu niṟam uṭiyatāka iruntatu. kirīs, urōm mutaliya nāṭukaḷil kurumār, araca kuṭumpattiṉar, perumakkaḷ allāta piṟar civappu āṭiyi uṭuttal ākātu eṉṉum caṭṭam iruntu vantatu. iṉṟum urōmaṉ kattōlikka uyarnta kurumār civappu aṅkiyiyē aṇivar. intiya nāṭṭilum ivvaḻakkē iruntu vantatu. mattiya tarikkaṭaliṉ kiḻakku ōraṅkaḷil vāḻnta piṉīciyar civappu āṭikaḷi intiyāvukkuk koṇṭuvantu vāṇikam purintārkaḷ. avvāṭi mika vili uyarntatāka iruntatu. piṟkālaṅkaḷil aracar pūcārikaḷ perumakkaḷ māttiram civappu āṭiyi aṇitalākiya vaḻakku maṟakkappaṭṭatu. kaṭavuḷiṉ aṭiyār eṉat tammik kāṭṭikkoḷḷa virumpiya makkaḷ ellōrum civappu āṭi uṭuttiṉar. civappu āṭi mika vili uyarntatāka iruntatu. ākavē civappukkup patil kāvi tōytta āṭikaḷ payaṉpaṭuttap paṭṭaṉa. putta kurumār tammi muṉṉiyavarkaḷiṉiṉṟum vēṟupaṭuttik kāṭṭum poruṭṭu mañcaḷ uṭi uṭuttaṉar. ituvē kāvi uṭi aṇivatiṉ varalāṟākum.
caṅkuvāttiyam
ivvulaka makkaḷ ellōrum caṅkip puṉitamuṭiyatākak koṇṭaṉar. caṅkuvāttiyam kaṭavuḷ vaḻipāṭṭiṟ payaṉpaṭuttap paṭṭatu. kiṟittuva vētattilum caṅkuvāttiyam payaṉpaṭuttappaṭṭa ceyti kāṇappaṭukiṉṟatu. iṉṟum cila kiṟittuva ālayaṅkaḷil cila ciṟappuk kālaṅkaḷil caṅku payaṉpaṭuttappaṭukiṉṟatu. intiyā, cappāṉ, amerikkā, kirēttā, kirīs mattiyatari nāṭukaḷilellām kōyil kaḷil caṅkuvāttiyam payaṉpaṭuttappaṭṭatu.
muttu
muttu uyirccattiyi aḷippatāka ellā makkaḷālum koḷḷap paṭṭatu. atu aracarālum perumakkaḷālum pūcārikaḷālum aṇiyap paṭṭatu. teyvaṅkaḷukkum avi aṇiyappaṭṭatu. muttukkuṭi, muttuppallakku mutaliyaṉa ciṟappuṭiyaṉa. muttu mikavum vili ēṟap peṟṟatu. piṟkālaṅkaḷil kaṭavuḷ toṇṭar eṉat tammik kāṭṭik koḷḷa virumpiya intiya nāṭṭu makkaḷ, muttukkup patil uruttirāk katti aṇintārākalām. itu ārāyccikkuriyatu.
cuvattikam
cuvattikam eṉpatu ñāyiṟṟiṉ kuṟi. iv vaṭiyāḷam iliṅka vaṇakkam, pāmpu vaṇakkaṅkaḷip pōla ulakam muḻumiyilum vaḻaṅkiṉa. ulakiṉ pala pākaṅkaḷil varalāṟṟuk kālattukku muṟpaṭṭa makkaḷ payaṉpaṭuttiya cuvattikam poṟitta poruḷkaḷ intiya nāṭṭilum, ulakiṉ pala pākaṅkaḷilum kāṇappaṭṭaṉa. putta matattiṉar ñāyiṟṟu vaḻipāṭṭiṉarākavē muṉ iruntārkaḷ. ākavē cuvattikatti avarkaḷ matacciṉṉamākak koṇṭaṉar. kāñciyiluḷḷa putta ālayat tiṉ aḻipāṭukaḷil civaliṅkaṅkaḷ pala kāṇappaṭṭaṉa. puttatantam eṉa vittu ilaṅki makkaḷāl vaḻipaṭappaṭuvatu puttariṉ pallaṉṟu; ciṟiya iliṅkamē eṉṟum, puttar kōyilkaḷil vikkappaṭum muṭi, iliṅkamēyeṉṟum ārāycciyāḷar kūṟiyuḷḷārkaḷ. cuvattika aṭi yāḷattiṉ iṉṉoru vakiyē ciluvik kuṟiyākum. kiṟittu nātarukku muṉpum ciluvik kuṟi camaya ciṉṉamākak koḷḷappaṭṭatu. atu kiṟittu nātar ciluviyil aṟiyappaṭṭamiyāl tōṉṟiyataṉṟu.
tēvatācikaḷ
teṉṉintiyak kōyilkaḷil tēvatācikaḷik kāṇkiṉṟōm. ivarkaḷiṉ kaṭamikaḷum oḻukkaṅkaḷum evi eṉpati īṇṭu virikka vēṇṭiyatilli. ivvakit tēvatācikaḷ papilōṉ, pālastīṉam, ciriyā, ciṉṉa āciyā, āpirikkā, kirīs, rōm mutaliya nāṭukaḷiluḷḷa kōyilkaḷilum iruntārkaḷ. tēvatāci vaḻakkam tōṉṟiyataṟkup pala kāraṇaṅkaḷ uṇṭu. muṉ ōriṭattil tarik kaṭavuḷ tāyk kaṭavuḷāka vaḻipaṭappaṭṭatu eṉak kūṟiṉōm. ak kaṭavuḷukkup peṇ pūcārikaḷē pūci ceytārkaḷ. aṅkup peṇ toṇṭarkaḷum vantu kūṭiṉārkaḷ. ak kaṭavuḷukkuc cantati uṟpattikkuriya nērttik kaṭaṉkaḷāl makiḻcci uṇṭākiṉṟateṉak karutappaṭṭatu. ākavē kōyilkaḷil āṇ aṭiyavarkaḷum, peṇ aṭiyavarkaḷum am makiḻccikkuriya ceyali av viṭattil nikaḻttuvārāyiṉar. aracaṉē kaṭavuḷāṉa pōtu, ñāyiṟṟuk kaṭavuḷiṉ kōyilkaḷil ceyyappaṭum kiriyikaḷ, ōr araṇmaṉiyil aracaṉukku avaṉ ēvalāḷar ceyyum paṇikaḷāka naṭattappaṭṭaṉa. aracaṉatu araṇmaṉiyil āṭalālum pāṭalālum aracaṉi makiḻvikkum peṇkaḷ palar iruntaṉar. itupaṟṟiyē tacarataṉukkum aṟupatiṉāyiram tēviyar. iṉṉum paḻiya nūlkaḷil collappaṭum aracarukkum nūṟṟukkaṇakkāṉa maṉiviyar irun tārkaḷ eṉak kūṟappaṭutal kāṇka. aracaṉ niṟivēṟṟum kiriyi kaḷik kaṭavuḷiṉ cārpāḷar (piratiniti)kaḷākiya kurumārē niṟivēṟṟi vantaṉar. piṉpu kōyilkaḷ viyapicāra viṭutikaḷāka māṟiṉa. ālayaṅ kaḷil kuṉṟāt tī vaḷarttalum vaḻakkāyiruntatu. mēṟkut tēcaṅkaḷil araca kumārikaḷum, uyarkulap peṇkaḷumē itaṟkāka niyamikkap paṭṭārkaḷ. kaṭavuṭpaṇi viṭi ceyyum poruṭṭu, ālayaṅkaḷil viṭappaṭṭa peṇkaḷ, kūṭā oḻukkamuṭiyavarkaḷāka māṟiyatum uṇṭu.
pali
paliyiṭum vaḻakku evvāṟu uṇṭāyiṟṟu eṉṟu muṉ kuṟippiṭṭuḷ ḷōm. maṉita paliyē teyvaṅkaḷukkup piriyamāṉatu eṉṟu makkaḷ karutiṉārkaḷ. maṉitar, maṉita ūṉ pucippavarkaḷāyirunta oru kālam iruntateṉpatip paṟṟi, nām varalāṟukaḷil paṭikkiṉṟōmaṉṟō? pōril ciṟi piṭikkappaṭṭōr, aṭimikaḷ, vilikku vāṅkappaṭ ṭōr, kuṟṟavāḷikaḷ eṉpōr perumpālum teyvaṅkaḷukkup paliyāka veṭṭappaṭṭaṉar. avarkaḷiṉ irattam kalaṅkaḷil ēnti teyvac cili mītum, makkaḷ mītum teḷikkappaṭṭatu. cila camayaṅkaḷil paliyiṭappaṭṭavarkaḷiṉ ūṉ pucikkappaṭṭatu. avvuṭalkaḷi neruppil iṭutalum, kōyiliṉ pakkattē uḷḷa maraṅkaḷiṟ kaṭṭit tūkkuvatum vaḻakkamāyiruntu vantatu. cila camayaṅkaḷil aracar tam piḷḷikaḷit teyvaṅkaḷukkup pali celutti irukkiṟārkaḷ. ivvakip paliyip paṟṟik kiṟittuva vētattiṉ paḻiya ēṟpāṭṭil kāṇalām.
aracaṉē teyvattukkuc ciṟanta pali eṉa makkaḷ oru kālattiṟ karutiṉārkaḷ. ivvāṟu aracaṉiyē makkaḷ koṉṟu pali celuttiya varalāṟukaḷ pala carittiraṅkaḷil kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. kaḷḷikkōṭṭi aracar paṉṉiraṇṭu āṇṭukaḷukkup piṉ taṟkoli puriya vēṇṭu meṉṉum vaḻakku iruntati mēlnāṭṭuc carittirakkārar kūṟiyiruk kiṉṟaṉar.
aracaṉukkup patil makkaḷāl terinteṭukkappaṭṭa, allatu vilikku vāṅkappaṭṭa oruvaṉi, aracaṉākap pāvittu paliyiṭuvatum vaḻakkāka iruntu vantatu. iṉṉum makkaḷ aṟivu ciṟitu paṇpaṭṭa pōtu maṉitaṉukkup patil erumi, māṭu, āṭu, paṉṟi, oṭṭakam mutaliya vilaṅkukaḷ paliyiṭappaṭṭaṉa. urōmiyil ilakkiya kālattilum maṉitarip paliyiṭum vaḻakkam iruntatu.
paliyiṭuvatip paṟṟiyum oru vakiyāṉa tattuva ñāṉam uṇṭā yiruntatu. palariṉ pāvattukkāka oruvaṉip paliyiṭutalē atuvākum. ivvāṟu makkaḷiṉ pāvattukkāka āṇṭil oru muṟiyō iru muṟiyō avarkaḷāl terinteṭutta makkaḷ paliyiṭappaṭṭārkaḷ. kiṟittu nātar makkaḷiṉ pāvattukkākac ciluviyil aṟiyuṇṭu iṟantār eṉappaṭuvatum iv vaḻakkip paṟṟiyatē. oruvaṉiṉ pāvat tukkāka iṉṉoruvaṉ kaṭavuḷit toḻutal pōṉṟa vaḻakkum, mēṟpaṭi koḷkiyiṉ niḻalēyākum.
cekannātattil palar tērccakkaraṅkaḷiṉ kīḻ paliyāka viḻuntu iṟantaṉar. koṇṭ makkaḷ tarik kaṭavuḷiṉ poruṭṭu maṉita pali celutti vantaṉar. ivi āṅkila aracāṭciyārāl niṟuttappaṭṭaṉa. purāṇaṅkaḷil narapaliyāl teyvam āyiram āṇṭukaḷukkut tirupti yuṟukiṉṟatu eṉṟu eḻutappaṭṭuḷḷatu.
iṟantavar poruṭṭum palikaḷ celuttappaṭṭaṉa. iṟantavaṉit tīyiliṭṭuk koḷuttumpōtu avaṉ maṉivi, nāy, aṭimikaḷ pōṉṟavarkaḷum koḷuttappaṭṭārkaḷ. iṟanta kaṇavaruṭaṉ maṉivi yiyum patikkap patikkat tīyiliṭṭuk koḷuttum vaḻakkam (āṅkila āṭciyiṉarāl niṟuttappaṭum vari) intiya nāṭṭil iruntuvantatu. ataṟku vitīkar mantiraṅkaḷōṭu kūṭiya kiriyikaḷiyum eḻuti vittiruntārkaḷ. āppirikkāvil iṟantavaṉ oruvaṉukkuc ceyti aṉuppa vēṇṭi iruntāl ac ceytiyi aṭimi oruvaṉ kātil colliyapiṉ avaṉ kaḻuttuk koyyappaṭṭatu.
makkaḷ ivvāṟu teyvaṅkaḷukku maṉitariyum vilaṅkukaḷ paṟavikaḷiyum veṭṭik koṉṟu paliyiṭuvatē, tām ceyyat takunta mēlāṉa kaṭavuṭpaṇi eṉa nīṇṭakālam nampi vantārkaḷ. uyirkaḷik kolvatu pāvam eṉṉum uṇarcci avarkaḷ uḷḷattiṟ piṟakka villi.
mēṟkut tēcaṅkaḷil kiṟittuva matam tōṉṟip paraviṟṟu. ak kālaṅkaḷil paḻiya paliyiṭum vaḻakkaṅkaḷ ciṟitu ciṟitāka niṉṟu pōyiṉa. kiṟittuva camayattukkup piṉ mukamatiya camayam tōṉṟiṟṟu. appoḻutum iv vaḻakkam mēl nāṭukaḷil niṉṟu pōyiṟṟu.
intiya nāṭṭil aṟiyāmiyuṭiya makkaḷiṭiyē paliyiṭum vaḻakkam iruntu varuvatāyiṟṟu. āriyariṉ matattil paliyiṭuvatē mukkiya koḷki. paliyiṭṭu yākaṅkaḷ ceyvatāl, maṉitaṉ tēvar kaḷukku aracaṉāṉa pataviyi aṭikiṉṟāṉ eṉṉum koḷki valipeṟṟiruntatu. ākavē kutiriyākam, pacuyākam, āṭṭukkaṭā yākam, naramēta yākam pōṉṟa pala yākaṅkaḷ ceyyappaṭṭu vantaṉa. kurukkaḷāyiruntu avvaki yākaṅkaḷic ceyvataṟku ēṟpaṭṭōrē pirāmaṇar eṉṉum kuḻuviṉarāvar.
makkaḷiṉ aṟivu paṇpaṭṭatu; pāva puṇṇiyaṅkaḷip paṟṟiya aṟivu uṇṭāyiṟṟu. paṇṭu tām aṟiyāmiyāṟ purintu vanta palikaḷi, avarkaḷāl viṭamuṭiyavilli. ākavē avarkaḷ māvi ṉāl mirukaṅkaḷiyum paṟavikaḷiyum maṉitariyum ceytu teyvaṅ kaḷukkup paliyiṭṭārkaḷ. māviṉāṟ ceyta paṇiyāraṅkaḷip paṭittārkaḷ. cilar irattattiṉ kuṟi illāmal ceyyappaṭum paliyil tirupti uṟavilli. ākavē miruka palikkup patil pūciṉikkāy veṭṭappaṭṭatu. irattattukkup patil kuṅkumam pūcappaṭṭatu. iṉṟu iṭappaṭṭu varum pūciṉikkāyp pali, mirukapaliyiṉ tēyvēyākum.
pūcārikaḷ palamaṭital
pūcārikaḷ evvāṟu tōṉṟiṉārkaḷ eṉṟu muṉ kūṟiṉōm. kōyilkaḷ pala tōṉṟiṉa. kōyilkaḷil puriyum paṇiviṭikaḷ pala iruntaṉa. oruvaṉ mēlāṉa pūcāriyāka iruntāṉ. avaṉukku uṭ paṭṭup paṭippaṭiyē tāḻnta paṇikaḷic ceyvataṟkup pala paṭiyāṉa pūcārikaḷ iruntaṉar. urōmaṉ kattōlikka pūcāri variciyil itaṉik kavaṉikkalām. tamiḻnāṭṭil āṟuvakip pārppār eṉap paṭṭōrum ivvakiyiṉarē. oru kirāmattil allatu oru ūril kōyilē mukkiyam. kōyilic cūḻntu makkaḷ iruntārkaḷ. kirāmam allatu ūr, kōyilil irukkum kaṭavuḷ cārpāṉa peyarippeṟṟatu. makkaḷukkākak kōyil iruppatu eṉṉum karuttu māṟupaṭṭuk kōyilukkāka makkaḷ irukkiṟārkaḷ eṉṉum koḷki uṇṭā yiṟṟu. pūcāri kaṭavuḷiṉ viruppaṅkaḷi aṟintu collavum, makkaḷiṉ tēvikaḷik kaṭavuḷukku uṇarttavum, vallavaṉ eṉṟu makkaḷ nampiṉar. ataṟkēṟpa avaṉ kaṭavuḷiṉ vākku eṉa veḷippāṭu (oracle) coṉṉāṉ. makkaḷ avaṉiṭam mikavum payapatti uḷḷavarkaḷāka iruntaṉar. pañcam piṇi pōṉṟa kālaṅkaḷil makkaḷ avaṉi yōcaṉi kēṭṭārkaḷ. avaṉ teyvam āṭik, kaṭavuḷiṉ eṇṇaṅ kaḷit terivittāṉ. cila camayaṅkaḷil teyvam aracaṉiyē paliyākak kēṭkiṉṟatu eṉṟu avaṉ coṉṉāṉ. uṭaṉē makkaḷ aracaṉik koṉṟu paliyiṭṭārkaḷ.1
mōṭca narakaṅkaḷiṉ tiṟavukōl tamatu kiyil iruppatākavum, avarkaḷ makkaḷi nampa vittu naṭu naṭuṅkac ceytārkaḷ. ivarkaḷ aracariyum aṭi vaṇaṅkumpaṭi ceyyum valimiyip peṟṟaṉar. cakkara varttikaḷum avaṉ kāl aṭikaḷi muttamiṭṭārkaḷ.2 12 ām nūṟ ṟāṇṭil pōppāṇṭavar aracarukkāvatu vicuppāṇṭavarukkāvatu oru atikāramum illi eṉṟum, avarkaḷ peṟṟuḷḷa atikāram taṉṉiṭattiṉiṉṟu kiṭittatākumeṉṟum, tām ulakattukkut talivaṉ eṉṟum ōr aṟikkiyi veḷiyiṭṭār.
pūcārikaḷ mantiravātikaḷ
potumakkaḷ uyarnta aṟivukkuk kaṭṭuppaṭamāṭṭārkaḷ; maruntu, māntirīkam pōṉṟa vittikaḷukkē aṭimippaṭuvārkaḷ. itaṉi muṟkālap pūcāri aṟiyātavaṉallaṉ. avaṉ cila tantiraṅ kaḷik kiyāṇṭu makkaḷi vacappaṭuttiṉāṉ. avaṉ maṟṟavarkaḷ viḷaṅkik koḷḷāta vakiyil cila kiriyikaḷic ceytāṉ. maṟṟavarkaḷ viḷaṅka māṭṭāta cila coṟṟoṭarkaḷi mantirameṉa muṇumuṇuttāṉ. avaṉ ceyyum kiriyikaḷilum, collum mantiraṅ kaḷilum periya vallami iruppatāka makkaḷ nampiṉārkaḷ, iṉṉum nampi varukiṟārkaḷ. iṉṉum pūcāri nōykaḷukku nūl kaṭṭutal, kuḻi aṭittu mantiram (pāṭam) pōṭutal, taṇṇīril mantiram ōtik koṭuttal, teyvam ēṟi āṭi veḷippāṭu kūṟutal pōṉṟavi, paḻami toṭṭup pūcārikaḷ kiyāṇṭu varum tantiraṅkaḷēyākum.
camaya campantamāṉaviyum, kaṭavuḷ aruḷāl collappaṭṭaṉa veṉṟu avarkaḷāl eḻutappaṭṭaṉavumāṉa nūlkaḷi maṟṟavarkaḷ aṟiyāvaki maṟittu vittārkaḷ, paḻiya kiṟittavarkaḷ, āriyar, tamiḻar, ekiptiyar ellōriṭiyum iv vaḻakku iruntatu. kurumārkaḷ, maṟṟavarkaḷukku viḷaṅkāta oru moḻiyi vittuk koḷvatu vaḻakkam. ivvāṟu illāviṭil potumakkaḷi ēmāṟṟuvatu kaṭiṉamākum.
tokuppuri
ituvariyum kūṟiyavaṟṟāl, muṟkālattut toṭaṅki naṭi peṟṟa camayam eṉṉa eṉṟu namakku viḷaṅkukiṉṟatu. iṟantavarkaḷiṉ āvi vaṇakkattil toṭaṅkiya camayam, pūcārikaḷiṉ āṭci variyil paṭippaṭiyē vaḷarcci aṭintati nām naṉku aṟintukoṇṭōm. pūcārikaḷiṉ atikāram mēl ōṅkiyirunta kālattil, avarkaḷ tamatu varuvāyi nāṭip pala mūṭap paḻakkavaḻakkaṅkaḷi makkaḷiṭiyē tōṟṟuvittaṉar. ap paḻakkaṅkaḷi nilināṭṭum poruṭṭuk kaṭavuḷ coṉṉatākap pala kaṟpaṉi nūlkaḷi eḻuti, makkaḷiṭiyē paravac ceytaṉar. maṟumiyil taṉatu nilimi eṉṉa ākumō eṉṟu niṉittu ēṅkik koṇṭirunta makkaḷ, maṟumiyil tamakku nērakkūṭiya tuṉpaṅkaḷit tāṇṭuvataṟkut teppam kiṭittateṉa niṉittu appoy nūlkaḷiṟ collappaṭṭavāṟu oḻukat talippaṭṭārkaḷ. pala nūṟṟāṇṭukaḷākat toṭarntu varukiṉṟa am mūṭap paḻakkaṅkaḷi makkaḷ caṭutiyil niṟuttuvatu aritu. mācimakat tīrttam eṉṟu makkaḷ kōṭikkaṇakkil kumpalāyk kūṭik kuḷattil kuḷikkiṉṟaṉar. itaṟkuk kāraṇam kuṟikkappaṭṭa oru kuḷattil, kuṟikkappaṭṭa oru nāḷil kuḷittāl maṉitaṉ purinta pāvaṅkaḷ kaḻiyum eṉap pūcārikaḷ eḻuti vitta katiyē ākum. makkaḷ ellōrum pāvam ceypavarkaḷē. pāvam ceyyum mūṭamakkaḷ ataṉi eḷitil kaḻuviviṭalāmeṉat tiraḷkiṉṟaṉar. cukātārak kuṟiviṉāl vāntipēti pōṉṟa tottu nōy kaṇṭu uṭaṉē iṟakkiṉṟaṉar. pūcārikkup paṇam koṭuttuk kaṭavuḷukkuk kuṭamuḻukkāṭṭutal, āyiran tirunāmaṅkaḷic collac ceytal pōlvaṉa, pūcāriyiṉ “uṇṭiyali” nirappumpaṭi ceyyap paṭṭuḷḷa cūḻccikaḷē aṉṟip piṟavalla. tiruppatikkuk kuṭi koṇṭu pōtal pōṉṟa vaḻakkamum iv vakiyiṉatē. uṇmiyāka īṭēṟum vaḻiyi makkaḷ aṟintukoḷḷātu, muṭṭāḷ taṉamāka vīti vītiyāka alintu allōla kallōlap paṭuvatu mika mika iraṅkat takkatu. makkaṭ camūkam īṭēṟuvataṟku iṉṟu aṟiñar ceyyattakkatu pūcāri āṭciyi oḻippatum, makkaḷ camayam eṉṉum peyarāl viḻalukkiṟitta nīri oppa, poruḷiyum kālattiyum virayam ceyvatiyum taṭuppatumēyākum. iṉṟiya camayattiṉ muṭivu ettattuvak koḷkikaḷiyum aṭippaṭiyākak koḷḷātu. cōmpēṟikaḷākiya pūcārikaḷik koḻukka vippatēyākum.
camaya cīrtiruttam
mēṟku ulakil camayam mikavum cīraḻintiruntatu. camayam eṉṉum peyarāl pala koṭumikaḷ naṭantaṉa; kolikaḷ atikarittaṉa; viyapicāraṅkaḷ perukiṉa. pūcāri āṭci uccanili aṭintiruntatu. akkālattilēyē pālastīṉ nāṭṭil kiṟittunātar tōṉṟiṉār. avar teyvam oṉṟu eṉṉum koḷkiyi upatēcittār; “taṉṉip pōl piṟari nēci” eṉa makkaḷukku nallaṟivu koḷuttiṉār. kiṟittunātariṉ nallupatēcaṅkaḷ makkaḷiṉ maṉattik kavarntaṉa. palar avarukku māṇākkarāṉārkaḷ. nallaṟivu peṟa āvalkoṇṭa makkaḷ avaric cūḻntārkaḷ. kurumār itaṉik kaṇṭu poṟārāyiṉar. avari evvakiyilēṉum koṉṟuviṭak karutiṉārkaḷ; avar, tāṉē aracaṉ eṉa makkaḷukkup pōtittār eṉa, nītipatiyiṉ muṉ kuṟṟañcāṭṭiṉar. avaṉ avari avamāṉappaṭuttic ciluviyil aṟintu kollumpaṭi kaṭṭaḷi iṭṭāṉ. ak kālattil mata cīrttiruttañ ceyya eḻuvōriṉ muṭivu ivvāṟāka iruntatu. pūcārikaḷ, allatu kurumār tamatu atikārattukkup paṅkam viḷiyāta vāṟu mēṟkūṟappaṭṭatu pōṉṟa aṭakkumuṟic ceyalkaḷik ki yāṇṭu vantaṉar. pōppu āṭciyil ivvakiyāṉa pala koṭumikaḷ naṭantaṉa. avikaḷ varalāṟukaḷiṟ kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. mattiya kālat til uyarnta kalvi aṟivuṭiya oru pirapu, pōppu āṭcikku māṟāka nūl veḷiyiṭṭataṉ viḷivāka, kātu mūkku mutaliya uṟuppukkaḷ aṟukkappaṭṭum, cavukkāl aṭikkappaṭṭum ciṟiyiliṭṭum cittira vati ceyyappaṭṭa varalāṟu, nūlkaḷiṟ kāṇappaṭukiṉṟatu. 1kiṟittu nātar piṟkāla makkaḷkaḷāl vaḻipaṭappaṭṭār. kiṟittu matam pōp āṭcikku uṭpaṭṭup paḻiya pūcāri āṭciyiṉ kaṭumiyi aṭinta pōtu, mārṭiṉ lūtar eṉṉum pēraṟiñar tōṉṟi cīrtiruttattik koṇṭuvantār. mārṭiṉ lūtariṉ cīrtirutta muṟikaḷip palar piṉpaṟṟiṉar. avarkaḷ pōppu āṭciyiṉiṉṟum naḻuvi ip putiya matattil cērntaṉar.
kiṟittunātarukkup piṉ mukamatu napi eṉṉum oru periyār arāpiya nāṭṭil tōṉṟiṉār. akkālattil pūcāri āṭciyum ciṟu teyva vaḻipāṭukaḷum, peritum taliyeṭuttiruntaṉa. appoḻutu ‘napi kaṭavuḷ oruvarē uḷar; avar allā. vikkiraka vaḻipāṭukaḷ aḻikkat takkaṉa, eṉṟu makkaḷiṭiyē pōtittār. ataṉāl kōyilkaḷil varuvāy kuṟiyat toṭaṅkiṟṟu. pūcārikaḷ napiyik kolla muyaṉṟārkaḷ. napi ciṟanta pōrvīraṉ. avar palarit tamakkup pakka palamākat tiraṭṭik koṇṭu paṭi palattiṉāl nāṭṭiyē tam vacappaṭuttik koṇṭu taṉatu koḷkikaḷi nilināṭṭiṉār. kiṟittu matam, mukamatu matam eṉpavi mikap paraviṉamiyāl, makka ḷiṭiyē camayam eṉṉum peyaruṭaṉ kāṇappaṭṭa mūṭap paḻakka vaḻakkaṅkaḷ pala maṟintaṉa.
intiya nāṭṭi āriyar aṭintapōtu, vilaṅkukaḷik koṉṟu iyaṟṟappaṭum yākaṅkaḷāl māttiram makkaḷ īṭēṟalām eṉṉum pollāta koḷki makkaḷiṭiyē paraviṟṟu. eṇṇiṟanta vilaṅkukaḷ yākam eṉṉum peyariṉāl kollappaṭṭaṉa. ap poḻutu puttar eṉṉum periyavar vaṭanāṭṭil tōṉṟiṉār. avar āriyariṉ pollāta koḷkikaḷi etirttup pōrāṭiṉār. avar uṇmi upatēcaṅkaḷik kēṭṭa makkaḷ avarip piṉpaṟṟiṉar. ivar araca kuṭumpattavarāy iruntār. ivarukkup potumakkaḷiṉ ātaravu peritāka iruntatu. ākavē kiṟittu nātarik koṉṟatu pōlap pūcārimārāl puttariyum kolla muṭiyavilli. puttamatam ulakam eṅkum paraviṟṟu. makkaḷ puttariyē kaṭavuḷāka vaṇaṅkat talippaṭ ṭārkaḷ.
piṟkālattil tōṉṟiya civa camaya kuravarkaḷ, oru teyva vaḻipāṭṭiyē vaṟpuṟuttiṉārkaḷ. iṉṟu tamiḻaruṭiya camayam uṇmip pōkkiṉiṉṟum vilakiyuḷḷatu. paruppi eṟittuviṭṭuk kōtik kippaṟṟiyavaṉip pōla makkaḷ uṇmi vaḻiyi nāṭātu vīṇ āravāraṅkaḷiyē poruḷeṉak karutic cīraḻikiṉṟaṉar. iṉṟu perum puraṭci tōṉṟic camayattil cīrtiruttam uṇṭākka vēṇṭiyatu avaciyamākum.
tattuvañāṉam utayamātal
makkaḷiṉ aṟivu kālattukkuk kālam paṇpaṭṭuvantatu, āyiṉum perumpālōriṉ pōkku paḻiya pōkkilēyē ceṉṟatu. ciṟupāṉmi yōr maṉaamitiyuṭaṉ iruntaṉar. avarkaḷ camayam eṉṉum peyarāl ulakil naṭappavikaḷi nōkkiṉar. avikaḷil uyarnta koḷkikaḷ eviyum iruppatik kāṇārāyiṉar. ākavē uṇmi kāṇuvatil avarkaḷiṉ uḷḷam āḻntu ceṉṟatu. maṉitaṉiṉ maṉam mika āṟṟal vāyntatu. ataṉi ōr iṭattil niṟuttiṉāl periya āṟṟal uṇṭākiṉṟatu. maṉati oru vaḻippaṭuttic ceyyappaṭum maṉōvaciyam (hipnāṭṭicim) aṟituyil (māknaṭṭicim) mutaliya vittikaḷiṟ payiṉṟōr, nām viyakkattakka aruñceyalkaḷic ceytu kāṭṭukiṉṟaṉaraṉṟō? maṉati oru vaḻippaṭuttiya makkaḷ, tammip paṟṟiyum ulakippaṟṟiyum ivviraṇṭiyum iyakkum kaṭavuḷip paṟṟiyum uṇmikaḷik kāṇa muyaṉṟu vantārkaḷ. iv vuṇmikaḷi āravāraṅkaḷāṟ kāṇamuṭiyātu. mokañcatarōvil yōkattil vīṟṟirukkum kaṭavuḷ vaṭivuṭiya muttiri oṉṟu kāṇappaṭu kiṉṟatu. itaṉāl mika muṟkālattil aṟiñar cilar, maṉatti oruvaḻip paṭuttap paḻaki uṇmikaḷi aṟiya muyaṉṟu vantārkaḷ eṉat terikiṉṟatu.
avvāṟu maṉati oruvaḻippaṭuttiya aṟiñar uyir, ulakam, iṟivaṉ eṉṉum mupporuḷ uṇmikaḷi aṟintārkaḷ. tām aṟintavaṟṟip pakkuvam vāynta cilarukkuk kūṟiṉārkaḷ. ivvuṇ mikaḷ ivvāṟu nīṇṭakālam kuru māṇākka muṟiyil vantaṉa. avarkaḷ potu makkaḷ camayam eṉakkoṇṭu uḻalum puṟaviṭayaṅ kaḷil maṉam paṟṟātiruntaṉar. ivvāṟu ulakil iruvakic camayaṅkaḷ nilaviṉa. muṉṉatip puṟaccamayam eṉṟu kūṟalām. ataṉit tēṅkāyic cuṟṟi mūṭiyuḷḷa tōlukku oppiṭalām. pintiyatit tōliṉkīḻum, vayiramāṉa ōṭṭiṉ kīḻum uḷḷa ataṉ paruppukku oppiṭalām.
maṉam, vaḷarcci aṭivatiṉālē makkaḷ uyarnili eytutal kūṭum. mūṭap paḻakka vaḻakkaṅkaḷiṉāl maṉitaṉ tāḻnili eytuvāṉ. namatu nāṭṭil makkaḷ mūṭap paḻakka vaḻakkaṅkaḷukku aṭimikaḷāka irukkiṉṟaṉar. ākavē, avarkaḷ ellāt tuṟikaḷilum tāḻntu, ulaka makkaḷilēyē tāḻnta niliyiṉar eṉṉumpaṭi nāḷ vītam oṭuṅki varukiṉṟaṉar.
tattuva ñāṉaṅkaḷōṭu kūṭiya camayam, mēṟku ulakattavarāl aṟiyappaṭāmal iruntatu. kirēkka nāṭṭilē ki.mu. āṟām nūṟṟāṇṭu variyil pitākāras eṉṉum aṟiñar iruntār. avar uyir, ulakam, kaṭavuḷ pōṉṟa uṇmikaḷi viḷakkum ñāṉatti mutaṉ mutal kirēkka makkaḷukku veḷiyiṭṭār. ivar intiya nāṭṭukku yāttiri ceytu kapilariṉ cāṅkiya matakkoḷkikaḷip payiṉṟu ceṉṟār eṉṟu kōlpurūk (Colebrooke) eṉṉum āciriyar kūṟiyuḷḷār. kirēkkariṉ tattuva ñāṉak koḷkikaḷ perumpālum teṉṉintiya makkaḷiṉ cittānta cāttira nūṟporuḷkaḷi ottaṉa.
tamiḻariṉ camayam
ituvariyil ulaka makkaḷ ellōrukkum potuvāyuḷḷa camayakkoḷkikaḷik kūṟivantōm. muṟkālac camayam eṉpatu makkaḷiṉ palavakippaṭṭa aṟivu vaḷarccip paruvaṅkaḷil tōṉṟi vaḻaṅkiya paḻakka vaḻakkaṅkaḷiṉ tokutikaḷākak kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. iṉṟu kalvi aṟivillāta potumakkaḷiṉ camayam ituvē. kalvi yaṟivuḷḷavarkaḷil palarum ituvē uṇmiyāṉa camayam eṉak karuti varukiṉṟaṉar. “paḻakkaṅ koṭitukāṇ” eṉa oru tattuvañāṉi kūṟiyuḷ ḷār. cittānta nūlkaḷil kūṟappaṭṭuḷḷa tattuvak koḷkiyuṭiya camayam kāṇappaṭavilli.
mokañcatarō makkaḷiṉ camayam
mokañcatarō makkaḷiṉ camayam iṉṟikku aiyāyiram āṇṭu kaḷukku muṟpaṭṭatu. mokañcatarō muttirikaḷil poṟikkappaṭṭa eḻuttukkaḷik koṇṭu paḻiya cintuveḷit tamiḻariṉ camayam ev vakiyiṉatu eṉṟu nammāl aṟiyakkūṭiyatāy irukkiṉṟatu. heras pātiriyār mokañcatarōc camayattippaṟṟi ārāyntu kūṟi yiruppati iṅkut tarukiṉṟōm.1
mokañcatarō muttiri oṉṟil, “iṟuvaṉ kommiṉṉaṉīr” eṉap poṟikkappaṭṭuḷḷatu. kaṭavuḷukkuk kompu (vāttiyam) ūtukiṉṟa mīṉavar eṉpatu ataṉ poruḷ. iṉṉoru muttiriyil “kōyil ellāk kaṭavuḷ atu” eṉṟu poṟikkappaṭṭuḷḷatu. kōyililuḷḷa ellāk kaṭavuḷarilum periya kaṭavuḷ eṉpatu ataṉ poruḷ. iraṇṭu paṭṭiyaṅkaḷ nālūril irukkum viṭukaṇ eṉṉum kaṭavuḷippaṟṟik kūṟukiṉṟaṉa, kaṭavuḷarukku kaṇṇimi illi eṉa vaḻaṅkum intiya makkaḷiṉ aitīkaktōṭu itu peritum ottirukkiṉṟatu. avarkaḷ ellāvaṟṟiyum pārttukkoṇṭu irukkiṉṟamiyāl, kaṇṇi mūṭamāṭṭārkaḷ eṉpatē kaṇṇi imiyātavarkaḷ eṉpataṉ poruḷākum.
oru muttiriyil mūṉṟu mukaṅkaḷ uṭiyatum, yōkattil amarn tiruppatum ākiya ōr kaṭavuḷiṉ vaṭivam kāṇappaṭukiṉṟatu. ataṉic cūḻntu yāṉi, kāṇṭāmirukam, puli, erutu mutaliya vilaṅkukaḷ kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. cēryōṉ mārcal eṉpār avvaṭi vam civaṉip pacupati eṉṟu kāṭṭum poruṭṭu amikkappaṭṭa teṉṟu kūṟiyuḷḷār. ōr iṭattil kaṭavuḷik kuṟikka eṇmi eṉṉum peyar kāṇappaṭukiṉṟatu. oru paṭṭiyam kaṭavuḷiṉ mūṉṟu kaṇkaḷip paṟṟik kūṟukiṉṟatu. mūṉṟu paṭṭiyaṅkaḷ kaṭavuḷiṉ ōr kaṇṇip paṟṟik kūṟukiṉṟaṉa. avi kuṟippiṭṭuḷḷa “ōr kaṇ” kaṭavuḷiṉ mūṉṟāvatu kaṇṇiyākum. kaṭavuḷ pērāṇ eṉṉum peyarālum vaḻipaṭappaṭṭār. pērāṇ eṉpatē perumāṉ eṉṟu āyiṟṟuppōlum. kaṭavuḷ tāṇṭavam ceypavar eṉṉum karuttum, akkāla makkaḷiṭiyē paravi iruntatu. itu “tāṇṭavaṉ ir nāl maram” eṉṉum paṭṭiyattāl naṉku viḷaṅkukiṉṟatu.
kaṭavuḷ civaliṅka vaṭivilum vaḻipaṭappaṭṭāreṉpatu arappā mokañcatarō eṉṉum iṭaṅkaḷiṟ kiṭitta avvakip poruḷkaḷ palavaṟṟāl naṉku viḷaṅkukiṉṟatu. iliṅkam uyarattil uḷḷa cūriyaṉākak karutappaṭṭatu eṉpatik kuṟikkum paṭṭiyaṅkaḷum kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa.
cumēriya makkaḷ āṇ ammā eṉlil eṉṉum mummūrttikaḷi vaḻipaṭṭārkaḷ. tāyk kaṭavuḷiṉ vaṭivaṅkaḷ pala, mokañcotarō arappā eṉṉum iṭaṅkaḷiṟ kāṇappaṭṭaṉa. arappāp paṭṭiyaṅ kaḷil, ammaṉi mīṉ kaṇṇi eṉak kuṟikkiṉṟaṉa. “uyar eltēr ōr ammaṉ” eṉap poṟikkappaṭṭa paṭṭiyattiṟ kāṇappaṭum kaṭavuḷ vaṭiviṉ, pāti (iṭappuṟam) āṇ vaṭivākavum, pāti (valap puṟam) peṇ vaṭivākavum kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. ivvakiyāṉa kaṭavuḷ cumēriyāvilum ammā (amma) eṉṉum peyaruṭaṉ kāṇappaṭukiṉṟatu. ik kaṭavuḷic civar arttanārīcurar eṉak kūṟuvar.
oru cācaṉattil ōriṭattil māttiram kaṭavuḷ pāmpu vaṭiviṉarākak kūṟappaṭṭuḷḷār. “mīṉavar mūṉṟu kaṇṇuḷḷa pāmpit tiyāṉikkiṉ ṟārkaḷ” eṉa oru paṭṭiyam kūṟukiṉṟatu. itippōlavē iṉ ṉoru paṭṭiyam, kikkōṭari (maḻu) yip paṟṟik kuṟippiṭukiṉṟatu. maṟiyaṟ paṭuttappaṭṭa mīṉavar periya kaṭavuḷiṉ mūṉṟu kaṇkaḷit tiyāṉikkiṉṟārkaḷ eṉa oru paṭṭiyam kūṟukiṉṟatu.
mokañcatarō makkaḷ nāṭṭukku aracaṉ kaṭavuḷ eṉṟum, avar cārpil aracaṉ āḷkiṉṟāṉ eṉṟum nampiṉārkaḷ. mokañ catarō naṇṭūr eṉappaṭṭatu aracaṉ naṇṭūr uḻavaṉ allatu naṇṭil uḻavaṉ eṉappaṭṭāṉ. aracaṉ pūcāriyākavum iruntāṉ. itu, “mīṉaṉīr māṟu aṭu aiyaṉ ceṟital tal ellā” eṉṉum paṭṭiyat tāl viḷaṅkukiṉṟatu. itaṉ poruḷ “mīṉavariṉ pakik kuriyavaṉ ciṟippaṭuttappaṭṭa aracaṉākiya pūcāri” eṉpatākum.
ñāyiṟṟiṉ kōyilkaḷ caturavaṭivākak kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. ataṟku muṉṉāl tiṟanta talivāyil iruntatu. ñāyiṟṟik kuṟikkum vaṭṭa vaṭivam kaṭṭiliṉ mītu vikkappaṭṭirukkiṟatu.
iṅkuk kūṟappaṭṭavikaḷāl 5000 āṇṭukaḷukku muṉṉum, makkaḷiṉ vaḻipāṭu iṉṟiya vaḻipāṭṭi ottiruntateṉṟē teri kiṉṟatu. ak kālattilēyē makkaḷ maṉatti oruvaḻippaṭuttic ceyyap paṭuvatākiya yōkattip paṟṟi aṟintiruntārkaḷ.
acurar eṉa āriyarāl vaḻaṅkappaṭṭa makkaḷ, civaṉi nōkkik kaṭiya tavaṅkaḷip purintu periya varaṅkaḷip peṟṟārkaḷ eṉap purāṇaṅkaḷil kūṟappaṭum paḻaṅkatikaḷ, tamiḻar maṉati oru vaḻippaṭuttic ceyyappaṭum yōkattiṉāl periya āṟṟalip peṟṟu viḷaṅkiṉārkaḷ eṉṉum uṇmiyi viḷakkuvaṉavē. kiṟistunātar, puttar, makāvīrar, mukamatu mutaliyōr taṉimiyiliruntu cintiyi oṭukkit tavañ ceytamiyiṉālēyē ñāṉattip peṟṟu, maṟṟavarkaḷ īṭēṟum vaḻiyik kāṭṭiṉārkaḷ eṉa ulakam nampivarukiṉṟatu.
1caṅka kālattil tamiḻar vaḻipāṭu
caṅka kālam eṉpatu iṟṟikku iraṇṭāyiram āṇṭukaḷiṉ muṉ, caṅka ilakkiyaṅkaḷil tamiḻar vaḻipāṭu evvāṟu iruntateṉṟu naṉku kūṟappaṭṭuḷḷatu. makkaḷiṉ vāḻkki muṉṉēṟṟam avaravar vāḻum iṭaṅkaḷukkēṟṟavāṟiruntatu. ataṟkēṟpavē avarkaḷiṉ vaḻipāṭukaḷum iruntaṉa.
caṅka kāla nūlkaḷ nāṭṭi, mali, kāṭu, vayal, kaṭaṟkari, maṇal veḷi eṉa aivakiyākak kūṟukiṉṟaṉa. ovvoru nilattum vāḻum makkaḷ, uṇavu tēṭum poruṭṭuk koṇṭa toḻilkaḷ vevvēṟu vakiyiṉa. avikaḷukkēṟpa avarkaḷ vāḻkkiyum iruntatu.
muruka vaṇakkam
mali nāṭṭil vāḻnta makkaḷ murukakkaṭavuḷit tamatu kula teyvamākak koṇṭiruntaṉar. muruka vaṇakkam eṉpatu ñāyiṟṟu vaṇakkattiṉ iṉṉoruvaki. kāṭukiḻāḷ allatu turkkiyē muṟkālattil pōrk kaṭavuḷāka iruntāḷ. piṉpu murukaṉ pōrk kaṭavuḷākak koḷḷappaṭṭār. kaṭaliṭattē kāliyiṟṟōṉṟum iḷañāyiṟu, mayilmītu eḻum iḷaṅ kaṭavuḷākak koḷḷappaṭṭatu. pālastiṉ nāṭṭu makkaḷum ñāyiṟṟi mutiya pakal (old baal) eṉṟum iḷiya pakal (young baal) eṉa iruvakiyil vaḻipaṭṭārkaḷ. ivviḷam pakaliyē kirēkkar “mārs” eṉṉum pōrk kaṭavuḷākak koṇṭaṉar. malikaḷil vāḻum makkaḷ murukaṉiṉ vaṭivāka vēli naṭṭum, kaṭappa maratti alaṅkarittum, maṟiyaṟittup pali tūvi vaḻipaṭṭārkaḷ. tiruccentūr, tirupparaṅkuṉṟam mutaliya iṭaṅkaḷil ālayaṅkaḷil makkaḷ pūvum pukiyum kiyuṟikaḷum koṭuttut tām eṇṇum eṇṇaṅkaḷ palikkavēṇṭumeṉa murukak kaṭavuḷi niṉintu vaḻi paṭṭaṉar. ālayaṅkaḷil periya viḻākkaḷ naṭipeṟṟaṉa. 
tirumāl vaṇakkam
mulli nilam allatu kāṭu cārnta iṭaṅkaḷil vāḻnta makkaḷ tirumāli vaḻipaṭṭaṉar. māl ñāyiṟṟuk kaṭavuḷiṉ iṉṉoruvaki. māl eṉpatu periya el (mā+el) eṉṉum poruḷ tarum peyar. el eṉpatu al āyiṟṟu. ik kaṭavuḷ muṉpu tāyk kaṭavuḷākak koṇṭu vaḻipaṭappaṭṭatākavum, piṉpu tantik kaṭavuḷākak koḷḷappaṭṭa teṉṟum karuta iṭamuṇṭu. “ariyalāṟ ṟēviyilli aiyāṟaṉārkkē” eṉat tēvārattil varutalum kāṇka. pāratap pōrukkup piṉ kiruṭṭiṇa vaṇakkamum tirumāl vaṇakkamum oṉṟākak koḷḷappaṭa lāyiṉa. tirumāliṉ kiyilirukkum cakkaram ñāyiṟṟik kuṟippatu. ulaki mūvaṭikaḷāl aḷantār eṉac collappaṭuvatiluḷḷa tirumāl ñāyiṟu. avariṉ mūṉṟu aṭikaḷ, utayam, ucci, cāyvu eṉṉum mūṉṟu iṭaṅkaḷil cellum celavukaḷ ākum. ivvāṟē tirumāl mūvaṭika ḷāl ulaki aḷantār eṉṉum katikkup poruḷ urikkappaṭu kiṉṟatu.
mulli nilattu āyar, tirumālukkup pāṟpoṅkal poṅkip paṭittu vaḻipaṭuvar, iṭicciyar kikōrttu niṉṟu kuravik kūttāṭuvar. tirumālukku uyirp palikaḷ iṭappaṭṭatākac caṅka nūlkaḷil kāṇappaṭavilli. ‘tiruvaṉantapurattilum, tiruveḵkāvi lum tirumāl kōyilkaḷ mikac ciṟappuṟṟu viḷaṅkiṉa. tiruvaṉantapuratti luḷḷa tirumāl kōyilil makkaḷ ceṉṟu vaḻipaṭum iyalpu patiṟṟup pattu eṉṉum nūliṟ kāṇappaṭukiṉṟatu. tam viṇ eṉpatu viṣṇu vāyiṟṟu eṉa ārāycciyāḷar aṟivar.
vēntaṉ vaṇakkam
marutam allatu vayal cārnta iṭaṅkaḷil vāḻntōr, intiraṉi vaḻipaṭṭārkaḷ. intiraṉ eṉpatu iṟivaṉ eṉpataṉ tiripākalām. muṟkāla makkaḷ maḻi peytaṟkum, ulakam ceḻippataṟkum aracaṉē kāraṇam eṉak karutiṉārkaḷ. ākavē avarkaḷ aracaṉiyē teyvamākak koṇṭu vaḻipaṭṭārkaḷ. ulaka varalāṟṟil itu putumi yaṉṟu. muṉṉōriṭattil araca vaṇakkam tōṉṟiyataṟkup piṟitōr kāraṇamum kūṟiṉōm. aracaṉāl maḻi peykiṉṟatu eṉṉum karuttik koṇṭē, intiraṉ mukili vākaṉamāka uṭiyavaṉ eṉṉum aitīkam uṇṭāyittal vēṇṭum. intiya nāṭṭi aṭinta āriya makkaḷum tām vantaṭinta nāṭṭil makkaḷ iṟivaṉi vaḻipaṭutalik kaṇṭu tāmum avvāṟu ceytaṉarākalām. avarkaḷ iṟivaṉiyē intiraṉ eṉat tirittum vaḻaṅkiṉārkaḷākalām. piṟkālattil it teyvam tikkuppālakaril oṉṟākak koḷḷap paṭṭatu. vayali aṭuttē periya paṭṭiṉaṅkaḷum aracaṉ talinakarum iruntaṉa. vitippuk kālat toṭakkattilum, aṟuppuk kālattiṉ piṉpum, intiraṉukkup periya viḻākkaḷ eṭukkappaṭṭaṉa. ak kālaṅ kaḷil ālayattil āṭal pāṭal pōṉṟa palavakip poḻutu pōkkukaḷ naṭipeṟṟaṉa. intiraṉiṉ vaṭivam irumput taṇṭā yutattip piṭittu niṟpavaṉāka amikkappaṭṭiruntatu.
kaṭaṟkarikaḷil vāḻntavarkaḷiṉ kula teyvam varuṇaṉ. varuṇaṉ acuraṉ eṉa vaṭamoḻi vētaṅkaḷil kūṟappaṭuvatāl, ak kaṭavuḷ tamiḻar kaṭavuḷē eṉa ārāycciyāḷar muṭivu ceytirukkiṉṟa ṉar. tamiḻariṉ varuṇaṉ eṉṉum kaṭavuḷiyē āriyamakkaḷum vaḻi paṭṭaṉar. varuṇaṉ ātittaruḷ oruvaṉ eṉappaṭukiṉṟamiyāl, ñāyiṟṟik kuṟikkum aruṇaṉē varuṇaṉāyiṟṟu eṉak karuta iṭa muṇṭu. varuṇaṉukkup periya kōyilkaḷ iruntaṉaveṉṟu teriya villi. kaṭaṟkarikaḷil vāḻum mīṉ piṭippōr, pūraṇik kālaṅ kaḷil tāḻikaḷiṉ kīḻ cuṟāk kompukaḷi naṭṭu malarkaḷit tūvi varuṇaṉi vaḻipaṭṭārkaḷ.
kāḷi vaṇakkam
pāli nilaṅkaḷ allatu veyyilāl pul pūṇṭukaḷ karintu pōṉa kāṭṭu, mali otukkukaḷil vēṭṭiyāṭi vāḻum piṟpōk kuṭiya makkaḷ vāḻntārkaḷ. ivarkaḷ uyirp paliyiṭṭuk kāḷiyi vaḻipaṭṭārkaḷ. ik kāḷi vaḻipāṭṭip paṟṟip paraṇi nūlkaḷ naṉku virittuk kūṟukiṉṟaṉa.
kiruṭṭiṇa, palatēva vaḻipāṭukaḷum maruta nilaṅkaḷilum mulli nilaṅkaḷilum iruntuvantaṉa. iṉṉum vīra, vaṇakkaṅkaḷum pala ciṟu teyva vaṇakkaṅkaḷum iruntu vantaṉa.
civa vaṇakkam
tolkāppiyattil muṟkūṟiya aimperun teyvaṅkaḷiṉ vaḻi pāṭukaḷē kūṟappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. civa vaḻipāṭu kūṟappaṭavilli. ātaliṉ tolkāppiyar kālattil civavaḻipāṭu tōṉṟavilli eṉac cilar kūṟuvar. tolkāppiya kālam ki.mu. 350 variyil eṉṟu kūṟiyuḷ ḷōm. ataṟku mika muṟpaṭṭa kālattilēyē civa vaḻipāṭu tōṉṟi yiruntatu. aintu nilaṅkaḷil vāḻum makkaḷum tattam kula teyvaṅ kaḷākak koṇṭu vaḻipaṭṭa teyvaṅkaḷip paṟṟiyē tolkāppiyar kūṟiyuḷḷār. āṉāl ellā makkaḷum civaṉiyē kula teyvaṅ kaḷukkum mēlāṉa perun teyvamākak koṇṭu vaḻipaṭṭārkaḷ. itu tamiḻ nāṭṭavar māttiram koṇṭa muṟiyaṉṟu; ulaka makkaḷ ellōrum koṇṭa muṟiyākum. tolkāppiyar kālattil pārppaṉarē kōyili mēṟpārttaṉar. ak kālattil pārppaṉar pirāmaṇa camayattik kik koḷḷavilli. tolkāppiyattil “aṟuvakippaṭṭa pārppaṉap pakkamum” eṉak kūṟappaṭṭatu. kōyiṟ paṇiviṭikaḷip pārkkum uyarnta pārppāṉ mutal, paṭippaṭiyē tāḻnta pārppaṉarēyākum. pārppaṉar pirāmaṇa matattik kik koṇṭapōtu ālayaṅkaḷil āriyam pāṭiṉar; ataṉi veṟuttut tamiḻ makkaḷ kaṇṭittirukkiṉṟaṉar. iṉṟu ālayaṅkaḷil pirāmaṇap pārppāṉ āriyam ōtikkoṇṭu veḷiyē niṟkum paṇṭārattit tamiḻ pāṭac ceykiṉṟāṉ. itu tamiḻip peritum iḻivu paṭuttuvatākum.
uṇmi ñāṉam
