tattuva ñāṉam mikap paḻaṅkālam mutal kurumāṇākka muṟiyil upatēcikkappaṭṭu vantatu. atu irakaciyam allatu upatēcam eṉappaṭṭatu. vīṭu pēṟṟukkuriya ñāṉaṅkaḷi eḻuti vippatu tamiḻ marapaṉṟu. iṟivaṉ teṉmukak kaṭavuḷāka amarntu muṉivarkaḷukku ñāṉatti muṉamākaviruntu upatēcittār eṉac collappaṭu kiṟatu. vīṭṭu nūlkaḷ eḻuti vikkappaṭuvatilli eṉpatit tol kāppiyam kuṟippiṭukiṉṟatu. parimēlaḻakar, nacciṉārkkiṉiyar mutaliya uriyāciriyarkaḷum itaṉik kuṟippiṭṭirukkiṉṟaṉar. kuru māṇākka muṟiyil vanta tattuvañāṉa nūlkaḷ vaṭa nāṭṭil upaniṭataṅkaḷ eṉa vaḻaṅkiṉa. upaniṭataṅkaḷiṟ collappaṭum tattuva ñāṉattukkum ākamaṅkaḷiṟ collappaṭum tattuva ñāṉattukkum neruṅkiya oṟṟumiyuṇṭu eṉa aṟiñar kūṟuvar. ākama ñāṉak karuttukkaḷ tamiḻa riṭiyē mikap paḻaṅkālam mutal iruntu varuvaṉa. upaniṭata ñāṉaṅ kaḷi aṭiniliyākak koṇṭu cāṅkiyam, puttam, yōkam, camaṇam mutaliya tattuva ñāṉaṅkaḷ eḻuntaṉa. kapilar, puttar, makāvīrar mutaliyōr tirāviṭamarapic cērntavarkaḷeṉpatu ārāycciyāḷar karuttu. upaniṭatak karuttukkaḷit teḷivuppaṭuttuvataṟku vētānta cūttiraṅkaḷ ceyyappaṭṭaṉa. piṟkālattavar iccūttiraṅkaḷukkut tattam koḷkikaḷip pukutti uri kaṇṭaṉar. puttam camaṇam mutaliya tattuva ñāṉaṅkaḷ vaṭakkiṉiṉṟum teṟku nōkkip paravik koṇṭiruntaṉa. ataṉāl teṟkil paraviyirunta tattuva ñāṉak karuttukkaḷil taṭumāṟṟaṅkaḷ eḻuntaṉa. ak kālattil tirumūlar, tamiḻar tattuva ñāṉak karuttukkaḷi viḷakkit tirumantiram eṉṉum ñāṉa nūlic ceytār: camayakuravarkaḷum, āḻvārkaḷum tamiḻaratu tattuva ñāṉak karuttukkaḷit tamatu pāṭalkaḷil iṭiiṭiyē eṭuttuk kūṟiyirukkiṉṟaṉar. caṅkarāccāriyār vētānta cūttiraṅkaḷukku uri ceytār. avar tamatu uriyil kaṭavuḷ oṉṟē uḷporuḷ; maṟṟavi poyt tōṟṟaṅkaḷ eṉak kūṟiṉār. ikkoḷki kaṭavuḷ, uyir, ulakam eṉṉum mupporuḷkaḷi uḷ poruḷkaḷeṉavum, iṟivaṉiyum, uyiriyum āṇṭāṉ aṭimi eṉavum koḷḷum tamiḻar ñāṉamākiya civa cintāntak koḷkikku muraṇāka viruntatu. ākavē meykaṇṭār, umāpati civam, aruṇanti civāccāriyār mutaliya aṟiñar civa cittānta ñāṉaṅkaḷi viḷakkit tamiḻil nūlkaḷ ceytaṉar. civa cittāntak karuttukkaḷ tōttira vaṭivāṉa civat tirumuṟikaḷilum, nālāyirap pirapantattilum iṭiyiṭiyē kūṟappaṭṭuḷḷaṉa.
52. kalvi
marattaṭi, kōyiliṉ patti allatu āciriyaṉiṉ vīṭṭut tiṇṇi eṉpavi paḷḷikaḷāka iruntaṉa. kalvi aintu vayatil toṭaṅkiyatu. nāṭṭuppuṟaṅkaḷil kāṇappaṭuvatu pōlac ciṟuvar maṇalil eḻutteḻutap payiṉṟārkaḷ. āciriyaṉiṉ mutal māṇavaṉ māṇavarukkuk kalvi payiṟṟuvatil utaviyāka iruntāṉ. oru māṇavaṉ colla maṟṟa māṇavarkaḷ kēṭṭuc collum muṟiyil neṭuṅ kaṇakkup payilappaṭṭatu. māṇavar āciriyaṉukkup paṇivum mariyāti yum kāṭṭiṉar. “eḻuttaṟi vittavaṉ iṟivaṉāvāṉ” eṉpatu tamiḻ nāṭṭup paḻamoḻi. māṇavar pāṭaṅkaḷip paṉi ōli ēṭukaḷil eḻutip payiṉṟārkaḷ. eḻutuvataṟkup paṉi ōliyum eḻuttāṇiyum payaṉpaṭuttappaṭṭaṉa. paḻaṅkālac cācaṉaṅkaḷ akkālattil eḻuttu muṟiyāṉa kalvi evvaḷavu tiruttam peṟṟiruntateṉpatik kāṭṭu kiṉṟaṉa. kōvilkaḷilum, marattaṭikaḷilum allāmal camaṇa maṭaṅkaḷi lum, putta vikārikaḷilum māṇavar kalvi payiṉṟārkaḷ. kalvi kaṟpikkappaṭum iṭaṅkaḷukkup paḷḷi eṉṉum peyar vaḻaṅku kiṉṟatu. itu putta matam campantappaṭṭa peyar. paḷḷiyil māṇavar eppaṭi naṭantukoḷḷa vēṇṭumeṉpatip paṟṟi naṉṉūl kūṟukiṉ ṟatu. māṇavar āciriyarukku ūtiyamāka vayalkaḷil viḷiyum poruḷ kaḷi āṇṭil oru muṟi allatu pala muṟikaḷil koṭuttārkaḷ. piṟkālattil ūr āciriyaṉukku ūtiyamāka māṉiyaṅkaḷ viṭappaṭ ṭiruntaṉa. kōyilkaḷil tutippāṭalkaḷ pāṭuvataṟku māṇavar payiṟṟap paṭṭārkaḷ. maṭaṅkaḷ tōṉṟiyapōtu maṭaṅkaḷum kalvic cāli kaḷāka viḷaṅkiṉa.
uyarnta kalvi kaṟka virumpiṉōr nāṭṭil āṅkāṅku pukaḻ peṟṟu viḷaṅkiya āciriyarkaḷi aṭintu avarkaḷuṭaṉ taṅkiyiruntu kalvi payiṉṟārkaḷ. āciriyarkaḷ māṇavarukku eḷitil kalvi payiṟ ṟaṟku utaviyākap putiya nūlkaḷic ceyvatum vaḻakkamāka iruntatu. patiṉeṇ kīḻkkaṇakku nūlkaḷ perumpālum paḷḷikaḷil kalvi payilum māṇavarukkākac ceyyappaṭṭavi. āciriyaṉuṭaṉ taṅki yiruntu kalvi payilum māṇavar avaṉuṭiya vīṭṭup paṇikaḷic ceytu avaṉukku utaviyāka iruntaṉar. araca kumārar āṭcikkuriya kalviyiyum, pōrk kalviyiyum vevvēṟu āciriyarkaḷiṭam payiṉṟārkaḷ. muṟkāla māṇavar ilakkiyaṅkaḷiyum, ilakkaṇaṅ kaḷiyum māttiramallāmal ici, kūttu, ōviyam pōṉṟa pala vakik kalvikaḷiyum payiṉṟaṉar. aracar, araciyar mutalāṉōr ici, naṭaṉam mutaliyavaṟṟil ciṟantu viḷaṅkiṉārkaḷ eṉa ilakkiyaṅkaḷ kūṟukiṉṟaṉa. peṇkaḷil cila vakuppiṉar aṟupattu nāṉku vakik kalvi payiṉṟaṉar. avi “eṇṇeṉ kali” allatu aṟupattu nāṉku kalikaḷ eṉappaṭṭaṉa. kittoḻil paṟṟiya kalikaḷ taṉittaṉi vakuppiṉariṭiyē eḻutākkaliyāka iruntu vantaṉa.
toḻil campantappaṭṭa kalvi payilvōr avvat toḻilil tiṟami peṟṟavarkaḷiṭam payiṉṟārkaḷ. perumpālum tantiyē taṉatu makaṉukkut toḻiṟkalvi kaṟpittāṉ.
53. kittoḻilkaḷ
“necavu kuṭicit toḻilāka iruntatu. necavu vēli ceyvōr perumpālum peṇkaḷāka iruntārkaḷ. kampaḷi, pañcu, marappaṭṭi, caṇal, ilavam pañcu mutaliyavaṟṟil nūṟkappaṭṭa nūlāl tuṇikaḷ neyyappaṭṭaṉa. palavakic caṇal nār, paṭṭu, irali māṉ mayir eṉpavaṟṟiliruntum āṭikaḷ ceyyappaṭṭaṉa. kayiṟukaḷ, kavacaṅkaḷ, vārkaḷ ceyvōrum iruntaṉar. 
“taccar, kammiyar, kuyavar, matuvaṭippōr, vāttiyakkārar, kūttar mutaliya pala toḻil purivōriruntaṉar. vaṇṭikaḷ, tērkaḷ pōṉṟa vaṟṟic taccar ceytaṉar. poṟkollar mukkiya toḻilāḷarāka iruntārkaḷ. irāca nikaṇṭu eṉṉum vaṭa moḻi nūl 42 vakip poṉṉip paṟṟik kūṟukiṉṟatu. āparaṇaṅkaḷum nāṇayaṅkaḷ cilavum poṉṉāṟ ceyyappaṭṭaṉa. poṉṉōṭu vēṟu ulōkaṅkaḷik kalantu vēli ceytal, mulām pūcutal, poṉṉil irattiṉak kaṟ kaḷip patittal, uri kallik koṇṭu poṉṉic cōtittal mutaliyaṉa aṟiyappaṭṭiruntaṉa. irumpu, cempu, īyam, takaram mutaliyavi kīḻāṉa ulōkaṅkaḷākak koḷḷappaṭṭaṉa. tilliyil cantirakupta ṉāl (ki.pi. 5ām nū.) nāṭṭappaṭṭa irumputtūṇ, akkālattil ulōkaṅkaḷi urukkivārkkum toḻil naṉku aṟiyappaṭṭiruntatu eṉpatit terivikkiṉṟatu. potuvāka vīṭṭil payaṉpaṭuttum poruḷkaḷ marattiṉāl ceyyappaṭṭaṉa. paḻiya vākaṭaṅkaḷil pātaracam kūṟappaṭavilli. atu kuṭaliyar kālattilum aṟiyappaṭa villi. cucurutar kālattil atu aṟiyappaṭṭiruntatu. nilakkīl, maliyilirukkum nāṉku ulōkaṅkaḷi veyil cūṭēṟac ceyvatāl vaṭiyum kaḷimpu eṉak karutappaṭṭatu. muttu, pavaḻam, irattiṉakkaṟkaḷ eṉpaṉa mikap paḻaṅkālam mutal aṟiyappaṭṭiruntaṉa. viraṅkaḷ veṭṭic cāṇi piṭittuc cuttañ ceyyappaṭṭaṉa. pōli irattiṉak kaṟkaḷum, iracak kalaviyik koṇṭu ceyyappaṭum pōli muttuk kaḷum aṟiyappaṭṭiruntaṉa”.1
ulōka vēli ceyvōr akkacāliyar, kammāḷar, aṟivar, ōvar, kaṇṇāḷar, kaṇviṉiñar, kammiyar, kollar, karumār, taṭṭār, tuvaṭṭar, pulavar, puṉiyar, vittakar, vittiyar mutaliya peyar kaḷāl aṟiyappaṭṭaṉar. ulōkat tuṇṭi aṭittuc ceyta takaṭu aṭar eṉappaṭṭatu. aṭariṉāl periya ēṉaṅkaḷ ceyyappaṭṭaṉa. caṅkukaḷ aṟuttu vaḷikaḷākac ceyyappaṭṭaṉa. irattiṉak kaṟkaḷil tuḷiyiṭuvōr eṉa aṟiyappaṭṭaṉar.
ovvoru kūṭṭattiṉarum paramparit toḻiliyē ceytu vantārkaḷ. toḻilkaḷil māṟṟamuṇṭākavilli. kūttar, mēḷamaṭip pōr, caṅku ūtuvōr, kampaṅ kūttāṭikaḷ, yāṉi paḻakkuvōr eṉpavarkaḷip paṟṟi nūlkaḷ kuṟippiṭukiṉṟaṉa. maṉitarukkum vilaṅku kaḷukkum vittiyam ceyyum maruttuvarum iruntaṉar.
54. āparaṇa alaṅkāraṅkaḷ
āṭavarum makaḷirum palavaki āparaṇaṅkaḷāl tammi alaṅ karittārkaḷ. avarkaḷ tammi alaṅkarittu koṇṭatallāmal tām payaṉpaṭuttum ellāp poruḷkaḷiyum alaṅkarittārkaḷ. vīṭu kaḷiṉ katavukaḷ, nilikaḷ, muṟṟaṅkaḷ eṉpaṉavum pala vēlippāṭu kaḷāl alaṅkarikkappaṭṭaṉa. katti, vāḷ pōṉvaṟṟiṉ piṭikaḷum palavāṟu alaṅkarikkappaṭṭiruntaṉa. makaḷir muṟṟattilum, vīṭṭu vāyililum viyakkattakka aḻakiya kōlaṅkaḷi iṭṭārkaḷ. vīṭṭiṉ cuvarkaḷilum kōyil cuvarkaḷilum maṉattiyum kaṇṇiyum kavarum aḻakiya ōviyaṅkaḷ eḻutappaṭṭiruntaṉa. kōyil kaṭṭaṭaṅkaḷilum tērkaḷilum aḻakiya ciṟpaṅkaḷ kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa.
maṇamākāta makaḷir tamatu kūntali aintu vakiyākak kōti muṭittārkaḷ. peṇkaḷ neṟṟiyil tilakamiṭṭārkaḷ; taliyil pala vakip pūkkaḷic cūṭiṉārkaḷ; cuṟāmīṉ, valampuric caṅku, piṟi pōṉṟa aṇikalaṉkaḷi aṇintārkaḷ; koṇṭiyilum kaḻutti lum pū mālikaḷ aṇintārkaḷ; cantaṉam kuṅkumam mutaliya niṟap poṭikaḷip payaṉpaṭutti mēṉiyi alaṅkarittārkaḷ; utaṭukaḷukku arakkiṉāl ceyyappaṭṭa cāyam ūṭṭiṉārkaḷ, mārpilum tōḷi lum toyyileṉṉum oruvakik kuḻampu pūciṉārkaḷ; ataṉ mītu karumpu, pūṅkoṭi eṉpavaṟṟi aḻakupeṟa eḻutiṉārkaḷ; kātil tōṭu aṇintārkaḷ; kālil cilampum, ki viralil mōtiramum ariyil mēkaliyum aṇintārkaḷ. āṭavarum kuḻi, kaṭakam, taṇṭi mutaliya palavaki aṇikaḷi aṇintārkaḷ. peṇkaḷ aṇinta aṇikaḷ mikap pala. caṅka ilakkiyaṅkaḷilum piṟkāla ilak kiyaṅkaḷilum palavaki aṇivakikaḷ kūṟappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. aṇital aḻaku ceytali uṇartta ār, cūṭu, puṉi, pūṇ, milivēy, mutaliya pala coṟkaḷ kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. paḻiya ciṟpaṅkaḷil muṟkāla āṭavar makaḷir aṇinta aṇivakikaḷ kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa.
piṟkālattum muṟkālattum vaḻaṅkiya aṇivakikaḷuḷ cila piṉ varuvaṉa: tōṭu, kārōli, muttumāli, pavaḻa māli, caṅkili, kuṟaṅku ceṟi, paṭṭiki, cataṅki, kiṇkiṇi, cilampu, kaḻal, vaḷi, mōtiram, mēkali, tiruppatam, tirumuṭi, paḷḷit toṅkal, koṟṟakkuṭi, tavaḷa cattiram, poṟpū, tiraḷmaṇi vaṭam, kāṟi, aṭikkāṟi, aṉṉam, kiḷi, cōṉakac ciṭukku, cōṉakac ciṭukkiṉ kūṭu, makuṭam, vāḷi, vaṭukavāḷi, kaṇmalar (nayaṉam), poṭṭu, patakkam, ēkavali, kālvaṭam, kamalam, vāku valayam, tuṭar, tiruppaṭṭi, tirumaṇi vaṭam, kikkāṟi (puyavaḷi), pātacālam, pattiram, kaṇṭatuṭar (māli), kokkuvāy (kaḻuttu āparaṇaṅkaḷi ellām cērttup piṭikkumpaṭi aṇiyum caṅkili), kaṭṭakam (pavaḷam patitta kivaḷi), irattiṉa vaḷiyal, ciṟu cantam, pācamāli, captacāri, patakkam, kalāvam (patakkattiṉ pakuti), pirapi, kamalam, ceṭi, carappaḷḷi, teyvavutti, valampuric caṅku, pūppāḷi, teṉpalli, kaṭukkaṉ, kaṭakam, caṉṉavīram, utarapantam.
55. poḻutupōkku
aracar perumpālum vēṭṭiyāṭuvatilum āyutappayiṟci pōrp payiṟcikaḷilum poḻutu pōkkiṉar; yāṉi ēṟṟam kutiri ēṟṟam eṉpaṉavum avarkaḷiṉ poḻutupōkkāka iruntaṉa. pōr vīrar maṟpōr, kuttuc caṇṭi, cilampam, vāṭpōr, viṟpōr mutaliyaṉa purintu poḻutu pōkkiṉar. makaḷir ammāṉi, pantu, kaḻaṅku mutaliya viḷiyāṭṭukaḷilum, teḷḷēṇam, cāḻal, kōlāṭ ṭam, kuravi, kummi mutaliya āṭalkaḷilum yāḻ vācittal pāṭutal mutaliyavaṟṟilum poḻutupōkkiṉar. potu makkaḷ kāṭip pōr, kutārip pōr, āṭṭup pōr, yāiṉi ōṭṭam, kutiri ōṭṭam, tērōṭṭam, nāṭṭuk kūttu, kaḻik kūttu eṉpavaṟṟip pārttup poḻutu pōkkiṉar. ciṟuvarum ciṟumiyarum ciṟu tērōṭṭiyum, ciṟu paṟi aṟintum, ciṟṟil puṉintum, ūcalāṭiyum, vil koṇṭu ampu eytum poḻutu pōkkiṉar. ūcalāṭutal vaḷarntavarkaḷiṉ poḻutupōkkākavum iruntatatu. āyarkula vālipar ēṟu taḻuvip poḻutu pōkkiṉar. ēṟu taḻuvutal eṉpatu callikkaṭṭu eṉpatu pōṉṟatu. mutiyōr tāyam āṭiṉar.
viḻākkaḷ, uṇṭāṭṭukaḷ, kaḷiyāṭṭukaḷ, eṉpaṉavum ciṟanta poḻutu pōkkukaḷāka iruntaṉa. peṇkaḷ cellum tēriyum yāṉiyiyum peṇkaḷ ōṭṭic celvatum akkāla vaḻakkāka iruntatu. āṟṟil putu veḷḷam varum pōtu nīrāṭṭu viḻā eṭukkap paṭṭatu. appoḻutu āṭavarum makaḷirum tērkaḷ, vaṇṭikaḷ, yāṉikaḷi ūrntu ceṉṟu palavaki āṭamparaṅkaḷōṭu nīrāṭuvar; āṟṟaṅkarikaḷil iṭappaṭṭuḷḷa kūṭāraṅkaḷuḷ taṅkum pōtu matuvuṇṭum, naṟum paṇṭaṅkaḷic cuvittum, āṭiyum pāṭiyum kaḷippar. kārttiki viḻāvil vīṭṭukku viḷakkēṟṟap paṭṭatu. timātap piṟappil makaḷir viṭiyaṟ kāliyil nīrāṭi viratamiruntaṉar.
ciṟuvar nellikkāyi vittu vaṭṭāṭutal, kiṇaṟṟuḷ kutittu nīr aṭiyilirukkum kalli eṭuttu varutal pōṉṟa poḻutu pōkkukaḷ ilakkiyaṅkaḷil kūṟappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. viḻāk kālaṅkaḷil pulavarkaḷ paṭṭi maṇṭapattilēṟit tattam pulamiyik kāṭṭum coṟpoḻivāṟṟiṉar. vicaya nakara aracar kālattil araṇmaṉikkuḷ poḻutupōkku araṅku iruntatu. aracaṉatum araṇmaṉiyiluḷḷa varkaḷatum poḻutupōkkukkāka vilaṅkukaḷ pōr ceyyumpaṭi viṭappaṭṭaṉa; maṟpōr naṭattappaṭṭaṉa. maṟpōril peṇkaḷum kalantu koṇṭārkaḷ.
56. ici
ovvoru nilattukkum uriya icikaḷiruntaṉa. kuṟiñci nila makkaḷ kuṟiñcip paṇpāṭiṉārkaḷ1. mulli nila makkaḷ mullip paṇ pāṭiṉārkaḷ. aḵtu iṉṟu mattiyamāvati eṉa aṟiyappaṭukiṉ ṟatu. marutanila makkaḷ marutap paṇ pāṭiṉārkaḷ. atu iṉṟu kētāram eṉa aṟiyap paṭukiṉṟatu. neytal nilattukkuriya paṇ iṉṟu puṉṉākava rāḷi eṉa aṟiyappaṭukiṉṟatu. pāṭi āṭumpōtu koṭṭappaṭum mēḷaṅkaḷ iruntaṉa. vevvēṟu ōcikaḷi eḻuppum paṟikaḷ vevvēṟu ceyal puriyum kālaṅkaḷil koṭṭappaṭṭaṉa. niri kavarumpōtu koṭṭappaṭuvatu ēṟu kōṭ paṟi. veṟiyāṭumpōtu olikkappaṭum paṟi murukiyam. maṇak kālattil muḻakkappaṭuvatu maṇamuḻavu. tēriḻukkum pōtu koṭṭappaṭuvatu tērōṭṭup paṟi. nellaṟukkum pōtu aṟiyil pāṭuvatu nellarikiṇi. aracaṉ veḷiyē puṟappaṭum pōtu taṭṭappaṭuvatu puṟappāṭṭup paṟi. mīṉ piṭikkac cellumpōtu koṭṭappaṭuvatu mīṉ kōṭ paṟi. cūṟiyāṭum pōtu koṭṭappaṭuvatu cūṟi kōṭpaṟi.
pōrkkālattu yāṉi kutiri kālāṭ paṭikaḷukku ūkka mūṭṭum poruṭṭup palvaki vāttiyaṅkaḷ olikkappaṭṭaṉa. avi iyam, icik karuvi, vāttiyam, vācciyam eṉappaṭṭaṉa. ivi tōṟ karuvi, tuḷik karuvi, narampuk karuvi, kañcak karuvi eṉa nālvakip paṭṭaṉa. tamiḻukkuriya ēḻicikaḷ kural, tuttam, kikkiḷi, uḻi, iḷi, viḷari, tāram eṉpaṉa. ivikkuriya eḻuttukkaḷ ā mutaliya neṭil ēḻum. ca, ri, ka, ma, pa, ta, ni eṉṉum eḻuttukkaḷ piṟkālattil vaḻakkukku vantaṉa. mūṅkil, koṉṟip paḻattaṉi kōtu, āmpaṟ ṟaṇṭu, maram mutaliyavaṟṟil ceyyappaṭṭa kuḻalkaḷiruntaṉa. ekkāḷa vakikaḷil tāri, kāḷam, kākaḷam, ammiyam, ciṉṉam eṉpaṉavum kompu vakikaḷil kōṭu, irali, vayir mutaliyaṉavum iruntaṉa.
narampuk karuvikaḷil ciṟappuṭiyatu yāḻ. avikaḷukku ēḻu, irupattoṉṟu allatu ataṟku mēṟpaṭṭa narampukaḷ iruntaṉa. paṟi, muracu, pēriki, mattaḷam, ākuḷi, ellari, calliki, kiṇi mutaliyaṉa mēḷa vakikaḷuḷ cila. iṉṟu, ilaṅkit tīvil eḻupatukku mēṟpaṭṭa mēḷa vakikaḷ vaḻaṅkukiṉṟaṉa. itaṉāl akkālattil palavaki mēḷaṅkaḷ iruntaṉaveṉṟu aṟiya varukiṟatu. pāṇar kiyil koṇṭu tirintu aṭittup pāṭum ciṟiya mēḷaṅkaḷ tāri, uṭukki mutaliyaṉa.
tamiḻar nūlkaḷip pāṭal vaṭivil ceytu iciyōṭu pāṭi vantaṉar. āṭalkaḷōṭu pāṭalkaḷum pāṭappaṭṭaṉa. peṇkaḷ, iḻavuk kālattil tamatu tukkatti oppāri eṉṉum pāṭalkaḷākap pāṭiṉar.
“pantāṭuvatilum pāṭṭu, ūcalāṭuvatilum pāṭṭu, neṟkuṟṟu vatilum pāṭṭu, uḻavilum pāṭṭu, pōrilum pāṭṭu tamiḻariṭiyē malintu kāṇap paṭum. tamiḻarkku aḻukiyum pāṭṭāy varum. maṇamum pāṭṭāy nikaḻum. toḻukiyum pāṭṭāl viḷaṅkum. tamiḻar tey vattippāṭṭum iciyum payilavē vaṇaṅkuvar. ēṟṟap pāṭṭu, kappaṟ pāṭṭu, iṟavippāṭṭu, paḷḷi yeḻuccippāṭṭu, tālāṭṭuppāṭṭu, pāvippāṭṭu, maṟattiyarpāṭṭu, kuṟattiyarpāṭṭu, irēkippāṭṭu, kuṟippāṭṭu, paḷḷuppāṭṭu, paṟippāṭṭu, vaḷḷuvarpāṭṭu, vaṇṭip pāṭṭu, ammāṉippāṭṭu, kaḻaṅkup pāṭṭu, pallāṅkuḻippāṭṭu, tōḻippāṭṭu, pāṇṭippāṭṭu, kaṭi tiṟappuppāṭṭu, cintuppāṭṭu, cantappāṭṭu, piḷḷippāṭṭu, koḷḷippāṭṭu, kaḷḷarpāṭṭu, veṟṟippāṭṭu, vāḻttuppāṭṭu, maṅkalappāṭṭu, maṇappāṭṭu, kātaṟpāṭṭu, kāvaṭippāṭṭu, pakaṭurappaṟpāṭṭu, iṭiyarpāṭṭu, vēṭuvarpāṭṭu, naṭippāṭṭu, kummippāṭṭu, kuravippāṭṭu, kivīcaṟpāṭṭu, cappāṇippāṭṭu, kīrippāṭṭu, kōlappāṭṭu, kōlaṭippāṭṭu, cilampappāṭṭu, villuppāṭṭu, talluppāṭṭu (oruvarp pāṭa etirttup pāṭum pāṭṭu - mali nāṭṭu vaḻakku), kōyil pāṭṭu, kuḻaṟpāṭṭu, kūttiṟ pāṭṭu mutaliya icip pāṭṭukaḷ ellām tamiḻaruṭiyavi”.
muṟkālattil ici vaḷartta kuṭumpattār pāṇar eṉa aṟiyap paṭṭaṉar. akkālattilirunta ici aṟiñar tuḷik karuvivācip pōr, tōṟkaruvi vācippōr, narampuk karuvi vācippōr, kaṇṭat tāṟ pāṭuvōr eṉa nālvakip piriviṉarāka amintu ici vaḷart tārkaḷ. tirunīlakaṇṭa yāḻppāṇar vācitta yāḻ cakōṭa yāḻ. tēvāra tiruvācakaṅkaḷ akkālattil ciṟanta icippāṭalkaḷāka viḷaṅkiṉa. cōḻa nāṭṭil uṟiyūril tōṉṟiya tiruppaṇṇāḻvār tiruvaraṅkak kaṭavuḷukku icit tamiḻt toṇṭu ceytu perumpēṟu peṟṟār. tiruttoṇṭar purāṇattil kūṟappaṭum āṉāyaṉār vēyṅkuḻalil iṟivaṉiṉ ainteḻutti icic curaṅkaḷākak koṇṭu vācittu iṟivaṉaruḷ peṟṟār. aruṇakiri nātar pāṭiya pākkaḷ canta ici yil ciṟantavi. tirumuṟi kaṇṭa cōḻaṉ, tirunīlakaṇṭa yāḻppāṇar marapil vanta pāṭiṉiyārik koṇṭu tēvāraṅkaḷukkup paṇṇamiti yiṉi vakuttamittāṉ. cēntaṉār mutaliya oṉpatiṉmarāṟ pāṭap peṟṟa pāṭalkaḷ tēvāratti oppap paṇṇaṭivu peṟṟuḷḷaṉa. irācarāca cōḻaṉ tēvārat tiruppatikam pāṭutaṟkum ici pāṭutaṟ kum palarit tañcip periya kōyilil niyamittāṉ. muttut tāṇṭa var kīrttaṉi, irāma nāṭakak kīrttaṉi mutaliyaṉa piṟkāla icip pāṭalkaḷākum. yāḻum vīṇiyum iruvēṟu icik karuvikaḷ.
iciyiṉ kālatti aḷappataṟkut tāḷam vaḻakkil iruntatu. tāḷattip paṟṟik kūṟum tāḷa ōttu, tāḷa camuttiram mutaliya nūlkaḷ iruntaṉa. iciyip paṟṟik kūṟum ici nuṇukkam, mutu nāri, mutu kuruku, intira kāḷiyam, pañcamarapu, parata cēṉāpatiyam mutaliya pala nūlkaḷ iruntaṉa. ivi ippoḻutu iṟantu viṭṭaṉa.
57. pōr
tamiḻaracar perumpālum tamatu āṇiyip piṟa aracar mītu celuttum poruṭṭup pōr ceytaṉar. pōr perumpālum aṟuppuk kālattiṉ piṉ nikaḻntatu. mēṟkoḷḷappaṭṭa pōrkaḷiṉ taṉmi nōkki avi veṭci, vañci, uḻiñi, tumpi, vāki eṉap peyar peṟṟaṉa. pōr vīrar avvak kālattil muṭiyil cūṭik koṇṭa pūkkaḷ kāraṇamāka appeyarkaḷ tōṉṟiṉa. tamiḻnāṭṭi āṇṭa mūvēntarukkum vevvēṟu pūkkaḷ iruntaṉa. pāṇṭiyaṉukku vēppam pūvum, cōḻaṉukku āttip pūvum cēraṉukkup paṉaṅkuruttum aṭiyāḷap pūkkaḷākum. iv varacarkaḷiṉ paṭi vīrar tammaracariṉ pūvic cūṭutal marapu. cila camayaṅkaḷil avarkaḷ ap pūkkaḷip poṉṉiṉāl ceytu cūṭiṉar. veṭci eṉpatu oru aracaṉ māṟṟāṉuṭiya pacuk kūṭṭaṅ kaḷik kavartal. pacukkaḷi mīṭṭal karanti eṉa aṟiyappaṭum. vañci, māṟṟāṉ mītu paṭi eṭuttuc cellutal. uḻiñi, ōr aracaṉ iṉ ṉoru aracaṉiṉ kōṭṭiyi muṟṟukiyiṭutal. tumpi, iru paṭi kaḷum oṉṟi oṉṟu etirttup porutal. vāki, veṟṟiyik kuṟikkum. kāñci, ulaka niliyāmiyik kūṟuvatu. pāṭāṇ, aracar peru makkaḷiṉ veṟṟiyiyum pukaḻiyum pulavarkaḷ pāṭuvatu. muṟkālap pōrkaḷ vīram, tiṟami, valimi mutaliyavaṟṟik kāṭṭutaṟkuc ceyyap paṭṭamiyāl avi aracariṉ poḻutu pōkkukaḷākavum iruntaṉa. 
pōrkkaḷam, kaḷari, paṟantali, mutunilam eṉa aṟiyappaṭṭatu. paṭikaḷ aṇi, uṇṭi, oṭṭu mutaliya pala pirivukaḷākap pirikkap paṭṭiruntaṉa. muṉṉaṇi, ākkam, koṭippaṭi, tār, tūci, nirip paṭi eṉappaṭṭatu. piṉ paṭi kūḻi eṉappaṭṭatu. yāṉi, tēr, kutiri, kālāḷ eṉap paṭi nālvakip paṭṭiruntatu. yāṉi vīraṉ pulittōl kavacam aṇintu ceṉṟāṉ. avaṉic cūḻntu cila vīrar ceṉṟaṉar. yāṉi pākaṉāl naṉku paḻakkappaṭṭiruntatu. atu kantu allatu taṟiyil kaṭṭappaṭṭatu. ataṟku ariciyum carkkariyum kalanta cōṟṟuk kavaḷam koṭukkappaṭṭatu. ataṟku nīrāṭṭik kuṅkumam pūci neṟṟippaṭṭaṅ kaṭṭappaṭṭatu. cūḻi, ōṭi eṉpaṉa neṟṟip paṭṭattik kuṟikkum peyarkaḷ.
tērkaḷ niṟamūṭṭiya tuṇikaḷālum, pūmālikaḷ, ilikaḷā lum alaṅkarikkappaṭṭaṉa. avi niri niriyākap pōrkkaḷattukkuc ceṉṟaṉa. pōril vil, ampu, vaḷitaṭi, īṭṭi, vēl, vāḷ pōṉṟa āyutaṅkaḷ payaṉpaṭuttappaṭṭaṉa. taṭi, taṇṭu, eṟuḻ, kuṇil mutaliyaṉa taṇṭu vakikaḷil cila. vil, kokkari, cili, taṭi, tavar, muṉi, koṭu maram mutaliyaṉa vil vakikaḷil cila. vāḷ, uvaṇi, ēṟi, kaṭuttali, tuvaṭṭi, navir, nāṭṭam, vañcam, cuṟumpiṭi, curiki, mutaliyaṉa īṭṭi vakiyil cila. vēl, eyil, araṇam, eḵkam, kuntam, ñāṅkar, uṭampiṭi, viṭṭēṟu mutaliyaṉa vēlvakiyuḷ cila. ampu, kaṇi, katiram, kō, kōl, toṭi, tōṇi, pakaḻi, paḷḷam, puṭi, vaṇṭu, vāḷi mutaliyaṉa ampu vakiyuḷ cila. nāṇi, nāṇ, pūram, āvam, koṭi, nāri, narampu, pūṭṭu, uṭu mutaliyaṉa vil nāṇiṉ peyarkaḷ. kēṭakam, kiṭuku, kaṭakam, taṭṭu, parici, palaki, maṟi, vaṭṭaṇam, vaṭṭam, tōl, tōṟparam mutaliyaṉa parici vakiyuḷ cila. mēlakam, araṇi, ācu, kantaḷam, mey yuṟi eṉpaṉa kavaca vakikaḷuḷ cila. kik kavacam kippuṭi eṉap paṭṭatu. aracaṉiṭattil pōr muracu iruntatu. atu nīrāṭṭi, neṟkati rāl alaṅkarittu uyirp paliyiṭṭu vaḻipaṭappaṭṭatu. māṟṟaracaṉiṉ kāval maratti veṭṭit tuṇṭāṭi ataṉāl pōr muracu ceyyap paṭṭatu.
pōril iṟappōr vīra corkkam celkiṟārkaḷ eṉa makkaḷ nampiṉārkaḷ. pōril iṟavātu mutumi aṭintu allatu nōy vāyppaṭṭu iṟakkum aracariṉ uṭalit taruppiyil kiṭattivāḷāl pōḻntu piṉ cuṭuvatu allatu nallaṭakkam ceyvatu akkāla vaḻak kāka iruntatu. pōr toṭaṅkum muṉ antaṇar, peṇkaḷ, nōyā ḷar, vayōtikar, ciṟuvar eṉpōri appuṟappaṭuttumpaṭi pakivar muṉṉaṟivippuc ceyvar.
otta paṭik kalaṅkaḷillātavaṉuṭaṉ pōr ceyvatu, tōṟ ṟōṭuvōṉ, kuṭumi kulintōṉ, tūtar mutalāṉōrik kolvatu nītikku māṟu eṉak koḷḷappaṭṭatu. pōril kāyampaṭṭavarkaḷ palakiyil vittu eṭuttuc cellappaṭṭārkaḷ. kāyaṅkaḷ ūciyi ṉāl tikkappaṭṭaṉa. avvūci neṭu veḷḷūci eṉa aṟiyappaṭṭatu. pōril vīram kāṭṭiyavarkaḷukku aracaṉ paṭṭaṅkaḷ vaḻaṅkiṉāṉ. paṭit talivaṉ ēṉātip paṭṭattukku aṭiyāḷamāka mōtiram vaḻaṅkappaṭṭatu. veṉṟa aracaṉ tōṟṟa aracaṉiṉ muṭiyi urukkiya poṉṉāl vīra taṇṭi allatu māli ceytu aṇintāṉ. veṟṟi peṟṟa aracaṉ māli ceytu aṇintāṉ. veṟṟi peṟṟa aracaṉ tōṟṟa aracaṉiṉ nīrt tuṟiyil taṉatu koṟṟak kuṭiyi nīrāṭṭu talum avaṉuṭiya kāval marattil taṉatu yāṉiyik kaṭṭutalum ciṟanta ceyalkaḷākak karutappaṭṭaṉa.
58. paṭi
mūlap paṭi, kūlip paṭi, naṭpup paṭi, pakip paṭi, nāṭṭup paṭi, vēṭṭuvap paṭi eṉap paṭikaḷ aṟu vakiyiṉa. talimuṟi yāka aracaṉiṭamiruntu varuvatum, pōrp payiṟciyil tali ciṟantatu mākiya paṭi mūlappaṭi eṉappaṭṭatu. tirukkuṟaḷ itaṉit tol paṭi eṉak kūṟukiṉṟatu. aracaṉ ivarkaḷi eppoḻutum pōrukku āyattamāka vittiruntāṉ. taṉakku utaviyākavuḷḷa naṭpu aracar utaviya paṭi naṭpup paṭi eṉappaṭṭatu. ippaṭiyiṉar nampikki uṭiyavarkaḷāka iruppārkaḷō eṉpatil cantēkam iruntatu. ākavē ippaṭiyiṉar muṉ eccarikkiyōṭu payaṉpaṭuttappaṭṭārkaḷ. etirikaḷiṭamiruntu akappaṭuttappaṭṭārkaḷ allatu etiriyiṉ paṭiyi viṭṭu vilaki vantavarkaḷ pakippaṭiyiṉar eṉappaṭ ṭārkaḷ. nāṭṭup paṭiyōṭu ivarkaḷic cērttup pōrukku aṉuppu vatil kavaṉam celuttappaṭṭatu. vēṭṭuvap paṭiyiṉar pōril kiṭikkum koḷḷip poruḷkaḷukkākap pōr ceytaṉar. pōrk kālattil nāṭṭiliruntu tiraṭṭappaṭṭavarkaḷ aṭaṅkiya paṭi nāṭṭup paṭi eṉappaṭṭatu. kūliyiṉ poruṭṭup pōr ceyvōr kūlip paṭiyiṉar eṉa aṟiyappaṭṭaṉar.
paṭi alaku patti eṉappaṭṭatu. iḵtu oru tēr, oru yāṉi, mūṉṟu kutiri, aintu kālāḷ koṇṭatu.
59. yāṉip paṭi
yāṉikaḷ pōrmuṉiyil niṉṟu pōr ceyyumpaṭiyum, aṇiyi viṭṭu vilakik kuḻappam ceyyātirukkum paṭiyum payiṟṟap paṭṭaṉa. avaṟṟiṉ uṭal tōl pōrviyāl kākkappaṭṭatu. yāṉi kaḷi veppa kālattil payaṉpaṭuttāmal viṭuvatu virumpappaṭṭatu. avi etiriyiṉ paṭiyit tākki aṇiyik kulittatu māttira mallāmal vēlikaḷiyum, kūṭāraṅkaḷiyum, araṇ ceyyappaṭṭa iṭaṅkaḷiyum aḻittaṉa. pōr yāṉikaḷiṉ kompukaḷil irumpi ṉāl ceyyappaṭṭa pūṇkaḷ iṟukkappaṭṭaṉa. pūṇkaḷ kimpuri eṉap paṭṭaṉa. cila camayaṅkaḷil kompukaḷil kūriya vāḷkaḷ kaṭṭappaṭṭaṉa. matil kataviṉ mītu pāyntu ataṉi uṭittaṟkup pūṇkaḷ utaviyāka iruntaṉa. pākaṉit tavira iruvar allatu mūvar ataṉ mītiruntārkaḷ. ovvoru yāṉiyum ciṟu kālāṭ paṭiyāl pātukākkappaṭṭatu. pōr ceyyātavarkaḷ vaṇṭikaḷuṭaṉ piṉṉē ceṉṟārkaḷ. yāṉikaḷ mika ariya uṭimikaḷākak karutappaṭṭaṉa. aracaṉuṭiya veṟṟi yāṉip paṭiyiṉ tiṟamiyip poṟuttatāka iruntatu. kōpaṅ koṇṭa oru yāṉi āyiram kutirikaḷukkuc camam eṉak karutap paṭṭatu. araca vakuppiṉar yāṉiyip payaṉpaṭuttiṉar. pōr toṭaṅ kuvataṟku muṉ yāṉikku matu ūṭṭutalum vaḻakkāka iruntatu. yāṉi mītu koṭi nāṭṭappaṭṭiruntatu.
13ām nūṟṟāṇṭil intiyāvukku vanta cīṉap pirayāṇi oruvaṉ eḻutiyiruppatu varumāṟu:
“cōḻa aracaṉiṭattil aṟupatiṉāyiram pōr yāṉikaḷ niṟkiṉṟaṉa. ovvoṉṟum ēḻu allatu eṭṭaṭi uyaramuṭiyatu. pōr ceyyum pōtu yāṉikaḷ mutukiṉ mēl vīṭu1kaḷik koṇṭu celkiṉṟaṉa. avaṟṟuḷ pōr vīrar iruntu tolivil niṟpavarkaḷ mītu ampu eytum, aṇmiyil niṟpavarkaḷi īṭṭiyāl kuttiyum pōr ceyvar”.
60. kutirip paṭi
kutirikaḷ irumpuk kavacamiṭṭuk kākkappaṭṭaṉa. vīrar, vil, īṭṭi, vāḷ eṉpavaṟṟit tāṅkiyiruntaṉar. kutirikaḷukkuk kaṭivāḷa miṭappaṭṭatu eṉṟum, cēṇam iṭappaṭavilli eṉṟum kirēkkar kūṟiyirukkiṉ ṟaṉar. vēvu pārppataṟkum etiriyiṉ paṭiyi ūṭuruvic celvataṟkum kutirip paṭi payaṉpaṭuttappaṭṭatu. kutirip paṭiyil kutirikaḷip paḻakkuvōrum vēlikkārarum iruntaṉar. kuṭa liyar kutirikaḷiṉ patiṉāṟu cāriyikaḷip paṟṟi kuṟippiṭṭuḷḷār. patiṉāṟu vakik kaṭi vāḷaṅkaḷum āṟu vaki muṭkaḷum kuṟippiṭap paṭṭuḷḷaṉa. oṭṭakaṅkaḷ piṟkālaṅkaḷil payaṉpaṭuttappaṭṭaṉa.
61. tērp paṭi
tērkaḷil iraṇṭu kutirikaḷ pūṭṭappaṭṭaṉa. avaṟṟil pōr ceypavaṉum tērppākaṉum niṟkak kūṭiyatāka iruntatu. pōr ceypavaṉ iṭappuṟattil niṉṟāṉ. tērkaḷiṉ vaṭivam ikkālam teṉṉintiya kōyilkaḷil kāṇappaṭum tērkaḷiṉ vaṭivi ottiruntatu. avi virivil cellak kūṭiyaṉa. kaliṅkattup paraṇi mutaliya ilak kiyaṅkaḷiṟ kūṟappaṭuvaṉa koṇṭu itaṉi aṟiya muṭikiṟatu. tērkaḷ cama nilaṅkaḷil māttiram payaṉpaṭuttappaṭṭaṉa. tēril cāratiyit tavira iraṇṭu pōr ceyyum vīrar iruntaṉar eṉṟu mekastīṉas kūṟiyuḷḷaṉar. tērppākaṉ kavacamaṇintu kiyil villip piṭit tiruntāṉ. vaṭanāṭṭil tēr celuttuvōṉ cūtaṉ eṉa aṟiyap paṭṭāṉ. avaṉ pōrkkaḷattil kaṇṭa kāṭcikaḷiyum, veṟṟi kaḷiyum pāṭalkaḷākap pāṭiṉāṉ. avaṉ aracariṉ varalāṟ ṟāciriyaṉākavum perumi aṭintāṉ.
62. kālāṭ paṭi
kālāṭ paṭiyiṉar pavaṉi cellavum akaḻ veṭṭavum, matilkaḷ eḻuppavum, irākkālat tākkutalkaḷic camāḷikkavum, ekkālattum evvaki iṭattum pōr ceyyavum āyattamāka irukkumpaṭi paḻakkappaṭṭiruntārkaḷ. kaṭṭāya vēlikkākat tiraṭṭappaṭṭōr paṇṭaṅkaḷiyum, pōrk karuvikaḷiyum, kāyappaṭṭōriyum eṭuttuc ceṉṟaṉar. 
63. pōrk kaṭṭaḷikaḷ
pattu, nūṟu, āyiram eṉṉum kūṭṭaṅkaḷākap paṭi pirikkappaṭ ṭiruntatu. yāṉikaḷ, kutirikaḷ, tērkaḷukkup poṟuppāṉa ati kārikaḷ iruntārkaḷ. cēṉātipati paṭikaḷiṉ talivaṉāka iruntāṉ. ippeyar pattup pēraṭaṅkiya paṭip piriviṉ talivaṉik kuṟippa tāvum iruntatu. makā cēṉātipati, nāyakaṉ eṉṉum talivar muṭik kuriya irāca kumāraṉi otta uyarnta niliyiluḷḷavarkaḷāka iruntaṉar. aracaṉ peyaraḷavil ellārilum mēlāṉa taḷapatiyāka iruntāṉ.
kaṭṭaḷikaḷ camikkikaḷālum, vāttiyaṅkaḷi vēṟupaṭa olikkum olikaḷālum aṟivikkappaṭṭaṉa. eḻutappaṭṭa ōlic curuḷi ampil kaṭṭi eytu ceytikaḷ aṟivikkappaṭṭaṉa. ovvoru ciṟiya irāṇuva alakukkum ataṉ koṭi iruntatu. mutaṉmiyāṉa vīrar taṉittaṉi aṭiyāḷamuḷḷa koṭiyi vittiruntaṉar eṉṟu māpāratam kūṟukiṉṟatu. cakuṉaṅ kūṟuvōrum pulavarkaḷum etiriyit tākkuvataṟku ēṟṟa nērattik kūṟiṉārkaḷ. appōtu avarkaḷ pōr vīrarukku uṟcākam ūṭṭiṉārkaḷ. pōr toṭaṅku muṉ paṭikkumuṉ veḷiccam kāṭṭappaṭṭatu. paṭi, nāḷoṉṟukku iraṇṭu yōcaṉi tūram ceṉṟatu. yōcaṉi eṉpatu 32,000 muḻam koṇṭa tūram. caṅku, kompu mutaliya vāttiyaṅkaḷum palavakip paṟikaḷum pōril olikkappaṭṭaṉa.
64. aṇivakuppu
cātāraṇa aṇivakuppu camaviyūkam eṉappaṭṭatu. ataṟku matti, iru ciṟakukaḷ, iru ciṟakukaḷiyum aṭutta iru pakkaṅkaḷ eṉa aintu pakutikaḷuṇṭu. ivaṟṟil mottam 45 tēr, 45 yāṉi, 225 kutiri, 675 kālāṭkaḷ uṇṭu. ivaṟṟōṭu kāvaṟ paṭi tuṇip paṭi aṭaṅkiya 4,050 vīrarkaḷ koṇṭa cēṉiyi oru paṭi eṉalām.
ovvoru varicikkum iṭiyil aintu muḻattūramum, oru vīraṉukkum maṟṟa vīraṉukkum iṭiyil pattu aṅkula veḷiyumiruntaṉa. yāṉikaḷ mattiyiṉ muṉ niṟuttappaṭṭaṉa. tērkaḷ iraṇṭu ciṟaku kaḷiṉ muṉ allatu piṉ niṉṟaṉa. tērkaḷillāviṭil kutirip paṭi aṇiyiṉ pakkaṅkaḷik kāttatu. yāṉip paṭiyiṉoru pakuti cēmap paṭiyāka niṟuttappaṭṭiruntatu. kavacamaṇintavarkaḷ muṉṉaṇiyilum, maṟṟavarkaḷ pakka aṇikaḷilum, villāḷar iraṇṭām aṇiyilum niṉṟārkaḷ.
kampa aṇi etiriyi nēr variciyākat tākkuvatu. kaḻuku aṇi, kaḻuku pōl iraṇṭu pakka aṇikaḷuṭaṉ ceṉṟu tākkuvatu. ūci muṉi aṇi pakka aṇikaḷiyum, vilā aṇikaḷiyum uḷḷuk kiḻuttuk koṇṭu taṉṉilum atika eṇṇuḷḷa etiriyiṉ paṭiyit tākkuvatu. pāmpu vaḷivu aṇi, pāmpu pōla vaḷintu ceṉṟu paki varit tākkuvatu. vaṭṭa aṇi eṅkum paṭimukam iruppatu pōlat tōṉṟumpaṭi vaṭṭamāka amikkappaṭuvatu. ivvāṟu pala aṇi vakuppukkaḷiruntaṉa.
etiriyiṉ talivarkaḷik kolvataṟku vekumatikaḷ vaḻaṅkap paṭṭaṉa. aracaṉik kolpavaṉukku 100,000 paṇamum, paṭittali vaṉik kolpavaṉukku 50,000 paṇamum, yāṉiyik kolpavaṉukku 5,000 paṇamum, kutiriyik kolpavaṉukku 1000 paṇamum, ciṟu atikārikaḷik kolpavaṉukku 100 paṇamum, kāvalarkaḷik kol pavaṉukku 20 paṇamum vaḻaṅkappaṭṭaṉa. paṭiyiṉ piṉ maruntu utavum paṭi iruntateṉṟum, paṇi ceyyum peṇkaḷ piṉṉē niṉṟu uṟcākam ūṭṭiṉārkaḷ eṉṟum kuṭaliyar kūṟiyuḷḷār. taṉippaṭṭa paṭi, paṭikku vēṇṭiya poruḷi muṉṉamē koṇṭu ceṉṟu cērttatu.1
65. pōr āyutaṅkaḷ
palavakip pērāyutaṅkaḷ iruntaṉa. muṉṉāl entirak karuvikaḷ ceṉṟaṉa. cakkaraṅkaḷ cuḻalumpōtu kavaṇil kaṟkaḷi eṟintaṉa. muḷ irumput taṇṭāyutaṅkaḷ (nūṟṟu varikkolli) itikāca kālattil aṟiyappaṭṭiruntaṉa. kōṭṭi matilkaḷil kal eṟiyum entiraṅkaḷ nāṭṭap paṭṭiruntaṉa. neruppup paṭikkalaṅkaḷ payaṉpaṭuttap paṭṭaṉa. neruppup paṭik kalaṅkaḷ eṉpaṉa neruppip koṇṭu cellum ampukaḷ. īṭṭikaḷil palavakikaḷ iruntaṉa. potuvāṉa īṭṭi muṟṟilum ulōkattiṉāl ceyyappaṭṭiruntatu. ataṉ nīḷam aintaṭi eṭṭu aṅkulam. cila marakkip piṭiyum ulōkamuṉiyum uṭiyavi. tōmaram eṉpatu yāṉip paṭiyiṉ mukkiya āyutam; atu nīṇṭa īṭṭi. tiricūlam, cakkaram, kavaṇ, taṇṭu, cammaṭṭi, mūṉṟu muṉikaḷuṭiya kaṇṭa kōṭāri mutaliya āyutaṅkaḷum payaṉpaṭuttap paṭṭaṉa. vaccirameṉpatu eṟipaṭi. vāḷkaḷil pala vakikaḷ iruntaṉa. avi nīṇṭum oṭuṅkiyum iruntaṉa. kippiṭikaḷ kompu, tantam, maram, mūṅkil eṉpavikaḷāliṭappaṭṭaṉa. vil uyar vakuppiṉarāl payaṉ paṭuttappaṭṭatu. atu paṉi, pirampu, vayiramaram, kompu eṉpavaṟṟāl ceyyappaṭṭatu. nalla vil aintaṭi eṭṭu eṅkula nīḷamuṭiyatu. nāṇ, caṇal, mūṅkil nār, vilaṅkukaḷiṉ narampukaḷāka iruntaṉa. ampi viṭumuṉ atu nāṇil vittuk kātu vari iḻukkappaṭṭatu. cuyamvarattil ampeyvatu mutaliṭam peṟṟiruntatu. taṟkāppukkuriya karuvikaḷ pala payaṉpaṭuttappaṭṭaṉa. tali, tōḷ, uṭal, muḻaṅkāl kaḷik kākkum kavacaṅkaḷ iruntaṉa.
66. kōṭṭiyum pācaṟiyum
kōṭṭikaḷiṉ amippu iṭaṅkaḷukkēṟpa vēṟupaṭṭiruntaṉa. kōṭṭiyi akaḻ allatu mali araṇ ceytatu. ciṟpanūl pat toṉpatu vakik kōṭṭikaḷip paṟṟik kuṟippiṭukiṉṟatu. kōṭṭi perumpālum nāṭṭiṉ elliyil kaṭṭappaṭṭiruntatu. ataṟku mūṉṟu akaḻkaḷiruntaṉa. avi muṟiyē 56, 48, 40 muḻa akalamuṭi yavi. ovvoru akaḻikkumiṭiyil nāṉku muḻa veḷiyiruntatu. akaḻkaḷiṉ āḻam akalattilum pāti aḷaviṉatāka iruntatu. uḷ akaḻiṉ piṉ 24 muḻam uyarnta mēṭi iruntatu. itupōl irumaṭi akalattil nañcu muḷ maraṅkaḷum ceṭikaḷum naṭappaṭṭiruntaṉa. ataṉ piṉ 24 muḻa uyaramum, 12 aṭi akalamuḷḷa matil kaṭṭappaṭṭiruntaṉa. kōpuraṅkaḷiṉiṭiyē iraṇṭu māṭikaḷuṭiya kaṭṭiṭaṅkaḷ iruntaṉa. avaṟṟiṉ mēl māṭiyil mūṉṟu villāṭkaḷ maṟintu niṟkak kūṭiyatāka iruntatu. matilic cuṟṟi uṭpuṟattil vīti ceṉṟatu. pakivar muṟṟuki iṭuṅkālaṅkaḷil caṭutiyil ceṉṟu avarit tākkutaṟku veḷiyē cellum iṭaṅkaḷ iruntaṉa. kōṭṭi vāyiṟkatavukaḷ pala maraṅkaḷi oṉṟiṉ mītu oṉṟāka vittup poruttic ceyyappaṭ ṭiruntaṉa. avi iraṇṭu ciṟakukaḷāka amikkap paṭṭiruntaṉa. avi irumpuc calākikaḷāl tāḻiṭappaṭṭaṉa. kōṭṭiyuḷ curuṅki vaḻikaḷiruntaṉa.
pācaṟi eṉpatu paṭaṅkukaḷāliṭappaṭṭa araṇ ceyyappaṭṭa kūṭāram. itu cōtiṭariṉ ālōcaṉiyōṭu ciṟpikaḷāl karuttōṭu vakukkappaṭṭatu. iḵtu iṭaṅkaḷukkēṟpa vaṭṭamāka, nīṇṭa caturamāka allatu caturamāka amikkappaṭṭatu. itaṟku nāṉku vāyilkaḷum piṉṉē ilēcāṉa araṇkaḷumiruntaṉa. iḵtu āṟu pirivukaḷākap pirikkappaṭṭiruntatu. aracaṉuṟiyumiṭam mutaliraṇṭu aṟikaḷāka iruntatu. atikārikaḷ teṟkil iruntārkaḷ. yāṉikaḷum kutiri kaḷum kaṭṭumiṭam vaṭakkiliruntatu. atu oru ciṟiya paṭṭiṉamāka iruntatu. vāttiyakkārarum, vēṭṭuvarum kūṭārattukku veḷiyil taṅkiṉārkaḷ.
67. nampikkikaḷ
cōtiṭattilum cakuṉattilum nampikki iruntatu. eri koḷḷi viḻuvatu nāṭṭiluḷḷa periyavariṉ maraṇattukku aṟikuṟi eṉak karutap paṭṭatu. kūntal virittirukkum peṇṇip pārttal tītu eṉak karutap paṭṭatu. ciṟuvarit tīmikaḷiliruntu kāppataṟkāka aimpaṭittāli kaṭṭappaṭṭatu. pēykaḷi ōṭṭutaṟku veṇkaṭuku pukikkappaṭṭatu. ālamarattilum vēṟu cila maraṅkaḷilum pēyuṟivatākak karutappaṭṭatu. pāmpu cantira cūriyari viḻuṅkuvatāl kirakaṇa muṇṭākiṟateṉak karutappaṭṭatu. kākam karivatu viruntiṉar varuvataṟku aṟikuṟi eṉa nampappaṭṭatu. toliviṭattiluḷḷa oruvar oruvari niṉippatāl tummaluṇṭākiṟateṉak karutappaṭṭatu. nākattiṉ taliyil irattiṉam irukkiṟateṉa nampappaṭṭatu. palli colvatu naṟcakuṉa mākavō tīya cakuṉamākavō koḷḷappaṭṭatu. uṉṉamaram (ilavu) vāṭuvatu tīya cakuṉamākak karutappaṭṭatu. pōrkkaḷattil pēy tiriva tākavum, pēykaḷ piṇam tiṉpatākavum nampikki iruntatu. vēppili ciṟuvarip pēykaḷiliruntu kākkum eṉa nampappaṭṭatu. pōril iṟantavar vīra corkkamaṭivar eṉṉum nampikki iruntatu. valak kaṇ tuṭippatu naṟcakuṉamākavum. iṭakkaṇ tuṭippatu tīya cakuṉamākavum koḷḷappaṭṭaṉa. ciṟuvarukkuk kaṇṇūṟu paṭāmal avar tali mayiril neyyum veṇ ciṟu kaṭukum pūcappaṭṭaṉa. 
68. pōkkuvarattu
perumpālum makkaḷ kāl naṭiyākap pōkkuvarattuc cey tārkaḷ. palavaki vaṇṭikaḷ, pallakku, tēr, kaḻuti, erutu, yāṉi mutaliyaṉavum muṟkālap pōkkuvarattuc cātaṉaṅkaḷāka iruntaṉa. ūrti, oḻuki, cakaṭu, cākāṭu, viyam mutaliyaṉa vaṇṭiyik kuṟikkum peyarkaḷ. vaṇṭikaḷum kaḻutikaḷum potimāṭukaḷum paṇṭaṅkaḷi ōriṭattiliruntu ōriṭattukku eṭuttuccellap payaṉpaṭuttappaṭṭaṉa. aracarum perumakkaḷum tēr, yāṉi, pallakku mutaliyavikaḷil ceṉṟārkaḷ. nīril celvōr ōṭaṅkaḷil ceṉṟaṉar. ōṭaṅkaḷil pala vakikaḷ iruntaṉa. ōṭam, ampi, tōṇi, teppam, paṭaku, kalam, paḵṟi, catā, pōtam, toḷḷam, pakaṭu, paṭṭiki, pāṭṭimār, paṭuvi, puṇi, mitavi, vaḷḷam, timil mutaliyaṉa ōṭaṅkaḷik kuṟikkum peyarkaḷ. ivi vevvēṟu vaki ōṭaṅkaḷik kuṟippaṉavākalām. marakkalaṅ kaḷiṉ muṉpuṟam yāṉi mukam, kutiri mukam, arimukam pōṉṟu ceyyappaṭṭiruntatu. marakkalaṅkaḷukkup pāy maraṅkaḷum paṭaṅkum (pāyum) iruntaṉa.
69. ōviyam
mika muṟkālam mutal ōviyak kaliyil tiṟami peṟṟu viḷaṅ kiṉārkaḷ. muṟkāla eḻuttu muṟi ōviya vaṭivilēyē amintiruntatu. kaṟkāla vāḻkkiyilirunta makkaḷ kukic cuvarkaḷil tīṭṭiya ōviyaṅkaḷ kaṇṭupiṭikkappaṭṭuḷḷaṉa. avi tiṟamiyāka eḻutappaṭṭuḷḷaṉa. mokañcatārō makkaḷiṉ muttirikaḷil aḻakiya ōviyaṅkaḷ veṭṭappaṭṭuḷḷaṉa. avi ikkālam variyappaṭum ciṟanta ōviyaṅ kaḷōṭu otta kalittiṟami uṭiyaṉavāka irukkiṉṟaṉa. acantāk kuki ōviyaṅkaḷ ulakap pukaḻ peṟṟavi. caṅkakāla nūlkaḷil ōviyak kaliyip paṟṟiya kuṟippukaḷ kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. araṇmaṉic cuvar kaḷilum, kōyil cuvarkaḷilum, celvariṉ māḷikic cuvarkaḷilum aḻakiya ōviyaṅkaḷ variyappaṭṭiruntaṉa. akkālak kōyilkaḷil eḻuttu nili maṇṭapam eṉa oru pakuti iruntatu. aṅku perumpālum purāṇa campantamāṉa ōviyaṅkaḷ variyappaṭṭiruntaṉa.
itaṉi,
“intiraṉ pūci yivaḷakaliki yivaḷ
ceṉṟa kavutamaṉ ciṉaṉuṟak kalluru
voṉṟiya paṭiyiteṉ ṟuricey vōru
miṉṉam palapala veḻuttu nilimaṇṭapam”
eṉap paripāṭal aṭikaḷ kuṟippiṭukiṉṟaṉa.
“cuṭuma ṇōṅkiya neṭunili maṉitoṟu
miyaṟu paṭivattu vāṉavar muṉivar
evvaki yuyirkaḷu vuvamaṅ kāṭṭi
kaṇkala rōviyaṅ kaṇṭu niṟkunarum”
eṉṉum maṇimēkali aṭikaḷ akkāla maṉikaḷil ōviyaṅkaḷ eḻutappaṭṭiruntamiyi naṉku viḷakkukiṉṟaṉa. paḻantamiḻ ilakkiyaṅ kaḷil maṭalēṟutal eṉṉum oru vaḻakkam kūṟappaṭukiṉṟatu. oruvaṉ tāṉ kātalitta peṇṇip peṟamuṭiyāta pōtu avaṉ avaḷip pōṉṟa paṭamoṉṟi eḻuti, uyarttik koṇṭu paṉi maṭṭiyāl ceyta kutiriyilēṟi vītiyil varuvāṉ. itaṉāl avaṉ kātalikkum peṇ yāreṉa aṟiyak kūṭiyatāka iruntatu. itaṉāl potumakkaḷum ōviyam variyum tiṟami peṟṟiruntārkaḷ eṉat terikiṟatu.
70. ciṟpam
ciṟpak kali intiyāvil mikap paḻiya kālattil vaḷarcci yaṭintiruntatu. mokañcatārōvil pala aḻakiya cuṭumaṇ pāvi kaḷum, kallil cetukkappaṭṭa maṉita uruvaṅkaḷum, ulōkattil vārkkappaṭṭa nāṭṭiyap peṇṇiṉ uruvamum kaṇṭupiṭikkap paṭṭaṉa. kallil cetukkappaṭṭa cili oṉṟu kikaḷum taliyum illāmal kāṇappaṭṭatu. itu kirēkka ciṟpak kaliyi otta kalit tiṟami peṟṟatāka aṟiñar pukaḻntuḷḷārkaḷ. ulōkattil vārkkap paṭṭa naṭaṉamātu uruvattip palar pukaḻntu eḻutiyuḷḷārkaḷ. ēṟattāḻa ki.mu. 3000-il intiya makkaḷ ciṟpak kaliyil mika muṉṉēṟ ṟam peṟṟiruntārkaḷ. tamiḻar peṟṟirunta tiṟamiyik kuṟittuc caṅka ilakkiyaṅkaḷil kāṇkiṉṟōm.
“kallu mulōkamum ceṅkalu maramum
maṇṇuñ cutiyun tantamum vaṇṇamum
kaṇṭacark kariyu meḻuku meṉṟivi
pattē ciṟpat toḻiṟkuṟup pāvaṉa”
eṉat tivākaram kūṟukiṉṟatu.
teṉṉintiyak kōyilkaḷil karuvaṟiyilirukkum tiruvuruvaṅ kaḷ kallil cetukkappaṭṭu vantaṉa. piṟkālattil cempum piṟa ulō kaṅkaḷum cērttu urukki vārkkappaṭṭaṉa. ulōkattil vārkkap paṭṭa uruvaṅkaḷ tiruviḻāk kālaṅkaḷil veḷiyē koṇṭu cellap paṭṭaṉa. ivvaki uruvaṅkaḷum naṭarācat tiruvuruvamum ulaka makkaḷiṉ pārāṭṭip peṟṟuḷḷatu. iṉṟu teṉṉintiyā ilaṅki mutaliya nāṭukaḷil nūtaṉa poruṭkāṭci cālikaḷil vikkappaṭ ṭirukkum paḻaṅkālac ciṟpaṅkaḷ campantappaṭṭa poruḷkaḷ tamiḻariṉ ciṟpat tiṟamiyi veḷiyiṭukiṉṟaṉa. cōḻar, pallavar kālaṅkaḷil eṭukkappaṭṭa kaṟkōyilkaḷum, malikkuṭivuk kōyilkaḷum kaṟ kaḷil cetukkappaṭṭirukkum vilaṅku, maṉitar, paṟavikaḷ, marañ ceṭikaḷiṉ vaṭivaṅkaḷum tamiḻariṉ ciṟpat tiṟaṉi eṉṟum kāṭṭik koṇṭirukkum aḻiyāc ciṉṉaṅkaḷākum
71. maruntu
maruttuvakkali nōykaḷit tīrkkum mūlikikaḷik kaṇṭu piṭippatiliruntu toṭaṅkukiṟatu. mūlikikaḷiṉ kuṇaṅkaḷ naṉku aṟiyappaṭṭiruntaṉa. vātamaṭakki, vaṇṭu kolli, kirantināyaṉ, poṉṉāṅkaṇṇi pōṉṟu avvam mūlikikaḷukkuḷḷa kuṇaṅkaḷē avaṟṟukkup peyarkaḷāka vaḻaṅkiṉa. mūliki akarātikaḷil mikap pala mūlikikaḷiṉ peyarkaḷ kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. patārttakuṇa cintāmaṇi eṉṉum nūl piṟkālattiṟ ceyyappaṭṭatāyiṉum, atu makkaḷ mūlikikaḷip paṟṟi muṉṉamē aṟintiruntavaṟṟit taḻuvic ceyyap paṭṭa nūlākum. kiyāḻam, kuḷiki, cūraṇam, ilēkiyam, tilam, centūram eṉṉum pala vakikaḷil maruntākap payaṉpaṭuttappaṭ ṭuḷḷatu. acōkac cakkaravartti vilaṅkukaḷukkum makkaḷukkum maruttuva niliyaṅkaḷi niṟuviṉār eṉac carittiram kūṟukiṉṟatu. ivvaki niliyaṅkaḷ ilaṅkiyilum niṟuvappaṭṭiruntaṉaveṉṟu makāvamicam kūṟukiṉṟatu. acōkar kālattukkup pala nūṟṟāṇṭukaḷiṉ muṉ maruttuvakkali intiyāvil vaḷarcciyaṭintiruntatu. alekcāntar intiyāviliruntu pāmpukkaṭi vittiyarkaḷik kirēkka nāṭṭukkuk koṇṭu ceṉṟār eṉak kirēkka āciriyarkaḷ kūṟiyirukkiṉṟaṉar. kippakiriṭṭas eṉṉum kirēkkar intiyariṉ maruttuva muṟikaḷik kaṟṟu avaṟṟik kiyāṇṭār eṉac collappaṭuvatuṇṭu.
tamiḻar kiyāṇṭa vittiya muṟi piṟkālattil citta muṟi eṉa vaḻaṅkukiṟatu. irācayaṉa muṟiyāṉa tamiḻariṉ maruttuvakkali paḻimiyāṉatum, payaṉaḷikkak kūṭiyatum, tamiḻnāṭṭiṉ poruḷā tāra nili, kāla nilikaḷukku ēṟṟatumākum. atu citta vittiyam eṉappaṭum. ataṉ nōkkam, taṭuppu, kuṇappaṭuttuvatu, iḻantu pōṉa valimiyit tirumpap peṟuvatu eṉṉum mūṉṟu kūṟukaḷi uṭiyatu. tiṭamāṉa uṭalil tiṭamāṉa maṉam eṉṉum koḷki uṟutippaṭ ṭiruntatu. uṭal illāviṭil oru pēṟum kiṭṭātu; uṭalillā viṭṭāl vīṭu kiṭṭātu eṉac cittar kūṟiṉar.
“tēkamirutā lallō tittellā māṭalām
tēkamirun tākkāṟ cēralām pūraṇam
tēkamirun tākkāṟ ceyalellām pārkkalām
tēkamirun tākkāṟ cēralām muttiyē” (tirumūlar karukkiṭi vittiyam)
ātiyilē cittaṉārākiya civaṉār ceyta maruttuva nūl ēḻu laṭcam pāṭalkaḷuṭiyatu. piṉ nanti, caṉakar, caṉātar, caṉāntaṉar, caṉaṟkumārar, tirumūlar, patañcali, akattiyar, pulattiyar, pucuṇṭar, karuvūrar, taṉvantiri, caṭṭimuṉi, tēriyar, yūkimuṉi mutaliya palar nūl ceytaṉar. ivi maṇi (iracamaṇi), mantiram, maruntu mutaliya vaṟṟik kūṟukiṉṟaṉa. mūliki, uppu, tīnīr1, upavācam, 2uṭaṟporuḷ, pāṭāṇam, ulōkam, cattu3, iracakkuḷiki, yōkam eṉṉum pattuc cikicci muṟikaḷit tirumūlar kūṟiyirukkiṉṟār. mantirameṉpatu yōkattilum maṇi eṉpatu iracak kuḷikikaḷilum aṭaṅkum. mūlikikaḷ cūraṇam, iḻakiyam (ilēkiyam), meḻuku eṉpaṉa. ivi makkaḷuṟi eṉappaṭum. kaṭṭikaḷukku maruntākum tilam, cārāyattil ūṟa viṭappaṭṭa maruntukaḷ aṟuvi campantamāṉavi; centūram, cuṇṇam, ceynīr, tīnīr, cattu, maṇi mutaliyaṉa, paspam (cāmpal) eṉpatil aṭaṅkum. immuṟi citta maruttuvattil māttiramuṇṭu.
oppuṟi (ōmiyōpati pōṉṟatu), etiruṟi (alōpati), kalap puṟi eṉa mūṉṟu vaki maruntu muṟikaḷ uṇṭu. uppu vakikaḷ 25, pāṭāṇam 64, ulōkam 9, ulōkac cattukaḷ 120, maruntu mūlikikaḷ 1008. nāṭi pārttu vittiyam ceytal cittamuṟi. iṭakali, piṅkali, cuḻi muṉi eṉa nāṭi mūṉṟu. maruttuvaṉ nāṭiyip pārttu vātam, pittam, cilēṭṭumam eṉṉum mūṉṟum iyalpāy irukkiṉṟaṉavā allatu iyalpukku māṟāka irukkiṉṟaṉavā eṉa aṟikiṟāṉ. aṭutta paṭiyil kaṇ, nākku, uṭal, malam, mūttiram, cattam mutaliyavaṟṟip pārttalōṭu uṭalit toṭṭup pārttum aṟiyappaṭum. citta vittiyattip piṉpaṟṟum tiruvaḷḷuvar, nōyik kaṇṭupiṭi, ataṟkuk kāraṇatti aṟi, ataṟku marunti ārāyntu pār, kāla niliyik kavaṉi, mikap payaṉaḷippavaṟṟic cey eṉak kūṟukiṉṟār. maruntuk kali, nōyāḷi, maruttuvaṉ, maruntukaḷi arittō iṭittō piḻintō kalantu ceypavaṉ eṉṉum nāṉku pakutikaḷi uṭiyatu. maruttuvacāli niṟuvuvatu muppattiraṇṭu aṟaṅkaḷuḷ oṉṟākac collappaṭṭuḷḷatu. āṉma caktiyiṉāl allatu maṉōcaktiyiṉāl māṟṟuvatu iṉṉoru muṟi. itu camayakuravarkaḷ muṉivarkaḷāl kiyāḷappaṭṭa muṟi. pārvi pārttal, nīrōtik koṭuttal, mantiram cepittal pōṉṟavi āṉma cattiyāl nōyi āṟṟum muṟiyil aṭaṅkum.
cārakam, cucurarutam, taṉvantiri nikaṇṭu eṉpaṉa vaṭa nāṭṭāriṉ maruttuva nūlkaḷ. ivaṟṟil muṉ kūṟappaṭṭa mūṉṟu uṟikaḷiyum kāṇa muṭiyātu. āyurvētam eṉpatu citta vittiyamākum. āyurvētam eṉṉum peyaruṭiya nūl āriya moḻiyil illi. taṉvantiri ki.pi. 500il vikkiramātittaṉiṉ araca capiyiliruntavar. cucurutar avar kālattavar. cārakar avarukku muṉ viḷaṅkiyavar. aṭṭāṅka irutayam vākpātarāl 9ām nūṟṟāṇṭil ceyyappaṭṭatu. piṟkāla maruttuva nūlār cittar nūlkaḷip payiṉṟum paspam, nāṭi, puṭam pōṭutal mutaliya muṟikaḷi moḻi peyarttut tamatu nūlil cērttaṉar. cāraṅkatarariṉ caṅkiti 13ām nūṟṟāṇṭil ceyyappaṭṭatu. innūl, atu citta vittiyattukkuk kaṭamippaṭṭiruppatik kūṟukiṉṟatu. ceṉṉiyil paṇṭitar kōpālāccāriyariṉ talimiyil kūṭiya āyurvēta mānāṭṭil avarum itu pōṉṟa karuttit terivikkiṉ ṟār. kaṇṇāl pārttal, toṭṭup pārttal, cattattik kēṭṭup pārttal eṉṉum mūṉṟu cōtaṉikaḷic ceyvatē vaṭanāṭṭu muṟi. atarvaṇa vētattit tokuttu muṭittapiṉ āyur, artta, taṉur, kāntarva vētaṅkaḷi eḻutuvataṟkum tiṭṭamiṭappaṭṭatu. āyur vētameṉṉum nūl orupōtum eḻutappaṭavilli.
tamiḻaracariṉ viḻukikkup piṉ citta vittiyam vīḻcci yaṭintatu (tamiḻ intiyā - mu.ci.pū.).
72. irēki nūl
akattiyariṉ irēki nūl cāmuttirikam eṉappaṭum. innūliṉ muḻup peyarum puruṭa cāmuttirika ilaṭcaṇam. itu cuppiramaṇiyak kaṭavuḷ akattiyarukkuk kūṟiyatākac collappaṭukiṟatu. itu uḷḷaṅ ki maṇikkaṭṭukaḷiluḷḷa irēkikaḷ, varikaḷ, maccam, āḷiṉ uyaram, neṭuppam, kikaḷ, kālkaḷiṉ nīḷaṅkaḷip pārttu maṉitariṉ kuṇā kuṇaṅkaḷi aṟiyumpaṭiyāṉa vitikaḷik kūṟukiṉṟatu. oruvaṉatu uḷḷaṅki civappēṟiyum, ciṟitākavum iruntāl avaṉukkuc celvamum nīṇṭa āyuḷum uṇṭu; taṭippāka iruntāl avaṉ kavali uṭiyavaṉāvāṉ. caṅkip pōlum, cakkarattip pōlum irēkikaḷ iruntāl avaṉ atika varuvāy uṭiyavaṉāyum, tarumam ceypavaṉāyum, taṉṉi aṭintavarkaḷiṭattil tayāḷam uṭiyava ṉākavum irup pāṉ. oruvaṉuṭiya kiyil macca irēki allatu mīṉ pōṉṟa aṭiyāḷam iruntāl avaṉ tayāḷamuṭiyavaṉāka iruppāṉ. mūccukkuḻāy pōṉṟa irēki iruntāl pukaḻ aṭi vāṉ. arivāḷ pōṉṟa irēki iruntāl avaṉ tiriyamum ūkkamum uṭiyava ṉāvāṉ. cāṭipōla iruntāl cāntamāṉavaṉāka iruppāṉ. cantiraṉip pōla iruntāl kalvimāṉāvāṉ. ivvāṟu annūl pala ceytikaḷik kūṟukiṉṟatu. ikkali pāṇṭi nāṭṭi liruntu arēpiyāvukkuc ceṉṟu aṅku niṉṟum airōppāvukkuc ceṉṟatu. (mu.ci.pū.)
73. vāṉārāycci
tamiḻar periya kaṭal payaṇakkārarāka iruntaṉar. avarkaḷ tamatu payaṇaṅkaḷil irākkālattil cantiraṉum naṭcattiraṅkaḷum niṟkum iṭaṅkaḷip pārppatu avarkaḷukku utaviyāka iruntatu. avarkaḷ mātam tētikaḷik kāṭṭum kuṟippukaḷi eḻuti vittapōtu cūriyaṉum cantiraṉum periyaṉavākat tōṉṟumpaṭi kuṟippiṭappaṭṭa ṉar. veḷiccamāṉa kirakaṅkaḷ oṉṟukkoṉṟu evvaḷavu tūrattil niṟkiṉṟaṉaveṉpatum kuṟippiṭappaṭṭatu. mātattukkut tiṅkaḷ eṉap peyariṭappaṭṭatum 28 naṭcattirak kūṭṭaṅkaḷ koḷḷappaṭuvatum tamiḻariṉ mātam tētik kaṇakku cantiramāṉa aḷaviyāka iruntateṉat terivikkiṟatu. paḻiya vaṭanāṭṭu ilakkiyaṅkaḷil nāṭkaḷi vāramākak koṇṭu kuṟippiṭum muṟi kāṇappaṭavilli. vāramuṟi yāṉa kaṇita muṟi tamiḻaruṭiyatu. tamiḻar mēṟku nōkkic ceṉṟa pōtu yūpriṭṭicu tikirīcu āṟṟōraṅkaḷil kuṭiyēṟiṉārkaḷ. ākavē vāra muṟiyāṉa kaṇita muṟiyi ivarkaḷ annāṭṭil parappi ṉārkaḷ.
kirakaṅkaḷum naṭcattirak kūṭṭaṅkaḷum maṉitaṉuṭiya palāpalaṉ kaḷil āṭci celuttukiṉṟaṉa eṉpatu mikap paḻaṅkālattil aṟiyap paṭṭiruntatu. cūriyaṉuṭiya celvākku iyaṟkip poruḷkaḷilum cantiraṉuṭiya celvākku kaṭalvaṟṟup perukkukaḷilum iruntu varuvati viññāṉikaḷ kūṟukiṉṟaṉar. ivvaṭippaṭiyil varalāṟ ṟukku muṉ cōtiṭak kali toṭaṅkiṟṟu. erikoḷḷi erintu viḻuvatu varavirukkum tīmiyik kāṭṭuvatākavum, cantira, cūriya kirakaṇaṅkaḷ keṭutalāṉavi eṉṟum karutappaṭṭaṉa. karuppamāṉa peṇ evaḷāvatu kirakaṇattip pārkkamāṭṭāḷ.
paḻantamiḻar paruva kālattik kār, kūtir, muṉpaṉi, piṉpaṉi, iḷa vēṉil, mutuvēṉil eṉa āṟu pirivukaḷākap pirittiruntārkaḷ. cūriyaṉ ciṅka rāciyil cellum kālam āvaṇiyāka iruntatu. muṟ kālattil āvaṇi āṇṭu toṭaṅkum mātamākavum, āṭi āṇṭiṉ iṟuti mātamākavum iruntaṉa. āvaṇi mātattil cūriyaṉi mukilkaḷ maṟippatāl mantāramuṇṭākat toṭaṅkukiṟatu. kuḷir kālam kaḻintu veyil kāyat toṭaṅkum kālamākiya tit toṭakkattil tamiḻar poṅkal viḻāvik koṇṭāṭiṉārkaḷ.
caṅka ilakkiyaṅkaḷil kaṇikaḷ eṉpōrāl kaliyāṇaṅkaḷukku nāḷ kuṟittal kuṟippiṭappaṭṭuḷḷatu. “mūvakik kālamum neṟiyilāṟṟu vatāvatu pakalumiravum iṭiviṭāmal ākāyattip pārttu āṇṭu nikaḻum villum, miṉṉum, ūrkkōḷum, tūmamum, miṉ vīḻvum, kōḷ niliyum, maḻi niliyum piṟavum pārttuk kūṟutal” eṉa ivarkaḷik kuṟittu iḷampūraṇar kūṟiyuḷḷār. kaṭṭilukku mēlē yuḷḷa mēṟkaṭṭiyil paṉṉiraṇṭu irācikaḷum eḻutappaṭṭiruntaṉa veṉṟu neṭunalvāṭi kūṟukiṟatu. kuṟiñci nila makkaḷ cantiraṉ parivaṭṭaṅkoḷḷum kālattil maṇam ceyvārkaḷ. paripāṭal, cilappatikāram, pattuppāṭṭu mutaliya nūlkaḷil āṅkāṅku vāṉa nūṟ kuṟippukaḷ kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa.
74. celvaṉ vāḻum māḷiki
1celvaṉ vāḻum māḷiki iraṇṭākap pirikkappaṭṭiruntatu. muṉ puṟattil āṭavarum piṉpaṟattil makaḷirum vāḻntaṉar. vīṭṭut talivaṉ taṉatu karumaṅkaḷik kavaṉittuk koṇṭu mīḷvōri upacarittāṉ. vīṭṭil ovvoru tēvikkum vēṇṭiya pala aṟika ḷiruntaṉa. vīṭṭi aṭuttu vicālamāṉa tōṭṭamiruntatu. tōṭṭat til pūñceṭikaḷum paḻamaraṅkaḷum uṇavukku vēṇṭiya kāy piñcukaḷ koṭukkum ceṭi koṭikaḷum uṇṭākkappaṭṭiruntaṉa. ataṉ mattiyil kiṇaṟiruntatu. tōṭṭam vīṭṭiṉ piṉ puṟattil iruntami yiṉ vīṭṭiṉ taliviyē ataṉik kavaṉittāḷ. pūntōṭṭattil naṟumaṇa malarkaḷip pūkkum malliki mulli mutaliya koṭikaḷ paṭarntiruntaṉa. avikaḷiṉiṭiyē amikkappaṭṭirunta mēṭi mītiruntu avaḷ ullācamākap poḻutu pōkkiṉāḷ. vīṭu mikac cuttamāka iruntatu. vīṭṭil teyvaṅkaḷ vittu vaḻipaṭappaṭṭaṉa. kaṇavaṉum maṉiviyum nilā muṟṟattil iruntu veṇ matiyiyum viṇmīṉkaḷiyum nōkki makiḻntārkaḷ. vīṭṭuc cuvarkaḷ āḷiṉuru vam piratipalikkumpaṭi miṉukkañ ceyyappaṭṭiruntaṉa. vīṭṭuk kūri kaḷi aḻakiya tūṇkaḷ tāṅki niṉṟaṉa. tōṭṭattil nīrāl cūḻap paṭṭa nīrāḻi maṇṭapam iruntatu. atu kōṭikālattil uṟivataṟku ēṟṟatu. peṇkaḷ taṅkum pakutiyiṉ nāṟpuṟaṅkaḷilum aṟikaḷ iruntaṉa. 
talivaṉ uṟiyum aṟiyil pañcu mettikaḷ iṭappaṭṭa iraṇṭu kaṭṭilkaḷ iruntaṉa. mettiyiṉ nāṟpakkaṅkaḷilum aṇikaḷ iṭappaṭṭiruntaṉa. talip pakkattukku aṇmiyil ularnta marattaṭṭu iruntatu. kāliyil alaṅkarittuk koḷvataṟku vēṇṭiya cantaṉam, vācaṉit tilam, pūmāli mutaliyaṉa ataṉmītu vikkappaṭṭiruntaṉa. tariyil eccil umiḻum kāḷāñci iruntatu. aṟikku veḷiyē vaḷarkkum kiḷikaḷ kūṭukaḷil iruntaṉa.
talivaṉ kāliyil eḻuntu kālik kaṭaṉkaḷi muṭittapiṉ taṉṉi alaṅkarittāṉ. alaṅkārap poruḷkaḷil ciṟantavi cantaṉam, vācaṉit tiraviyaṅkaḷ eṉpaṉa. avaṉ vācaṉip puki ūṭṭappaṭṭa āṭiyi uṭuttup pūmāliyi aṇintāṉ. kaṇṇukku mi tīṭṭiṉāṉ; tāmpūlamiṭṭuc civanta itaḻkaḷukku arakkuk kūṭṭic ceyta cāyam pūciṉāṉ. taliyi vāriṉāṉ. viralkaḷukku mōtiraṅ kaḷi aṇintāṉ. mēlē uttarikam tarittāṉ.
kāliyil pārkkum kaṭamikaḷ muṭintatum avaṉ tiṉamum nīrāṭiṉāṉ. ovvoru iraṇṭāvatu nāḷum avaṉ uṭampu piṭittuk koṇṭāṉ. ovvoru mūṉṟāvatu nāḷum oruvakip poruḷip pūci nīrāṭiṉāṉ. nakaṅkaḷ miṉukkamāka irukkumpaṭi avaṉ avaṟṟi aḻaku ceytu koṇṭāṉ. viyarviyit tuṭippataṟku avaṉ eppoḻutum oru ciṟiya tuṇiyi vittiruntāṉ. muṉ poḻutil oṉṟum piṉpoḻutil oṉṟumāka nāḷirumuṟi uṇavu koṇṭāṉ. iṟicci porittum, camittum, avitta nīrākavum koḷḷappaṭṭatu. naṇpakal uṇavukkup piṉ avaṉ naṇparkaḷōṭu aḷavaḷāviṉāṉ. māli nērattil kōḻip pōr, kutārip pōr, āṭṭup pōr kaḷik kaṇṭu poḻutu pōkkiṉāṉ. kūṭukaḷil vaḷarkkum ciṅkaṅ kaḷum pulikaḷum niṉṟaṉa. iraviṉ muṟpakutiyil avaṉ iciyik kēṭṭum naṭaṉaṅkaḷip pārttum makiḻntāṉ. aṟikaḷil naṟumaṇam kamaḻntatu.
celvaṉiṉ maṉivi urattuc cirikkavum urattup pēcavum māṭṭāḷ. kaṇavaṉiṉ peṟṟōr kuṟi kūṟiṉāl avaḷ etirttup pēca māṭṭāḷ; periya celvattilum ullāca vāḻkkiyilum tiḷittapōtum akanti koḷḷamāṭṭāḷ; viḻākkaḷukkuc cellumpōtu āṭamparamākac celvāḷ. cila aṇikalaṉkaḷi aṇintu koḷvāḷ. kaṇavaṉ tūratēcam ceṉṟiruntāl avaḷ caṅku vaḷikaḷiyum tāliyiyumtavirap piṟa aṇikalaṉkaḷi aṇiyamāṭ ṭāḷ. avaḷ kāli, naṇpakal, māli eṉṉum mūṉṟu nēraṅkaḷilum illuṟi teyvaṅkaḷukkup pali tūvuvāḷ.
75. kūttu
ātikāla makkaḷ tammiṭam tōṉṟum uṇarccikaḷi āṭik kāṭṭiṉārkaḷ. piṟpōkkiluḷḷa makkaḷiṭiyē iṉṟum ivvāṭ ṭaṅkaḷ kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. ivvaki āṭṭaṅkaḷiliruntu kūttuk kali vaḷarcciyaṭintatu. atu iṉṟu naṭipeṟum nāṭakam pōlal lātu, oru karuttiṉi, uṭalnili, pārvi, apinayaṅkaḷāl naṭittuk kāṭṭum kaliyāka iruntatu. atu piṟkālattil parata nāṭṭiyam eṉavum catirāṭṭam eṉavum peyar peṟṟatu. cintuveḷi nākarika kālattil itu naṉku vaḷarcciyaṭintiruntatu. cintuveḷiyil kiṭitta tolporuḷkaḷil naṭarācarip pōṉṟu naṭaṉamāṭum mūṉṟu kompukaḷuṭiya oru kaṭavuḷ uruvamum, naṭṭamāṭum niliyil niṟkum peṇ teyvattiṉ uruvamum, nāṭṭiyamāṭum niliyil niṟkum oru nāṭṭiyap peṇṇiṉ uruvamum kāṇappaṭṭaṉa1. nāṭṭiyak kaliyi puttarum, camaṇarum, pirāmaṇarum veṟuttārkaḷ. ikkali teṉṉintiyāvilēyē vaḷarcciyaṭintatu. paratanāṭṭiya nūlic ceyta paratar tirāviṭa vakuppiṉarāvar2. paratar ceyta nūl vaṭamoḻiyiliruppatāl kūttukkali āriyanāṭṭiṉiṉṟu teṟkē vantateṉap palar tavaṟākak karutuvar.

1. Vishnu, Shiva and Kali, the great gods of Hinduism, are not Rigvedic deities at all. It is probably significant that the word Lingam is definitely of non-Aryan origin, as Przyluski has demonstrated. while the word puja is also believed to be a non-Samskritic loan word. 1. The progress of research into various phases of Indian antiquities is helping to pile up evidences to demonstrate the fact that the texure of Indian culture is
made of the work of non-Aryan and pre-Aryan threads crossed with the woof of Aryan Hinduistic character. In the light of these evidences the conviction has been gining ground that the great process popularly known as Hinduism is nothing but a synthesis and harmonization of complex elements of Aryan, pre-Aryan, non-Aryan and aboriginal culture, a good deal of which must have been autocthonus and indigenous, that is to say, was born on, or sprung from the soil of Indian continent. It has become impossible to contradict the fact that aboriginal and Indian Aryan cultures have greatly contributed to the development of what has become to be known during historical times as characteristically Indian civilization. Sometimes the elements and types of aboriginal culture has been transformed and modified so as to fit into the ideals and systems of Aryan thought and culture. Sometimes the aboriginal elements have been bodily annexed and appropriated into Indian system by removing the property mark of earlier aboriginal ownership and origins - Non.Aryan contribution to Indian Music - O.C.Ganguly - Annals of Bhandarkar - Oriental Research Institute - Vol. XIX (1938-1939).

On the grounds indicated above, we may infer the, Upanishadic speculations originated wholly outside the pale of Vedic Brahmanism and had their source in the religio-philosophical thought currents already prevalent in India since pre-Aryan days. That a rich culture which had been flourishing in India for at least two millena before the advent of the Vedic Aryans, should produce philosophical thinking and religious ideas of refined types is no difficult to make, for, it is but normal to expect this evolution ... the pre-Vedic elements constituted the texure while the Vedic did probably no more than imprint the stamp. It would be historically more correct, therefore, to regard Upanishadic as much as Jaina and Buddhist thoughts as having their roots more in non-Vedic than in Vedic ideas. We also find the basic ideas of the Samkhya and Yoga permeate Jaina, Buddhist as well as the Upanishadic outlook and it is probable that the primitive Samkhya consisted the philosophical background par excellence of pre-Vedic Indian thought and Yoga consisted an essential element in the cultivation of matters concerning the spirit. Both Samkhya and Yoga had developed probably already in pre-Aryan India ... the origin of Upanishads was not at all Vedic. We must not forget the priestly classes and philosophical thinkers with their religious practices and ideas who existed in India from before the coming of the Indian Aryans. By Buddhas time they have probably been absorbed in the part of the Vedic society and came to called Brahmans - Back ground of Buddhist philosophy - Prof. Dr.B.B.Bhattacharia, M.A.D., Ph.D. Indo Asian Culture, No.1.

It is an established fact that the god Siva was the form which the Vedic god Rudra later assumed. In other words the god Siva, at least as he has been described in classical times, was unknown to the Vedas, and Rudra the Tempest God of the Vedas is not given any of the distinctive epithets which later came to be associated with the god Siva. If we accept the alleged identification we have to date the god Siva or his proto type in the middle of the third millenium B.C. For, that is the date of the Mohenjo-Daro finds, as has been proved by Professor Selon Lloyd on the strength of the happy discovery of the cylindrical seal at Tel-as-mar which contins a representation of a typically mohenjo-Daro scene-an Indian elephant, rhinoceros and a crocodile. Identification of Mohenjo-Daro figure-B.A. Saletore-New review X, July - Dec. 1939.
Now it seems possible that Rudra in the Rig-Veda was an Aryanised form from the pre-Aryan proto-Siva. Only three hymns have been given to him, and he is identified with Agni. The cult of linga in three faced Siva is common among represen-
tations of Siva. It is ordinarily Agamic principle that Siva in his aspect of Maheswara or Sadasiva can be represented with one, three, four or five faces but not with two. But the fact is there, the image represented with three faces and other associations are clearly Saivic in character. The conclusion there fore seems to be thoroughly justified that it is the figure of Siva that is represented on this. This would only be confirmed by the yogic posture of Siva in one aspect is represented as Mahayoge and sometimes called Yoge - Daks hanamurthi. 1. From the identification of Chandragupta Maurya to the excavations of Mohenjo Daro and Harappa, from the deciphering of the inscriptions of Asoka to the comparative survey of epigraphic records over India, the material for the writing of Indian history was provided by the work of European scholars. Even more striking is the case of Indonesia, where few European scholars, mostly Dutch reconstructed from inscriptions the history of the great empires of Java and Sumatra which provided Indonesian nationalism with a solid historical basis. In this sense it cannot be denied that European scholars and thinkers, by their labour in the interest of knowlge, enabled India, Ceylon and Indonesia to think on terms of historical continuity.
- Asia and Western Dominance
K.M. Panikkar (London - 1954)
* Of European tongues, the nearest congeners to Sanskrit are the Samaritin languages of the Russian Empire, then the classical tongues of Rome and Greece, then those of Germany and the Keltic, this class of languages being called Indo-Germanic, of the sclavonic and Lithuanian, the two branches of samaritin, the affinities of the sanskrit are closer in the Lithuanian than with any other known tongue. Sanskrit next to Lithuanian is most like Sclavonic. It will thus
be observed that the Aryan or Sanskrit speakig races of India seem to have been closely connected with the Zend speaking, Greek speaking, Latin speaking races and not at all with Arabic, Phoenician and Hebrew families.

* Rudra has a very subordinate position in Rig-Veda being celebrated only in three entire hymns. He holds a thunderbolt in his arms and discharges lightning shafts from the skys. Siva the benignant with a whole tradition developed round him. - Indian Philosophy Vol. I. p.81 Dr.S.Radhakrishnan.
Rudra is the lord of animals, and forms the point of linkage between the Vedic religion and the later Siva worship. Siva in the Rig-veda means auspicious , but is not the name of a God; the Rudra in Rig-veda is a malignant cattle destroying deity. * The early Vedic religion was a cult of magic, a system of propitation or constrint of Nature-powers (Devas) by means of sacrifices (Yajnas), offerings of animal fat, (ghee vapa, etc) and fermented liquor (Soma) poured into fire regarded as the mouth of the Gods, and accompanied with the chanting of mantras. Some of these mantras were incantations of prise, and others combinations of sounds having no meaning, being sometimes inarticulate cries (“like the bellowing of a bull etc.”) They were believed to please or constrin the Devas and thus to secure the fulfilment of the sacrificers desires, whether these were the acquisition of material objects in this life or the enjoyment of pleasures in post-mortem states. - Outlines of Indian Philosophy p.118.

* They were translated from Sanskrit into Persian by or for Dara Shukoh, the eldest son of the Mugal emperor Shah Jehan who held the liberal religious views of Akbar. He had heard of the Upanishads in Kashmir in 1640 invited several Pandits to Delhi to assist in their translation and finished the work in 1657. Translated into Persian then the most widely read language of the East, they became generally accessible. In 1775 a manuscript of this Persian translation was sent by the French resident at the court of Shujud Daula to Anquetil Duperron the discoverer of the Avesta; and later another manuscript. Anquetil Duperron collected the two and translated the work into French and into Latin publishing the latter version in 1801 and 1802 under the title of Oupnekhat a corruption of upanishad. This Latin translation was studied by Schopenhaner. Twelve of them are translated by Maxmuller with introduction and notes in the “Sacred books of the East”. - The century cyclopedia of names.

* Vedanta - The most Common designation of the Uttaramimamsa school of Hindu philosophy given to it either as teaching the ultimate aim of Veda or as founded on the Upanishads, came at the end of the Veda as the last stage in its historic evolution. It is ascribed to Vyasa or Badarayana. The first of the names (‘arranger’) is also given to the legendary person who is supposed to have arranged the Vedas and written the Mahabharata, Puranas and Dharmasastra and was doubtless applied to various great writers or compliers as a kind of title. In this sense it seems to have been given to the founder of the Vedanta. Its principles are propounded in Sutras, but Badarayana’s Sutras are generally called Brahmasutras or sometimes Sharirakasutra. The text of the celebrated commentary of Sankaracharya have been edited in the “Bibliotheca Indica” and a portion translated, and also the commentary known as Vedanta Sara. The most authoritative recent works on the Vedanta are however pul Deussen’s “Die Sutras des Vedanta” - The Century Cyclopedia of Names.

# Smartas: Smarta Brahmins - one of the three principal classes into which the Hindus proper of the present day may be divided as to religion, the other two being the Saivas and the Vaisnavas. The Smarta believe that the man’s spirit is identical with the one spirit which is the essence of the universe and only cognizable through the three personal gods Brahma, Shiva and Vishnu with their subordinate dieties but only as co-equal manifestations of one impersonal spirit and as destined to be reabsorbed into the spirit. They are followers of Sankara - The Century Cyclopedia of Names.

* Puranas - The name of each of a class of Sanskrit works important in their connection with the later phases of Brahmanism, as exhibited in the doctrines of emanation, incarnation and triple manifestation. They are the Vedas of popular Hinduism and contin the history of the Gods, interwoven with every variety of legendary tradition on other subjects. Though nominally tritheistic, they are practically polytheistic and essentially pantheistic. Their form is in general that of dialogues in which a well known sage answers the questions of his disciples, while others are monologues. They are written in sloka matter of the Mahabharata, with occassional passages in prose. They are 18 in number. There are also 18 Upapuranas or Subordinate Puranas
- The Century Cyclopedia of Names.

* The Dharma Sutras were manuals written by the teachers of the Vedic Schools for the guidance of their pupils. Their use was therefore, at first restricted to these schools alone and it was not till a later period that they were acknowledged as authority all over India. The Smirthis on the other hand were declared to be of divine origin and hence climed from the very beginning to be authentic sources of law for all Aryans - “The History and Culture of the Indian People - Vol.II p.225.”

* No.99 in vol.ii. part V. of South Indian inscriptions gives an interesting account of a gift of a village for the purpose of supporting 308 learned Brahmans in persuit of their sacred vocations of studying and teaching as prescribed in the Sastras. Regarding the qualifications of the select body of Brahman scholars it is stated in the inscription that they had all studied the three Vedas and Smiritis. The inscription applies to them various learned designations such as Cathurvedin, Triveden, Somajajin, Sadangavid, Bhatta, Kramavid (proficient in the Krama - patha of the Rig Veda & C.)
A similar gift for establishing a similar colony of 308 Brahmans is also Registered in No.7 of 1912 No.277 of 1913 refers to the establishment of another cultured colony of 108 Brahman families equipped with all necessaries of life and even with library called Saraswathi Bhandara. No.278 of 1913 registers a similar grant for the same number of Brahman colonists. No.198 of 1919 records the interesting case of an assembly holding a special meeting in response to a royal order which requested them to adjudge the merits of a literary work composed by a poet. The work was recited before the assembly and the author obtined as a reward for his labours a grant of land to be held in perpetual ownership. Students of Tamil literature may find here a lingering literary tradition of the more ancient Dravidian Sangam established in Madura to scrutinze
the works of Tamil poets and advance the cuse of Tamil literature (mid. Ep. Rep. for 1919. p.98) - Local Government in Ancient India p.283. Radhakumud Mookerji M.A. Ph.D.

* The Agamas represent the oldest products of Dravidian literature, that in prehistoric times they were written in the Dravidian (Tamil) language, and a great part of them was lost in a flood which swept over the land south of the present Cape Comorin, the chief dwelling place of the old Dravidians. Only remnants of the older Agamas were translated into Sanskrit and preserved in this form. But as has been urged, all that one can say is that the home of the Agamas was in the land of the Dravidians i.e. the south of India. From the south they seem to have pushed up north, and later to have turned back to the south where they helped to drive out Jainsm and Buddhism. It has been further sid that should one incline towards the theory that Agama literature was of Dravidian origin, one must at the same time admit that it came under the influence of Sanskrit literature very early. What is preserved to us of the Agamas bears unmistakably the stamp of Sanskrit literature, for the Agamas that are preserved are in the Sanskrit language, and the systems based in the Agama and written in the non-Sanskrit language employ Sanskrit terms so that as matters now stand, we have to consider the Agama literature as a part of the Sanskrit literature - The Saiva Siddhanta in the Meykanda Sastra - Violet Paranjothi M.A.L.T.Ph.D. (Isabella Thouburn College, Lucknow - 1938) quoted as an English translation from Der Saiva Siddhanta, a German book by H.W. * The Vedic culture which resembles that of the Homeric Greeks or the Celtic Irish at the beginning of the Christian era, or that of the pre-Christian Teutans and Slaves becomes transformed in the epics into the Hindu culture through the influence of Dravidians. The Aryan idea of worship during the earliest period was to call on the Father sky or some other shining one to look from on high on the sacrificer and receive from him the offerings of fat or flesh, cakes and drink. But soon puja or worship takes the place of Homa or sacrifice. Image worship which was a striking feature of the Dravidian faith was accepted by the Aryans. The ideals of vegetarianism and non-violence (ahimsa) also developed. The Vedic tradition has dominated by the Agamic and today Hindu culture shows the influences of the Agama as much as that of the Vedas. The Aryan and the Dravidian do not exist side by side in Hinduism. “contact with the highly civilized Dravidians led to the transformation of Vedism into theistic religion.” - Hindu view in life - Dr.S.Radhakrishnan.

1. Many other nations mention, in the mythological part of their history, in undations which in their essential particulars, agree with the scriptural account of Noah’s preservation. Hence many persons have inferred the universality of this inundation. To this it has been replied that each nation localizes the chief events and actors as connected with itself, necessitating an Ararat, an ark and a Noah in each instance. Fohi in the Chinese mythology, Satyavrata in the Indian, Xisuthrus in the Chaldean, Ogyges and Deucation in t he Greek, have each been recognised by many as the Noah of the sacred scripture under different names. Even the American Indians have a tradition of a similar deluge, and a renewal of the race from the family of one individual. All these individuals are sid be their respective nation to have been saved , and to have become the father of mankind.’ - A New Popular Encyclopedia Vol.IV p.325.

1. Ann (āṇ) is supposed to be the highest God, the God of Heaven. In fact he is, as we shall see later on, identified with the sun. Now the sun in the course of the year travels through the constellations of the Zodiac, which were called houses. Accordingly each month of the sun being in a different house was supposed to take a different form and since the constellations of the Poto - Indians as sid above were only eight, the forms of the sun i.e., the Supreme Being were eight. The eight forms of the Supreme Being were the eight constellations which were the following: The Ram, the Harp, the Crab, the Mother, the Scale, the Arrow, the Jar and the Fish or the two Fishes. Images of the supreme being under these forms were worshipped in different parts of the country. The most popular of these forms of God, seem to have been the Fish. Several inscriptions refer to this - Father Heras.

Ophiolatria, the worship of the serpent next to the adoration of the Phallus , is one of the most remarkable and at first sight unaccountable forms of religions the world has ever known. Until the true source from whence it sprung can be reached and understood, its nature will remin at mysterious as its universality, for what man could see in an object so repulsive and forbidding in its habits, as this reptile, to render worship to its one of the most difficult of problems to find a solution to. There is hardly a country of the ancient world, however where it cannot be traced pervading every known system of mythology, and having proofs of its existence and extant in the shape of monuments, temples and earthworks of the most elaborate and curious character. Babylon, Persia, Hindustan, Ceylon, China, Japan, Burmah, Java, Arabia, Syria, Asiya minor, Egypt, Ethiopia, Greece, Italy, North and Western Europe, Mexico,
Peru, America all yeild abundant testimony to the same effect and point to the common origin of Pagan system wherever found Ophiolatria - p.1.

1. Horned Gods were common in Mesopotamia, both in Babylon and Assyria. The great Gods and Goddesses had seven horns, which is the reason that the divine lamb in the book of revelation was sid to have seven horns ... The horns were a sign of divinity. When king or high priest appeared as the God Asshur with the queen or high priestess as his consort Ishtar, the appropriate number of horns was worn on the royal pir being then regarded as the incarnat e deities. When Alexander the Great rised himself above the king of the earth and made himself a God, he wore horns in sign of his divinity hence his name in the Koran Dhu’l Karnan, the two horned ... The Indian figures of the horned Gods found at Mohenjo - Daro, are of the earliest bronze - age. The most remarkable is that of a man with bull’s horns on his head sitting crosslegged, surrounded with animals the representative was regarded in historic times as a form of Siva and is called Pasupathi ... When in relief sculpture Pasupathi is three faced, as here; but in figures in the round he has four faces. Such a representation in a native attempt to show the all seeing God, as is found in Europe in the four faced of Janus. It is still uncertin whether the four faced form arose independently in India and Europe, or whether one is the prototype of the other if the later, the India appears to be the earlier - The God of the witches p. 15 - Margret Allice Murray.

“The beared God who grasping a trident in his extended left hands heads, the procession of male figures is probably the father deity. The great Hittite God
of thundering sky, whose emblems were the thunderbolt and the bull; for the trident which he carries may resonably be interpreted as thunderbolt. The deity is represented in two stone monuments of Hittite art which were found at Zenjirli in Northern Syria and Bobylonia repectively. On both we see a male God wearing the usual Hittite costume of tall cap, short tunic, and shoes turned up to the toes, a crescent hilted sword in girt at his side; his hands are rised in the right, he holds a single headed axe or hammar, in his left a trident of wavy lines, which is thought to stand for forked lightning or a bundle of thunderbolts. On the Babylonian slab which bears a long Hittite inscription the God’s cap is ornamented with a pir of horns. The horns on the cap are probably those of a bull; for in another Hittite monument found at Malatia on the Euphrates there is carried a deity on the usual Hittite costume standing on a bull grasping a trident or thunderbolt in his left hand, while facing him stands a priest clothed in long robe holding a crook or curved staff in one hand and pouring a libation with the other.” 
In the sculpture the God on the bull holds in his right hand what is discribed as a triangular bow instead of a mace or an axe or a hammer. The Hittite Thunder God also is known to us from a treaty of alliance which about the year 1290 B.C. was contracted between Huttusil, King of Hittites and Remeses II, King of Egypt. By a singular piece of good fortune we possess copies of this treaty both in Hittite and in Egyptian languages. The Hittite copy was found some years ago inscribed in cuniform characters in a clay tablet at Borgazkeni; the copies of the treaty of Egyptian language are engraved on the walls of the temples of Thebes. From the Egyptian copies which have been read and translated, we gather that the sun God was principal deity, of the Hittites and the Hittite scales which appended to the treaty exhibited the king embraced by the Thunder - God and the queen embraced the sun goddess Arenna. The Hittite divinity of thundering sky appears to have long survived at Doliche in Commagene, forin late Roman art he reappears under the title of Jupiter. Dolichenus wearing a phrygian cap, standing on a bull and weilding double axe in one hand and a thunder bolt in the other. In this form his worship was transported from the native Syrian home by soldiers and slaves, till it had
spread over a large part of the Roman Empire especially in the frontiers, while it flourished in the camps of the legions. The combination of the bull with the thunderbolt as emblems of the deity suggests that the animal may have been chosen to represent the sky God not merely of its virility but of its voice; for in the peal of thunder primitive man may well have heard the bellowing of a celestial bull.

The tall flat totted hat with perpendicular grooves which she wears, and lioness or panther in which
she stands, remind as the turetted crown and lion drawn car of Cybele, who was worshipped in the neighbouring land of Phrygia across the Halys so stagnates the great Syrian Goddess Hierapolis Bambyce, was portrayed sitting on lions and wearing a tower on her head. 1. The theory and practice of yoga are entirely foreign to the trend of early and later Vedic religious thoughts and inclinations. It has now been definitely shown by Mr. Chanda with the help of some Mohenjo - Daro sculptures that the idea can be traced to Indus people. It is but natural that the people should have attributed to their God all the characteristics of a yogie including austerities and self - mortification. It is common to believe that the creator himself must perform austerities in order to aualify himself for the capacity of creating manthought Gods, in his own light; process which could bring destruction on man must have been gone thoroughly by Gods to attin their exalted position. It must have been such a belief which led the Indus people to conceive of and depict their God as a meditator.
The intimate connection between Samkhya and yoga are too well known to require repetition. The philosophy of the yoga system may be regarded as practically the same as that of the Samkhya with conception of a personal God super imposed upon it. It therefore appears certin that Samkhya too, which orthodox Hindu opinion has regarded as non-Vedic in character, was, like yoga, a system of thought which had a pre-Vedic origin.
It has been suspected for a long time by scholars that some non-Aryan tracts are contined in the later-day. Siva worship the tract assumption that everything. The word Sambu - as a Vedic epithet, is well known to be derived from Sam; blessing, welfare, prosperity plus the radical bhu; ‘be, become and to mean’ being a blessing beneficient as a name in later times, of Siva. I feel that it is likely to have been chosen becuse it suggested in the minds of the speakers some Dravidian word akin to the Tamil Cem, ‘redness’ (of Tamil cempoo ‘copper’) the colour red being always associated with this deity. That is to say, the application of the epithet to Siva - seems to me to become more intelligible under the above assumption of the existence in northern India at an early period of a race or races related to the Dravidians of the South, Sambu as a name of Siva becomes in Tamil Campu which, if an early importation, would as I argue, have been originally pronounced with an initial sound like that of the English Church. I venture the suggestion that this word has reverted to Sanskrit from some Dravidic dialect in the form of Jambu, as a name of Siva bearing the connection of ‘reddishness’. Both Jambuka and Siva are used to denote a jackal, possibly becuse of the tawny colour of the animal and when it is considered that the area characterized pre-eminently by the worship of Siva must have been originally south of the zone into which Aryan civilization had advanced, it will not, I think, be felt to be impossible that it was to this unkown region that the expression Jambu-dvipa, ‘the Siva-country first had a reference - Sanskrit Element in the Vocabularies of the Dravidian Languages pp.61,62 - Remarks by M.Collins.
